docs.title: Autoware CARLA Scenario
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for autoware-carla-scenario, a CARLA scenario testing framework for Autoware autonomous driving software.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This package provides a framework for creating and running automated scenario tests in the CARLA simulator, designed for validating Autoware's autonomous driving capabilities.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Automated scenario execution in CARLA simulator (UE5: 0.10.0 and ue5-dev), through the statically typed typesafe_carla client
  • Configurable scenarios using Hydra compose + structured configs
  • Glob-pattern batch execution of multiple scenarios in a single CARLA session
  • Condition-based scenario evaluation: timing, collisions, traffic signals, speed / standstill, lane / area position, waypoint crossing, plus logical (And / Or / Not), latching (Sticky), and persistent combinators
  • Action system for side effects: turns, lane changes, traffic-light state, on-demand camera attachment
  • Entity management for ego (EgoVehicle) and NPC vehicles with spawn retry and ground projection
  • Coordinate transforms between Lanelet2, OpenDRIVE, and CARLA world
  • Lanelet-based constraint sweeping via a Hydra lanelet_constraint sweeper plugin (also resolvable without CARLA from the viewer)
  • Web UI (FastAPI + Uvicorn) for browsing results and triggering runs
  • A trajectory log of every run (actors, lights, map, plan, conditions, verdict; JSON Schema published), which a Rerun recording is made from to see the run (Seeing a run), beside CARLA's native recording
  • scenario-setup downloads CARLA's nightly build, which the runner then launches by itself
  • pytest integration via CarlaScenarioFixture (auto-skip when there is no CARLA to launch)

docs.title: Adversarial Actions and NADE
docs.text:
The framework ports TeraSim's adversarial behaviour generation (#385). There are three ways to use it:

  • An adversarial action: one named NPC or pedestrian does one adversarial thing when its trigger holds. For example, it brakes hard in front of a follower, or cuts in.
  • NADE: an environment action that picks, every tick, which agent near the ego carries out which adversity. It samples them more often than they happen naturally, and keeps the importance-sampling weight that makes the run's statistics unbiased.
  • Scheduled static adversities: a stalled vehicle, or the aftermath of a collision, from one time to another.

docs.title: The layers
docs.text: Layer Module What it does Observation adversity.observation Builds a Scene of the agents in the Lanelet2 map frame. It answers TeraSim's traci questions: the leader and follower within 40 m, the lanes beside, the next signal, a pedestrian's crosswalk and nearest road. Triggers adversity.triggers One pure function per kind. Each takes what the agent sees and returns an AdversarialCommand, or None. adversity_command applies the location gate first, then the kind's trigger. Location adversity.location AdversityLocation: ANY, INTERSECTION, HIGHWAY, ROUNDABOUT. These are read from the map by the ODD's own probes, so an adversity fires where coverage records that location. Commands adversity.command An acceleration, a lane change or a path, planned along the lanes into a timed path (plan_command, predict_command). Execution actions._adversarial_execution Drives the path: it takes the vehicle from its traffic backend, follows the path, then hands the vehicle back. NADE adversity.nade, adversity.avoidance Candidates, prediction, challenge, avoidability, importance sampling and the victims' response. Actions actions.adversarial, actions.adversarial_traffic, actions.stalled_object What a scenario registers.

docs.title: The kinds
docs.text:
The numbers are TeraSim's defaults; each can be overridden in TriggerThresholds. The accelerations come from the Intelligent Driver Model (adversity.idm), which stands in for SUMO's car-following model.

Kind Action TeraSim Fires when Does BRAKE_CHECK AdversarialBrakeAction Follower A follower is close behind, and neither is stopped. The agent is not speeding up, and the follower is not slowing. Brakes at the emergency deceleration (9 m/s²) for 2 s. IGNORE_LEADER IgnoreLeaderAction Leader Its leader holds it back by more than 1.5 m/s² (free flow against car following), and the speed difference is at least 2 m/s. Accelerates at the free-flow rate for 2 s. CUT_IN AdversarialCutInAction LaneChange A lane beside is blocked only by the vehicle behind there (closer than SUMO's secure gap). Changes into that lane in 1 s. LANE_CHANGE_ABORT LaneChangeAbortAction LanechangeAbort Blocked as for CUT_IN. The agent is moving, and its lanelet lasts at least 1 s more at its speed. Drifts half a lane toward that side and back in 1 s. HEAD_ON HeadOnAction Headon As for IGNORE_LEADER, but the agent's lanelet and its leader's start more than 120° apart. Uses IGNORE_LEADER's command. TRAFFIC_RULE RunTrafficRuleAction TrafficRule It is stopping for a red or yellow light rather than for its leader. Drives on through at the free-flow rate for 2 s. MERGE AdversarialMergeAction Merge It is beside a merging lane with traffic on it, and not already changing lanes (turned 5° or more off its lane). One lane over: speeds up as if the merging vehicle ahead were not there, when that beats giving way by more than 1.5 m/s², for 2 s. Two lanes over: changes into the lane between in 1 s, when nobody there is within 2 s of headway. JAYWALKING JaywalkAction Jaywalking A pedestrian is off any crosswalk, with a road within 10 m. Walks straight across at its speed (1.4 m/s if it stands) × U(0.5, 2.0), for up to 5 s. RUNNING_RED_LIGHT PedestrianRunRedLightAction RunningRedLight A pedestrian is waiting (at most 0.2 m/s) within 3 m of a crosswalk whose light is red. Crosses it end to end at 2.8 m/s. STOP_CROSSING StopCrossingAction StopCrossing A pedestrian is on a crosswalk. Stands still for N(2 s, 0.5 s), then walks a crosswalk's length on along its heading at 2.8 m/s.

The pedestrian kinds (PEDESTRIAN_KINDS) are only ever a pedestrian's, and the other kinds only a vehicle's.

docs.title: When an action fires
docs.text:
Each adversarial action takes the entity and a required location. Its default trigger is an AdversityFeasibleCondition of its kind at that location, which holds while the kind's trigger would fire. When the action fires, the command the condition found is planned on the map and driven (following_mode: FOLLOW by default, or POSITION, as TeraSim's moveToXY does). At the end of the path the vehicle is handed back to its traffic backend.

A condition given instead decides when the action fires. On that tick the adversity's own trigger is still asked; when it does not hold, nothing is done and a warning is logged. To require both, give the AndCondition of the two.

from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    AdversarialCutInAction,
    AdversityLocation,
    ElapsedTimeCondition,
)

# Cuts in on a highway whenever the gap allows it.
self.register_pre_tick(AdversarialCutInAction("npc1", AdversityLocation.HIGHWAY))
# Asked once, 3 s in: cuts in if it can then, else logs a warning.
self.register_pre_tick(
    AdversarialCutInAction(
        "npc2", AdversityLocation.ANY, ElapsedTimeCondition(3.0, label="later")
    )
)

docs.title: What is a merging lane
docs.text: TeraSim recognises a ramp by its SUMO edge name, which contains "Ramp". Lanelet2 has no such name, so MapFeatures.merges defines a merging lane as a lane that ends into the lane on its left. It either ends beside that lane, or shares what follows with it. This holds at the lanelet itself, or along its straightest successors within 100 m (MERGE_WINDOW_M).

docs.title: A crosswalk's light
docs.text: RUNNING_RED_LIGHT reads the Lanelet2 traffic-light regulatory element that the crosswalk lanelet carries. That is the pedestrian signal in an Autoware map. A crosswalk without one has no red light to run.

docs.title: NADE
docs.text:
AdversarialTrafficAction runs TeraSim's NADE loop on every tick of the run:

  1. Candidates: the max_controlled (5) vehicles nearest the ego within control_radius (50 m), and every pedestrian there.
  2. Adversity: each candidate's adversity is the first entry of adversities whose trigger fires. That gives {normal: 1 - p, adversarial: p}.
  3. Prediction: horizon (5 s) every resolution (0.5 s). The ego is predicted normal: it holds its acceleration along its lane, or changes lane when its turn indicator says so.
  4. Challenge: the candidate's adversarial future conflicts with the ego's normal future (TeraSim's AV-centred NADE). With challenge_npcs, it is also checked against the other candidates' futures.
  5. Avoidability: if no victim can brake out of the conflict (emergency brake, with a 0.5 m buffer), p is multiplied by 3e-4 and the magnitude by 40.
  6. Importance sampling: q = clip(p × magnitude (20), 0, max_is_probability (0.05)), or fixed_is_probability when that is set. At most one adversity is sampled per tick, the nearest challenger first, and none for cooldown (5.5 s) after one.
  7. Response: the sampled adversity's NPC victims avoid it with probability q = 0.2 (p = 0.99) by braking at the emergency deceleration for 3 s, or else accept it and hold their speed for 2 s. That response carries its own weight. An ego victim is never driven.
from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    AdversarialTrafficAction,
    AdversityKind,
    AdversityLocation,
    NadeAdversity,
)

self.register_pre_tick(
    AdversarialTrafficAction(
        [
            NadeAdversity(AdversityKind.CUT_IN, AdversityLocation.HIGHWAY, 0.002),
            NadeAdversity(AdversityKind.BRAKE_CHECK, AdversityLocation.ANY, 0.001),
        ],
        seed=7,
    )
)

It drives the NPCs and pedestrians a scenario registers, and with drive_background (the default) the traffic backend's background vehicles in the world too (#417): the TrafficManager's background traffic (background<N>), SUMO's ambient vehicles (sumo:<id>). One that carries out an adversity, or responds to one, is taken over for as long as its path lasts -- off autopilot, or published into SUMO from CARLA like a released entity -- and handed back to the backend after. SUMO's mesoscopic vehicles have no actor to take over, and SUMO's pedestrians are not driven.

docs.title: The weight
docs.text:
Each tick of a run multiplies the run's likelihood ratio by one factor:

  • p / q when an adversity is sampled;
  • (1 - p) / (1 - q) for each candidate whose adversity challenged a victim but was not drawn;
  • the response's own factor, when one is drawn.

A statistic weighted by this ratio is the naturalistic one. The action's weight is the ratio. BaseScenario.importance_sampling_weight is the product of every action's weight, which is 1.0 without NADE. You can read it:

  • as the built-in metric importance_sampling_weight (aggregation last; see Metrics);
  • in the trajectory log, where each sampled adversity is an adversity record with its p, its q, the weight at that point, the victims and the response (see Trajectory Log).
  • in the run's coverage file, as outcome.weight: a run is importance sampled when one of its actions is (BaseScenario.outcome_weight; NADE is), and only such a run records a weight.

To count which kinds were sampled, register a coverage item on AdversarialTrafficAction.sampled_kind (see Coverage). Merging a batch's coverage files (scenario-coverage) then estimates the naturalistic failure rate per scenario and environment: the mean of the weighted failures with its 95% interval, the relative half width it has converged to (TeraSim's NADE stops below 0.3), the self-normalised rate and the effective number of runs (openodd's weighted outcomes, see Coverage).

docs.title: Stalled objects and collisions
docs.text:
TeraSim's StalledObjectAdversity and CollisionAdversity are scheduled, not sampled. StalledObjectAction stands a vehicle still at a pose from start_time to end_time (scenario seconds; None means it is never removed). Outside that window the vehicle is out of the world.

A vehicle cannot be spawned once a run has started, so the scenario spawns it in setup, preferably out of the world (spawn.hidden). The action is a FollowTrajectoryAction of a held pose, with hidden_outside_trajectory. collision_objects creates two of them for a collision's aftermath.

from autoware_carla_scenario import Lanelet2Pose, StalledObjectAction, collision_objects

self.register_pre_tick(
    StalledObjectAction("stalled1", Lanelet2Pose(1043, 30.0), start_time=5.0)
)
for crashed in collision_objects(
    "npc3", "npc4", Lanelet2Pose(2001, 12.0), Lanelet2Pose(2001, 17.0, heading=0.4),
    start_time=0.0, end_time=60.0,
):
    self.register_pre_tick(crashed)

docs.title: Construction zones
docs.text:
ConstructionZoneAction lays out TeraSim's ConstructionAdversity along a lane (adversity.construction): from start_s to end_s metres along it, past its lanelet's end on along the straightest successors. These are the zones:

Zone Where Objects warning warning_zone_length (100 m) before the start signs on the shoulder, every warning_zone_spacing (30 m) taper_in taper_length_in (60 m) from the start cones, from 0.3 m inside the lane's edge to the work zone's offset buffer buffer_zone_length (10 m) cone, cone, barrier work to taper_length_out (30 m) before the end construction_type: cone, barrier, or mixed taper_out to the end cones, back to the edge termination termination_zone_length (30 m) after the end signs

spacing (20 m) is the distance between objects, scaled by 0.7 in a taper and 0.8 in the buffer. With use_dynamic_spacing and speed_limit_mph, MUTCD's spacings apply instead. A taper can be linear or curved (an s-curve). The zone closes in from side, "right" by default; TeraSim instead picked the side from the SUMO lane's index.

From start_time to end_time (None: never removed) the objects stand in the world as CARLA props, each added by a PropAction and named <label>/<zone>/<n> (docs/api.md). Unlike a vehicle, a prop may appear while a run is under way. When the zone appears, two things happen:

  • clear_traffic takes the backend's background vehicles in the zone off the road;
  • close_lane tells the backend the lane is closed. SUMO then disallows every vehicle class on it, as TeraSim's full_lane mode does. The TrafficManager cannot close a lane, and says so; a TrafficSinkAction on the zone keeps its traffic out.

TeraSim's full_lane mode places no object. Here the objects are always placed: a closure Autoware cannot see is one it drives into. At end_time the props are removed and the lane is reopened; when the run ends, the lane is reopened and the runner takes the props away with every other.

from autoware_carla_scenario import ConstructionSettings, ConstructionZoneAction

self.register_pre_tick(
    ConstructionZoneAction(
        1043, start_s=120.0, end_s=260.0,
        settings=ConstructionSettings(construction_type="mixed", side="right"),
        start_time=0.0,
    )
)

docs.title: Coordinate conventions
docs.text:
• Triggers and NADE: everything is in the Lanelet2 map frame: x East, y North, yaw in radians counter-clockwise from +x. Gaps run bumper to bumper along the lanes. A lane's s is measured along its centreline, and t is positive to the left.
  • Execution: planned paths are MapPose vertices in that frame. The trajectory follower places them in CARLA's left-handed world (y South, yaw in degrees clockwise) through the map's offset, as for any trajectory.
  • Signals: a light's state is keyed by its Lanelet2 traffic-light regulatory element's id, and read off CARLA by adversity.snapshot.

docs.title: Differences from TeraSim
docs.text: TeraSim (SUMO) Here (Lanelet2 and CARLA) SUMO's car-following model The Intelligent Driver Model, with TeraSim's gains as defaults getLeader, getLaneChangeStatePretty Scene: lane chains of the routing graph, with SUMO's secure gap for "blocked" convert2D along an edge The lanelet's centreline and its normal A ramp by its edge name "Ramp" MapFeatures.merges (above) A walking area controlled by a TLS link The crosswalk lanelet's own traffic light A person's SUMO maxSpeed pedestrian_max_speed, 2.8 m/s (the fastest jaywalker) StopCrossing counts steps at dt = 0.1 The wait is in seconds is_lane_changing: heading 5° or more off the SUMO lane's angle The same, off the Lanelet2 lanelet's direction (LanePosition.heading) Background vehicles are adversarial So are they, with drive_background (default): the backend's background vehicles in the world (#417) Construction zones: SUMO vtypes for cones, barriers and signs; full_lane only closes the lane CARLA props (static.prop.*), always placed, plus the lane closed to the backend (#402)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This page lists the public surface of autoware_carla_scenario. All symbols exported via the top-level package (autoware_carla_scenario) are stable; symbols only reachable through deeper subpackages should be considered internal unless explicitly noted.

docs.title: Top-level package
docs.text:
from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    BaseScenario, EgoConfig, ScenarioQueue, ScenarioRunner,
    CarlaServerManager, CarlaScenarioFixture,
    # Conditions, actions, kinematics, coordinate poses ...
)

The full list of re-exports is defined in autoware_carla_scenario.__all__ and includes the conditions, actions, kinematics, coordinate, entity, and sensor types described below.

docs.title: Scenario orchestration
docs.text:
Symbol Module Purpose BaseScenario scenario_base Abstract base for user scenarios. Subclasses implement setup() and is_done(). EgoConfig scenario_base VehicleEntityConfig subclass that fixes role_name to EGO_ROLE_NAME and carries both ends of the run: the spawn and the ego's goal_pose. None means "not named yet" — a scenario may derive the goal in setup(), and one that ends setup with none is refused. ScenarioRunner scenario_runner Executes a single BaseScenario against a CARLA world (sync mode tick loop, recording, cleanup). ScenarioQueue scenario_queue Context manager that owns a CarlaServerManager and runs registered scenarios sequentially with cooldown / retry. CarlaServerManager server Starts, reuses, and stops the CARLA UE5 process. Reads CARLA_EXECUTABLE, else launches the CARLA scenario-setup installed. CarlaScenarioFixture pytest_fixtures Helper that registers a scenario into a queue at import time and exposes a session-scoped pytest fixture for its ScenarioResult. EGO_ROLE_NAME constants Reserved CARLA role_name used for the ego actor. EntityRole entity_role Validated role_name wrapper for CARLA actors. Factories: EntityRole.ego(), EntityRole.npc(n).

CameraRecorder (the video renderer) was removed in 15.0.0 with the video itself: a run's trajectory log is what a run is seen from (Seeing a run).

docs.title: Coverage (autoware_carla_scenario.coverage)
docs.text:
See Coverage.

Symbol Purpose BaseScenario.register_cover(name, expression, *, unit, range, every, buckets, values, ignore, event, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) Declare a cover item, after cover() in OpenSCENARIO DSL. BaseScenario.register_cross(name, items, *, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) Cross coverage of cover items sampled on the same event. SamplingEvent When an item is sampled: START, END (default) or TICK. Re-exported from the top-level package. CoverItem, CrossItem The item definitions register_cover() / register_cross() build. autoware_carla_scenario.metrics: BUILT_IN_METRICS, Metric, read_metric(key, world), COLLISION_ANY, COLLISION_AT_FAULT, OFFROAD, WRONG_LANE, MIN_DISTANCE_TO_OBSTACLE_M, ... How the ego drives, read off the world per frame: AlpaSim's metrics. An outcome, which no ODD maps onto. See Metrics. BaseScenario.register_measure(key, read, *, unit, text), .measure(key, world), .measures A scenario's measures: what it sets up, under fixed keys (autoware_carla_scenario.measures: VEHICLE_AHEAD_GAP_M, VEHICLE_AHEAD_RELATIVE_SPEED_KPH, CROSSING_PEDESTRIAN_GAP_M, CROSSING_PEDESTRIAN_SPEED_MS). Replace a built-in one or add one of its own. See Scenario measures. CoverageCollector Samples items on their events during a run; written as {Scenario}_coverage.json. merge_coverage(documents), CoverageReport Merge coverage files and grade them. coverage.cod.export_cod(document, out_dir, stem) Write a run's ODD samples as an ASAM OpenODD COD table, manifest and taxonomy (scenario-coverage --export-cod).

docs.title: ODD (autoware_carla_scenario.odd)
docs.text:
See ODD.

Symbol Purpose OddAttribute(name, probe, *, unit, range, every, buckets, values, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) A measured taxonomy concept. Conditions: is_in, equals, between, at_least, at_most, greater_than, less_than, is_unknown. OddModule(name, *, include_and, include_or, exclude_and, exclude_or, labels, active, text, situation, target, cover_by, min_stay) A named rule; with situation=True, also covered as a situation. OddDefinition.situations() lists those. OddDefinition(name, attributes, modules, *, roots, text) The ODD: judges values with OpenODD's semantics (roots, labels, inactive modules, missing values), and marks buckets outside it. all_of, any_of, module_holds Group conditions; refer to another module or label. default_odd() The built-in ODD: openodd's bundled default (every attribute, no modules), measured in CARLA. register_odd(name, builder), resolve_odd(spec) Name an ODD; turn a name, .yaml path or module:function into one. Packages register through the autoware_carla_scenario.odds entry point group (a function calling register_odd). load_odd_file(path), load_odd_binding(path), load_openodd(*sources, bindings, name, text, situations) Read ASAM OpenODD 1.0 YAML (IMPORT, TAXONOMY, MODULES, ODD), with a binding file naming the probes. GitSource(url, rev, path), GitSourceError An OpenODD file in a git repository at a revision, for load_openodd() or a binding file's openodd list. ego_speed_kph, speed_limit_kph, lanelet_location, lanelet_subtype, lanelet_speed_limit_kph, in_junction, lane_count, illumination, rain, fog, traffic_density, pedestrian_nearby Built-in probes. lanelet_in_junction(lanelet), lanelet_road_type(lanelet), lanelet_speed_limit(lanelet) What the Lanelet2 probes read off one lanelet: its junction, road type (subtype) and speed limit (km/h). scenario_measure(key), ScenarioMeasure The probe mapping an attribute onto the running scenario's measure key (measure: in a binding file). See Scenario measures. typecheck.typecheck_odd(builder) Compile a Python ODD with Codon. plan_route_coverage(odd, scenario_or_route, *, lanelet_map, routing_graph, name) Check a planned route against the ODD on the Lanelet2 map: the verdict per lanelet (inside, outside, undecided) and the expected metres per bucket. Takes a scenario, a PlannedRoute(start, goal, via, name) or lanelet ids. Raises RouteError when the route cannot be planned. See Checking a planned route. combine_route_coverage(odd, routes) The expected coverage of several routes, and the buckets no route reaches. plan_route(route, lanelet_map, routing_graph) The lanelets of a PlannedRoute, with the metres driven on each. UNDECIDED What a probe's on_lanelet returns for a value only the run can tell. OddSampler(odd, knobs, *, controls, seed, strategy, coverage, max_tries) Draws concrete cases inside the ODD: .sample(count) gives OddSample(index, overrides, buckets, values, situation). strategy="coverage" draws the least covered buckets and the uncovered situations first. See Sampling scenarios from the ODD. OddKnob(key, *, values, scale, offset, integer, range), knobs_from_mapping(raw), DEFAULT_KNOBS A control: the config key that sets a measure (or, as a sweep knob, an attribute), and what it can stage. Scenarios declare theirs under controls in their config, by measure key.

docs.title: Conditions (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions)
docs.text:
All conditions inherit from BaseCondition and return a ScenarioResult from check(world, elapsed) once triggered (or None when not yet triggered). At the end of a run the runner calls close() on every pass and fail condition and every action's trigger: a condition that holds something in the simulator -- CollisionCondition's listening sensor -- stops and destroys it there, through its own handle. close() does nothing by default, and composite conditions close their children.

Symbol Description BaseCondition Abstract base class. Subclasses override _check(). ScenarioResult Pass / fail outcome with message, elapsed time, and per-condition statuses. ConditionStatus Per-condition leaf record used for reporting. AlwaysTrueCondition Default trigger for actions. AndCondition, OrCondition, NotCondition Logical combinators. NotCondition(child, holds_when_pending=True) is the logical NOT -- it holds while the child has not fired -- where the default flips a fired child's verdict; with OrCondition over EntityLanePositionConditions it says "on none of these lanelets" (cut-in). StickyCondition, PersistentCondition Latch / persist a child condition's truth value. TimeoutCondition, ElapsedTimeCondition Time-based triggers. MetricCondition(metric, rule, value, tolerance, *, label) A built-in metric -- how the ego drives -- against a threshold; usually a fail condition. See Metrics. EntityDistanceCondition, TimeToCollisionCondition Relative conditions between two entities: separation, and time to collision along the line joining them. CollisionCondition, EntityExistenceCondition Safety checks. OffRoadFractionCondition(fraction, entity_name=None, *, label) Fails once at least fraction (in (0, 1]) of the sample points of a 5 x 3 grid over an entity's (default: the ego's) bounding box -- edges and corners included, not an area -- are on no driving lane. The pass/fail counterpart of the offroad metric, with a tolerance. See Metrics. TrafficSignalCondition Traffic-light state check. RouteProgressCondition An entity's (default: the ego's) distance along the scenario's route, from an anchor (junction:0:entry, ...), compared with a rule; robust to lane changes. See Logical Scenarios from Routes. ComparisonRule, ScalarComparisonRule, compare Numeric comparison primitives. compare(actual, rule, value, tolerance) is the underlying helper. find_actor_by_role_name, find_actor_in_list Helpers for locating CARLA actors by role. find_actor_in_list is reachable via autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.

docs.title: Composition conditions (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.composition)
docs.text:
These build on CompositionCondition, which composes a child condition tree internally:

  • EntityLanePositionCondition
  • SpeedCondition, SpeedDirection, SpeedCoordinateSystem
  • StandstillCondition
  • TurnIndicatorCondition, TurnIndicatorState -- the turn indicators a vehicle shows (OFF / LEFT / RIGHT / HAZARD), read off its CARLA light state
  • TemporaryStopCondition
  • WaypointCondition, WaypointCheckType

docs.title: Actions (autoware_carla_scenario.actions)
docs.text: Symbol Description BaseAction Abstract base. Owns a trigger BaseCondition, a TickTiming, and an execute(world) side effect. TickTiming Enum: PRE_TICK / POST_TICK. TurnAction, TurnDirection Steer the ego through left / right turns via the CARLA TrafficManager route hints. TurnIndicatorAction Light a vehicle's turn indicators (TurnIndicatorState: OFF / LEFT / RIGHT / HAZARD), its other lights as they are; they stay so until set again. LaneChangeAction, LaneChangeDirection Trigger a TrafficManager lane change. TrafficSignalAction, TrafficLightTarget Set traffic-light states (e.g. all RED, all GREEN, or a specific actor). FollowTrajectoryAction Move a vehicle or pedestrian along a Trajectory (OpenSCENARIO FollowTrajectoryAction); speed paces the segments no time does; held_vertex names the vertex a waypoint condition is holding it at; appear_on_start=True brings a hidden entity in on its first vertex, moving at speed, when a run starts. See Trajectories and Recorded-Scene Replay.

docs.title: Adversarial actions (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.adversarial)
docs.text:
TeraSim's adversities, on a named NPC (exported from the top-level package, not from actions, which would pull in the Lanelet2 map layer). Each takes the entity and a required location (AdversityLocation: ANY, INTERSECTION, HIGHWAY, ROUNDABOUT); its default trigger is an AdversityFeasibleCondition of its kind there. When it fires, the command is planned on the map and driven (following_mode: FOLLOW by default, or POSITION), and the vehicle is handed back to its traffic backend at the end. A condition given instead fires the action, and the adversity's trigger is asked on that tick: when it does not hold, nothing is done. thresholds overrides TeraSim's numbers.

Symbol Description AdversarialBrakeAction Brake hard in front of a follower that keeps coming (BRAKE_CHECK). IgnoreLeaderAction Drive on as if the close, slower leader were not there (IGNORE_LEADER). AdversarialCutInAction Change lane in front of a vehicle too close behind in the next lane (CUT_IN). AdversarialMergeAction Beside a merging lane with traffic on it (MapFeatures.merges: a lane that ends into the lane on its left, there or within 100 m), cut a merging vehicle off: one lane over, speed up as if it were not there, when that beats giving way by more than 1.5 m/s², for 2 s; two lanes over, change into the lane between in 1 s when nobody there is within 2 s of headway (MERGE). LaneChangeAbortAction Start into the next lane in front of a vehicle too close behind there, drifting half a lane toward it, and swerve back, within 1 s (LANE_CHANGE_ABORT). HeadOnAction Drive on at a leader coming the other way: IgnoreLeaderAction's command, where the lanelets the vehicle and its leader are on start more than 120 degrees apart (HEAD_ON). RunTrafficRuleAction Run the red or yellow light the vehicle is stopping for (TRAFFIC_RULE). JaywalkAction Walk a pedestrian straight across the nearest road, off any crosswalk (JAYWALKING); seed seeds its speed. PedestrianRunRedLightAction Walk a pedestrian waiting at a crosswalk (at most 0.2 m/s, within 3 m) across it, end to end, when the crosswalk's Lanelet2 traffic light is red (RUNNING_RED_LIGHT). StopCrossingAction Stand a pedestrian on a crosswalk still for N(2 s, 0.5 s), then walk it a crosswalk's length on along its heading (STOP_CROSSING); seed seeds the wait. PropAction, PropOperation An operation on the environment (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.prop): PropOperation.ADD places a CARLA prop (static.prop.*; blueprint, a construction cone by default) named name at a position in any frame a trajectory vertex takes (CarlaWorldPose, Lanelet2Pose, OpenDrivePose, MapPose, RelativeLanePose against an entity, or a Route*Pose), on the road surface unless on_ground=False; a name already standing is replaced. PropOperation.REMOVE takes the prop of a name away. Props are kept by name, not as entities; the runner takes them all away (clear_props) when a run ends and before the next starts. apply(world, library, ground) does it at once, for an action built on it that places many props in one tick. StalledObjectAction, collision_objects TeraSim's scheduled static adversities (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.stalled_object): a vehicle the scenario spawned (out of the world, spawn.hidden, best) stands still at a pose -- a Lanelet2Pose, or an xy+yaw MapPose / CarlaWorldPose -- from start_time to end_time (scenario seconds; None: never removed), and is out of the world before and after. A FollowTrajectoryAction of a held pose with hidden_outside_trajectory. collision_objects is two of them, for a collision's aftermath. ConstructionZoneAction, ConstructionSettings TeraSim's construction zone (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.construction_zone): warning signs, an entry taper of cones, a buffer, the work zone, an exit taper and termination signs along a lane from start_s to end_s, as CARLA props from start_time to end_time; background traffic in it is taken off the road and the lane closed to the backend (SUMO). See Adversarial Actions and NADE. AdversarialTrafficAction, NadeAdversity, NadeSettings TeraSim's NADE as an environment action that runs for the whole run. Each tick, the NPC or pedestrian near the ego whose adversity (the first of adversities whose trigger fires) would challenge the ego carries it out, with the importance-sampling probability q = clip(p x magnitude, 0, max_is_probability), or a fixed one. One adversity at a time, then a cooldown. An adversity no victim can brake out of is unavoidable: its p is cut by 3e-4 and its magnitude multiplied by 40 (adversity.avoidance). With challenge_npcs, an NPC victim avoids it (emergency brake) or accepts it, with its own IS weight. weight keeps the run's likelihood ratio. It drives the registered entities and, with drive_background (default), the traffic backend's background vehicles (TrafficBackend.background_actors: TrafficManager background traffic, SUMO's ambient vehicles), each taken over while it carries out an adversity or responds to one and handed back after (#417). AdversityFeasibleCondition, AdversityKind, AdversityLocation Holds when the entity may carry out a kind adversity at location (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.adversity_feasible).

docs.title: Trajectories (autoware_carla_scenario.trajectory)
docs.text:
See Trajectories and Recorded-Scene Replay.

Symbol Description Trajectory, TrajectoryVertex A named polyline and its vertices: a position and the condition the entity departs it on (advance) -- a time, TrajectoryTimeCondition(t) (read back as vertex.time), or any other condition (waypoint conditions; Trajectory.is_gated, Trajectory.gated({index: condition})). TrajectoryTimeCondition A vertex's time: depart when the trajectory's clock reaches it. MapPose An absolute pose in Autoware's map frame, as a recording states it. RelativeLanePose A pose relative to an entity in lane coordinates (ds, offset, d_lane, yaw, entity_ref; OpenSCENARIO RelativeLanePosition), placed when the action starts. RouteLanePose, RouteOppositePose, RouteCrossingPose, RouteCrosswalkPose, RouteRoadsidePose Poses placed against the scenario's route (a logical scenario) when the action starts: along the route and across lanes, on the opposite road, on a lanelet entering a route junction from the left / right / opposite, on a junction's crosswalk, at the roadside. TrajectoryTiming, ReferenceContext How vertex times map onto the scenario clock (τ * scale + offset, from the scenario or the action start). TrajectoryFollowingMode POSITION (kinematic replay) or FOLLOW (a controller tracks it).

Recorded scenes (T4) are transcribed into documents outside the framework, by the separate scene_to_scenario_transpiler package (scenario-import-t4).

docs.title: Sensors (autoware_carla_scenario.sensor)
docs.text: Symbol Description CameraSensorBase, CameraSensorConfig Provider-agnostic camera sensor interface. CarlaCameraSensor, CarlaCameraSensorConfig CARLA RGB camera implementation, used by the driver rig.

docs.title: External driver (autoware_carla_scenario.driver)
docs.text:
Connects the ego to a driving policy served over alpasim's egodriver.EgodriverService. See External Driver Interface.

Symbol Description BaseEgoDriverClient Transport-agnostic client interface: session lifecycle, observation submission, drive. EgoDriverGrpcClient gRPC implementation against the vendored alpasim protos. DriverClientConfig, DriverCameraConfig Connection settings, policy cadence, and the camera rig streamed to the policy. ControlConfig, TrajectoryFollower, VehicleCommand Pure pursuit plus a port of Autoware's autoware_pid_longitudinal_controller (or the time_indexed tracker), turning a plan into carla.VehicleControl. Pose, Trajectory Rigid-transform primitives with protobuf conversions (right-handed frame). EgoObservation, DriveOutcome The state sent to the policy and the plan it returns. RendererDataBuilder Collects CARLA ground truth (governing traffic light, other vehicles, speed limit) into the renderer_data extension payload.

docs.title: Traffic backends (autoware_carla_scenario.traffic)
docs.text:
Owns the vehicles a scenario did not author, and answers the manoeuvre intents asked of the ones it did. See Traffic Backends.

Symbol Description TrafficBackend The interface: prepare / adopt / start / tick / close, plus the manoeuvre intents. TrafficContext The run a backend joins: client, world, map name, OpenDRIVE, step, seed, output directory. TrafficManagerBackend CARLA's TrafficManager — the default backend. NullTrafficBackend No traffic model at all (traffic=none). TrafficConfig, TrafficManagerBackendConfig Which backend drives a run, and the TrafficManager's own options. register_backend, build_backend, available_backends The registry a third-party backend joins through the autoware_carla_scenario.traffic_backends entry point. TrafficBackendError, TrafficBackendUnavailable A backend that cannot do what the run needs; the second names a simulator that is not installed.

docs.title: Coordinate transforms (autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate)
docs.text: Symbol Description Lanelet2Pose, OpenDrivePose, CarlaWorldPose, AnyPose Frame-tagged pose dataclasses. CoordinateFrame, FrameMismatchError, frame_of Coordinate-frame tagging and validation. MapManager Singleton owning the loaded LaneletMap, pyxodr road network, MGRS offset, and z offset. to_carla_world, to_carla_location, to_lanelet2, to_opendrive Pose conversion entry points (overload by input frame). project_onto_road Project a CarlaWorldPose onto a specified OpenDRIVE road. snap_to_carla_road Ray-cast a pose onto the rendered CARLA ground surface. GroundProjectionConfig Ray-cast tuning for snap_to_carla_road. lanelets_ahead A lanelet and the lanelets that follow it in the routing graph (no lane changes, every branch), up to a distance: the lanes a vehicle keeps to without changing lanes. get_stop_line_poses, get_stop_line_poses_with_following Resolve stop-line Lanelet2Poses for a lanelet (optionally including following lanelets).

docs.title: Entities (autoware_carla_scenario.entity)
docs.text: Symbol Description VehicleEntity, VehicleEntityConfig Generic vehicle actor with retry-aware spawn. EgoVehicle Subclass with the fixed EGO_ROLE_NAME, plus the on_scenario_start / on_tick / on_scenario_end lifecycle hooks ScenarioRunner calls. ExternallyDrivenEgo Base of every ego driven by a stack of its own rather than the TrafficManager: opts out of autopilot, refuses TrafficManager manoeuvres, and carries the termination request. BridgeHandshake The mission and readiness handshake with a stack over the AutowareBridge, optionally launching it per scenario; held by an ego (entity.bridged_ego). BridgedEgoEntity The ego that is nothing but a BridgeHandshake: the stack drives. AutowareEgoEntity The BridgedEgoEntity driven by Autoware through autoware_carla_interface. See Autoware. CarlaDriverEntity Drives the ego from an external policy's plan over the egodriver gRPC contract; given a bridge, starts the policy once a stack serving its world is ready. See External Driver Interface. SpawnLocation (Protocol) Tag interface implemented by spawn-point providers. SpawnTransform Spawn at an explicit carla.Transform. SpawnPointIndex Spawn at the N-th map spawn point.

docs.title: Kinematics (autoware_carla_scenario.kinematics)
docs.text:
Frame-aware velocity / acceleration types with affine-space arithmetic (absolute - absolute = relative; absolute + relative = absolute).

Symbol Description Vector3 Frame-tagged 3-vector. CoordinateFrame, FrameMismatchError, frame_of Re-exported from coordinate.frames. AbsoluteVelocity, RelativeVelocity, FrenetVelocity Velocity types. AbsoluteAcceleration, RelativeAcceleration, FrenetAcceleration Acceleration types.

docs.title: Lanelet constraint sweeper (autoware_carla_scenario.sweeper)
docs.text:
Powers the Hydra lanelet_constraint sweeper plugin. Can also be used directly from Python:

Symbol Description LaneletConstraintSweeper The Hydra Sweeper implementation (also re-exposed via hydra_plugins.autoware_scenario_sweeper). Constraint (ABC) Base class of the constraints above, with an abstract evaluate(lanelet). A constraint of your own may derive from it or only define evaluate(): the matching takes either. EqualsConstraint, InSetConstraint, OnRouteConstraint, LaneletLengthConstraint, HasStopLineConstraint, HasTrafficLightStopLineConstraint, HasAdjacentConstraint, IsJunctionConstraint, PreviousOfConstraint, FollowingOfConstraint Atomic constraints. AndConstraint, OrConstraint, NotConstraint Combinators. parse_constraint, find_matching_lanelets YAML-to-Constraint parsing and lanelet matching. The corresponding YAML type: keys for the atomics above are equals, in_set, on_route, lanelet_length, has_stop_line, has_traffic_light_stop_line, has_adjacent, is_junction, previous_of, following_of. Binding (Protocol), StopLineOffsetBinding, parse_binding Per-match parameter derivation (e.g. compute ego.spawn_s from a stop-line offset). load_lanelet2_map Lightweight Lanelet2 loader used outside of CARLA.

A scenario whose sweep holds a route search instead of constraints is expanded over the routes of the map that match it (expand_route, one case per match); see Logical Scenarios from Routes.

docs.title: Logical scenarios (autoware_carla_scenario.route)
docs.text:
See Logical Scenarios from Routes.

Symbol Description parse_route_search -> RouteSearchSpec Read a route search (LaneSegmentSpec / JunctionSegmentSpec segments, Range bounds, ego placement, max_matches, seed). No map needed. RouteMatch, RouteSegmentMatch A concrete route: lanelet ids, start / end s, each segment's route-s span and lanelets; anchor_s(anchor), to_config() / from_config() (the scenario.route.* keys). parse_anchor start, end, segment:K:start|end, junction:K:entry|exit. route.search.find_route_matches Every route of a Lanelet2 map matching a search, sorted (or shuffled by seed). route.frame.RouteFrame, ego_placement A match on its map: locate(s), point(s), project(x, y); where the ego spawns and its goal is. route.positions.resolve_route_pose Place a route pose against a frame and the ego's route s. set_scenario_route, scenario_route, scenario_route_frame, clear_scenario_route The route the running scenario is about. route.geometry.MapFeatures The per-lanelet questions a search asks (lanes beside, opposite lane, junction members and approaches, crosswalks), cached.

The plugin is registered with Hydra under hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint; see src/hydra_plugins/autoware_scenario_sweeper/.

docs.title: Result viewer (autoware_carla_scenario.ui)
docs.text:
Used internally by the viewer CLI. The web app is the supported surface, but the helper modules are importable for tooling:

Symbol Description ui.app FastAPI application object and route handlers. ui.scanner Discover sessions / scenarios under outputs/ and multirun/, build condition trees. ui.runner Background subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "scenario", ...]) orchestration with thread-safe progress. ui.sweep_resolver.resolve_sweep Resolve a sweep without launching CARLA. ui.cases Which files are a session's cases: the stem each case's files share (a SLURM batch's manifest, or matched against batch_results.json). ui.results A session's cases with their case, coverage and metrics (load_results, case_metrics), the cases in an ODD cell, and sessions compared case by case and cell by cell (compare). ui.slurm_launch Submitting a batch with launcher=slurm from the viewer (build_command, start_submit), a SLURM batch's progress (batch_status), and scenario-slurm run on it. ui.recordings A case's Rerun recording, made on demand with autoware_carla_scenario_rerun when installed, and where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from. ui.models Pydantic models (SessionSummary, SessionItem, ConditionNode, ScenarioResultView, RunProgress).

docs.title: Scenario authoring (autoware_carla_scenario.authoring)
docs.text:
The declarative authoring layer behind the Scenario Editor. None of it imports CARLA or lanelet2, so a document can be loaded, validated, compiled and exported anywhere.

Symbol Description ScenarioDocument The Scenario IR: entities, actions, assertions, an optional route search (a logical scenario), and a ui block that is presentation only. RouteSearch, LaneSegment, JunctionSegment, LengthRange, CountRange The route search as the IR states it; RouteSearch.to_sweep_dict() is what the route search reads. Entity, SpawnSpec, SValue, BindingRef, GoalSpec, EgoDriver Actors, how they spawn (fixed lanelet, or a constraint search with an optionally derived offset), and — for the ego alone — which stack drives it and where it is sent. LaneletChoice, LaneletSlot, ScenarioDocument.lanelet_slots Fixed or searched, and one view over every place a document names a lanelet — a spawn, a goal, an action's or a condition's lanelet parameter — so the picker, the validator and the Hydra config read one answer. ActionNode, ConditionNode, ConstraintNode Recursive IR nodes; a node's meaning comes from its registry spec, not from a type switch. ActionSpec, ConditionSpec, ConstraintSpec, BindingSpec, FieldSpec, ConditionVisual Metadata describing how a primitive is presented, edited and built. register_action_spec, register_condition_spec, register_constraint_spec, register_binding_spec Add a primitive; the GUI, validation and the compiler pick it up with no template change. validate_document -> ValidationReport Metadata-driven validation; errors block export, warnings do not. compile_document -> CompiledScenario Resolve entity ids to CARLA roles and type-check parameters, without importing CARLA. authoring.builders Factories that turn a compiled plan into the framework's own BaseAction / BaseCondition. Imports CARLA lazily. build_scenario_config, dump_scenario_config Render a document as the framework's Hydra scenario config, including a sweep section the existing sweeper understands. export_package -> ExportResult Write a reproducible Scenario Package and the wheelhouse built from it; raises PackageExportError (leaving nothing behind) when locking, verification or the wheelhouse fails. build_wheelhouse -> Wheelhouse Resolve a locked package's whole dependency graph into wheels that pip install --no-index --find-links can install with no uv, git or network; raises WheelhouseError. DraftStore, Draft, load_document, save_document YAML persistence for editor drafts and exported documents. new_document, blank_document Starter documents.

docs.title: Declarative runtime (autoware_carla_scenario.declarative)
docs.text: Symbol Description DeclarativeScenario A BaseScenario whose content comes from a ScenarioDocument. Registers the same pre/post-tick actions and pass/fail conditions a hand-written scenario would. Imports CARLA. DeclarativeScenarioConfig Hydra config group: document_path, timeout_seconds, spawn_overrides (the addressable per-entity spawn keys a sweep drives), param_overrides, and route (a logical scenario's route match, as scenario-expand writes it).

docs.title: Scenario editor (autoware_carla_scenario.editor)

Used by the scenario-editor CLI. A separate application from ui; neither imports the other.

docs.text: This document describes the software architecture of the autoware-carla-scenario package, with a focus on the scenario execution system and the result viewer.

docs.text: The scenario execution system is responsible for the full lifecycle of a CARLA scenario test: server management, map loading, actor spawning, tick-loop execution, condition evaluation, recording, and cleanup.

docs.title: Component Responsibilities
docs.text: Component File Responsibility CarlaServerManager server.py Start/stop/reuse the CARLA UE5 process. Manages lifecycle via process groups. ScenarioQueue scenario_queue.py Batch execution of multiple scenarios. Owns server and runner lifecycle. Context manager. ScenarioRunner scenario_runner.py Single-scenario execution: sync mode, tick loop, condition evaluation, recording, cleanup. BaseScenario scenario_base.py Abstract base. Subclasses implement setup() and is_done(). Registers conditions, actions, entities. TrafficBackend traffic/ Owns the vehicles the scenario did not author and answers their manoeuvre intents. traffic_manager by default; see Traffic Backends.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
The following sequence diagram shows the complete lifecycle of a single scenario execution:

sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI as CLI (main)
    participant SQ as ScenarioQueue
    participant CSM as CarlaServerManager
    participant SR as ScenarioRunner
    participant BS as BaseScenario
    participant W as carla.World
    participant TB as TrafficBackend
    participant TM as TrafficManager

    CLI->>SQ: add(scenario)
    CLI->>SQ: __enter__() / start()
    SQ->>CSM: start()
    Note over CSM: Reuse existing server<br/>or launch new process
    SQ->>SR: new ScenarioRunner(server, ...)
    SQ->>SR: load_map_by_name(), or<br/>load_map_by_overwriting_xodr()<br/>when map.overwrite_xodr is on
    SQ->>SR: Initialize MapManager<br/>(Lanelet2 + OpenDRIVE)

    CLI->>SQ: run_all()
    loop For each scenario
        SQ->>SR: run_scenario(scenario)

        rect rgb(240, 248, 255)
            Note over SR: Phase 1: Setup
            SR->>W: apply_settings(sync=True, dt=0.05)
            SR->>TB: prepare(TrafficContext)
            TB->>TM: set_synchronous_mode(True)
            TB->>TM: set_random_device_seed(seed)
            SR->>BS: set_client(client, tm_port)
            SR->>BS: set_traffic_backend(backend)
            SR->>BS: setup()
            Note over BS: Spawn NPCs, register<br/>conditions & actions
            SR->>W: Spawn ego vehicle
            SR->>BS: register_fail_condition(EntityExistence)
        end

        rect rgb(255, 248, 240)
            Note over SR: Phase 2: Warm-up (5 ticks)
            loop 5 times
                SR->>W: tick()
            end
            SR->>TB: start(world, skip_actor_ids)
            TB->>W: set_autopilot(True) on the vehicles it owns
            SR->>BS: set_initial_speed(ego)
        end

        rect rgb(240, 255, 240)
            Note over SR: Phase 3: Recording & Tick Loop
            SR->>W: start_recorder(path)
            SR->>BS: register_fail_condition(Timeout)
            loop Until done or condition met
                SR->>BS: pre_tick_actions.tick(world, elapsed)
                SR->>BS: pre_tick_callbacks(world)
                SR->>W: tick()
                SR->>BS: post_tick_actions.tick(world, elapsed)
                SR->>BS: post_tick_callbacks(world)
                SR->>BS: Check pass_conditions
                Note over SR: If any pass condition<br/>returns ScenarioResult → PASS
                SR->>BS: Check fail_conditions
                Note over SR: If any fail condition<br/>returns ScenarioResult → FAIL
                SR->>BS: is_done()?
                Note over SR: If True → PASS (default)
            end
        end

        rect rgb(255, 240, 240)
            Note over SR: Phase 4: Cleanup
            SR->>W: Destroy ego
            SR->>W: stop_recorder()
            SR->>TB: close()
            TB->>TM: shut_down()
            SR->>W: reload_world()
        end

        SR-->>SQ: ScenarioResult
    end

    CLI->>SQ: __exit__() / stop()
    SQ->>CSM: stop() (if owned)

docs.title: Tick Loop Detail
docs.text:
The tick loop runs at a fixed 20 Hz (0.05 s per tick) in CARLA synchronous mode. Each tick follows a strict evaluation order:

┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Single Tick Cycle                     │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Pre-tick actions      → action.tick(world, elapsed)   │
│  2. Pre-tick callbacks    → callback(world)               │
│  3. world.tick()          → advance simulation by 0.05 s  │
│  4. Ego entity            → ego.on_tick(world, elapsed)   │
│  5. Traffic backend       → backend.tick(world, elapsed)  │
│  6. Post-tick actions     → action.tick(world, elapsed)   │
│  7. Post-tick callbacks   → callback(world)               │
│  8. Coverage              → sample TICK / condition items │
│  9. Periodic logging      → ego OpenDRIVE position (1/s)  │
│  10. Pass conditions      → first satisfied → PASS & exit │
│  11. Fail conditions      → first triggered → FAIL & exit │
│  12. is_done() check      → True → PASS & exit            │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Evaluation semantics:

  • Pass conditions are checked first. The first condition to return a non-None ScenarioResult terminates the loop with a pass.
  • Fail conditions are checked only if no pass condition was satisfied. The first triggered fail condition terminates the loop with a failure.
  • If the loop exits via is_done() returning True with no condition triggered, the scenario is treated as passed.

docs.title: The scenario clock
docs.text:
_ScenarioClock supplies the elapsed every action, condition, entity and backend receives, and the elapsed_seconds on a ScenarioResult. It reads world.get_snapshot().timestamp.elapsed_seconds — simulated time, and nothing else.

The world advances by fixed_delta_seconds per tick and the loop steps it as fast as the slowest client allows (see max_tick_rate_hz), so how much simulated time fits into a second of real time is a property of the host. A scenario whose durations came off the wall clock would fire its triggers in different places on a fast machine and a slow one — the determinism that synchronous mode exists to provide.

That holds for ScenarioRunner.timeout_seconds as much as for a condition an author wrote. It is registered as a default TimeoutCondition on every scenario that registers no timeout of its own, so a scenario given sixty seconds is given sixty of its own however fast the host runs.

A scenario that registers a timeout of its own has said how long it runs, and the runner adds no default to cut it short: a red light whose drawn red phase is 13.4 s, given seven seconds after the green, runs for 20.4 s even when the run's default is twelve. Exactly these fail conditions count as its own:

  • a bare TimeoutCondition;
  • an OrCondition with a child that counts (an OR fires as soon as any child does);
  • a StickyCondition whose child counts (it hands on the child's failure as it comes; it latches only a pass).

A timeout under an AndCondition or a NotCondition does not count — it fires only on some other state of the world, so it does not bound the run — and neither does one under a PersistentCondition, which resets on every failure its child reports and so never fires around a timeout.

The run's default — ScenarioRunner(timeout_seconds=...), run_scenario(timeout_seconds=...), ScenarioQueue.add(timeout_seconds=...), and with them a scenario.timeout_seconds= override — therefore does not apply to a scenario with a timeout of its own. A hand-written scenario that builds its timeout from cfg.timeout_seconds still follows the override, since that is the same key; one that builds it from another (traffic_light_compliance with timeout_after_green_seconds set) does not. A DeclarativeScenario always has one: it registers its document's timeout_seconds (or the Hydra override of it) itself, so a timeout node in the document is a second limit beside it, and whichever fires first fails the run. A sweep keeps the wall-clock sweep.job_timeout_seconds guard over every job either way.

Wall-clock protection against a stuck simulator lives outside the scenario clock, where it belongs:

Guard Where Covers CARLA client RPC timeout (60 s) ScenarioRunner.__init__ world.tick() stops returning sweep.job_timeout_seconds (120 s) sweeper config a whole job overrunning

The clock starts after the ego is ready, so an entity that needs an autonomy stack to come up does not spend the scenario's timeout booting. Simulation time does advance during that wait, which is why the start is measured rather than assumed to be zero.

docs.title: ScenarioQueue: Batch Execution and Retry
docs.text:
ScenarioQueue wraps ScenarioRunner to support sequential execution of multiple scenarios:

graph LR
    subgraph ScenarioQueue
        direction TB
        A[Scenario 1] --> B[Cooldown]
        B --> C[Scenario 2]
        C --> D[Cooldown]
        D --> E[Scenario N]
    end

    subgraph Retry["Retry Logic"]
        direction TB
        R1["Attempt 1"] -->|fail| R2["Cooldown"]
        R2 --> R3["Attempt 2"]
        R3 -->|fail| R4["..."]
        R4 --> R5["Attempt N"]
        R5 -->|fail| R6["RuntimeError, or an errored result (continue_on_error)"]
    end

Key features:

  • Cooldown: Configurable wait time (cooldown_seconds) between consecutive scenarios to allow CARLA server cleanup.
  • Retry: Failed scenarios are retried up to cooldown_max_retries times before raising an error. With run_all(continue_on_error=True), which batch mode uses, a scenario that fails every attempt is recorded instead as a failed result naming the error (errored_indices() tells it from a scenario that ran and failed), the world is reloaded, and the queue goes on with the next one.
  • Server ownership: Accepts an external CarlaServerManager or creates and owns one internally.
  • pytest integration: as_fixture() generates a session-scoped pytest fixture with automatic skip when there is no CARLA to launch.

docs.title: Recordings of a run
docs.text:
A run leaves two recordings, neither of which renders anything:

  1. The CARLA recording ({stem}.log): CARLA's native recorder captures every actor's state from the moment the ego exists, warm-up included. CARLA's replayer (client.replay_file()) plays it back on a server running the same map.
  2. The trajectory log ({stem}.trajectory.jsonl, Trajectory Log): written by the runner itself after every tick of the scenario, in-process -- every vehicle and pedestrian, the lights, the map the run was on, the ego's debug markers, each condition's state and the verdict. A Rerun recording made from it with the autoware_carla_scenario_rerun package is how a run is seen (Seeing a run): with rerun.enabled=true the runner hands each closed log to a RerunConverter (rerun.py), which converts it on a background thread while the next case runs, and the run waits for it at the end.

Releases before 15.0.0 also rendered a video from the CARLA recording after each run ({stem}.mp4, a replay with an RGB camera and ffmpeg); that is gone, and so is the ffmpeg it needed.

docs.title: Debug markers
docs.text:
The ego entity can show what the world does not: EgoVehicle.debug_markers() returns what it is following on the current tick (DebugMarkers, polylines in CARLA world coordinates, from autoware_carla_scenario.debug_markers). The base class shows nothing; the entities that follow a trajectory show it, as a green line with a dot at each point:

Entity What it shows CarlaDriverEntity The driver policy's current plan Ros2EgoEntity The trajectory it is tracking, while a trajectory command source drives

After every tick of the scenario the runner asks the ego for its markers and writes them into the trajectory log when they change (a markers record). An entity hands out the same DebugMarkers object until its plan changes (plan_markers() builds one per plan), so the log holds one per plan rather than one per tick. A viewer of the run draws them beside the path the ego drove (DRIVEN_PATH_COLOR), which the log's ticks give.

An entity of your own shows more by overriding debug_markers():

from autoware_carla_scenario.debug_markers import DebugMarkers, DebugPolyline

class MyEgo(EgoVehicle):
    def debug_markers(self) -> DebugMarkers:
        markers = DebugMarkers()
        markers.add_polyline(
            DebugPolyline(self._path_points, color=(255, 0, 0), point_size=0.1)
        )
        return markers

docs.text:
Conditions evaluate scenario pass/fail criteria. All conditions inherit from BaseCondition:

    BaseCondition <|-- PersistentCondition

    BaseCondition --> ScenarioResult : returns

Condition categories:

Category Conditions Description Temporal TimeoutCondition, ElapsedTimeCondition Time-based triggers Safety CollisionCondition, EntityExistenceCondition, OffRoadFractionCondition Collision detection — with anything, or with a named entity or class of object — actor alive checks, and leaving the driving lanes by more than a tolerance Position EntityLanePositionCondition, WaypointCondition Road/lane position, waypoint crossing Relative EntityDistanceCondition, EntityPositionDistanceCondition, TimeToCollisionCondition, TimeHeadwayCondition, RelativeSpeedCondition Gap to another entity or to a place on the map, time to collision, following headway and speed difference Motion SpeedCondition, AccelerationCondition, StandstillCondition, TemporaryStopCondition Speed and acceleration thresholds, standstill detection, stop-and-go Traffic TrafficSignalCondition, TrafficSignalControllerCondition One light's state, or a whole junction's phase Composition AndCondition, OrCondition, NotCondition Logical combinators Stateful StickyCondition, PersistentCondition Latch once satisfied / persist across ticks Utility AlwaysTrueCondition Unconditional trigger (default for actions)

A collision with map geometry is a collision. CARLA gives no actor for the other side of a collision with a wall, a kerb or another part of the map that is not an actor (CollisionEvent.other_actor is None). An untargeted CollisionCondition (no target, target_type ANY) fires on it, and its details say other_actor_type: "not an actor". A targeted one ignores it, as it ignores any collision that is not the one named, and keeps waiting for that one (#277).

Distances carry a coordinate system. EntityDistanceCondition, TimeHeadwayCondition and TimeToCollisionCondition each take a coordinate_system, which is OpenSCENARIO's coordinateSystem attribute:

  • ENTITY (the default, so existing documents keep their meaning) is a world-frame offset projected onto the subject's heading or direction of travel. It equals the along-lane gap on a straight road, under-reads on a curve, and past a quarter turn inverts — at which point a headway stops firing for a leader that is directly in front.
  • LANE projects both entities onto the OpenDRIVE road they share and compares their s, which is what scenario_simulator_v2 measures. For TTC the closing speed is resolved onto the road too, so a vehicle's cornering is not counted as approach.

LANE follows the chain of connected roads between the two, which it has to: an OpenDRIVE map is cut into short roads — a median of 33 m on the converter's own fixture — so a leader at an ordinary following distance is usually on the next road, not the one behind it. Measuring within one road would answer "no measurement" to most following scenarios.

A junction is measured too. Its connecting roads are ordinary roads carrying junction="<id>", so the chain reaches them like any other, and two entities on one connecting road need no walk at all — which is the measurement an intersection scenario is usually about. What a junction cannot settle is which way out a vehicle will take, so that ambiguity is reported rather than hidden: where several chains reach the target the shortest answers, by distance rather than by which link the map happens to list first, and every measurement carries whether it ran through a junction. A caller that must not have a turn chosen for it passes across_junctions=False and gets no measurement instead.

Nothing falls back to the straight line: silently swapping one measure for another makes a scenario pass for the wrong reason. Bounded at 200 m, which covers a motorway-speed TTC over the seconds a threshold is set at. The measurement itself lives in autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate.lane_distance.

check() contract:

  • Returns ScenarioResult when the condition is triggered (satisfied or violated).
  • Returns None when not yet triggered.
  • __init_subclass__ auto-wraps check() to track the latest result for UI display.

docs.title: Action Architecture
docs.text:
Actions execute side effects when their trigger condition is met:

classDiagram
    class BaseAction {
        <<abstract>>
        +label: str
        +timing: TickTiming
        +once: bool
        +state: ActionState
        +reissues_while_running: bool
        +execute(world) void
        +tick(world, elapsed) void
    }

    class BaseCondition {
        <<abstract>>
    }

    class TrafficSignalAction
    class TrafficSignalControllerAction
    class EnvironmentAction
    class TurnAction
    class WalkStraightAction
    class LaneChangeAction
    class RoutingAction
    class SetSpeedAction
    class FollowTrajectoryAction

    BaseAction <|-- TrafficSignalAction
    BaseAction <|-- TrafficSignalControllerAction
    BaseAction <|-- EnvironmentAction
    BaseAction <|-- TurnAction
    BaseAction <|-- WalkStraightAction
    BaseAction <|-- LaneChangeAction
    BaseAction <|-- RoutingAction
    BaseAction <|-- SetSpeedAction
    BaseAction <|-- FollowTrajectoryAction
    BaseAction --> BaseCondition : trigger condition

Action lifecycle:

Each tick the runner calls action.tick(world, elapsed), which walks the action through the OpenSCENARIO storyboard element states held in ActionState (standbyState -> startTransition -> runningState -> endTransition -> completeState).

  1. Standby. The trigger BaseCondition is evaluated via condition.check(world, elapsed). A non-None result fires the action: execute(world) runs and the action enters startTransition.
  2. Running. The trigger is not re-evaluated, so one run cannot begin on top of another. Two independent questions are then asked every tick, in this order:

Does execute repeat? — reissues_while_running. This is a fact about the command, not about the manoeuvre: a TrafficManager target persists until it is changed, while a command that walks a target towards a goal has to be re-sent on every tick to move at all. Because that depends on what drives the entity, it is resolved in the order the knowledge is available:

Source Who knows reissue= constructor argument whoever knows the backend — the injection point _reissues_by_default() override the action, from its own configuration or by asking its entity REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT class attribute the action's class, when it has one answer

When does the run end? — until, a BaseCondition. This is the same kind of object the trigger is written in, so the two ends of a run read together. No until means there was nothing to wait for, and the run is over on the tick after the one it was commanded on.

Keeping the two apart is what lets both shapes exist. LaneChangeAction hands work to the simulator and watches for it to land — force_lane_change returns long before the vehicle is in the next lane, and must not be re-sent — so it supplies a LaneChangeSettledCondition as its until and does not repeat. A rate-limited speed change says both. 3. End. endTransition is held for one tick so a condition can watch for it. Then once decides: True (default) means completeState and no further evaluation; False returns the action to standby to be triggered again.

until, reissues_while_running and once are all independent — until says when this run ends, reissues_while_running says whether the command repeats while it does, and once says whether another run may begin.

The adversarial actions (TeraSim's adversities, one entity each), NADE (AdversarialTrafficAction, which picks which agent carries out which adversity, with its importance-sampling weight) and the scheduled stalled objects build on this lifecycle: see Adversarial Actions and NADE.

ActionStateCondition observes these states, which is what lets one actor react to another finishing a manoeuvre rather than to the command having gone out (done only reports the latter).

Tick timing:

Actions can be registered as pre-tick (before world.tick()) or post-tick (after world.tick()) via BaseScenario.register_pre_tick() / register_post_tick().

docs.title: Traffic signals: one light, or a junction's cycle
docs.text:
Two pairs of primitives, answering two different questions.

TrafficSignalAction / TrafficSignalCondition set and read one light. That is enough to arrange a specific state and no more: a junction assembled a light at a time can be left with two conflicting approaches green, a state no real road reaches, and an amber has no name at all — it is just a colour one light happens to be showing.

TrafficSignalControllerAction / TrafficSignalControllerCondition work in phases. A phase names every signal its controller drives and how long it holds, so showing one puts the whole junction into a known state at once, and waiting for one is a statement about the junction rather than about a colour.

A junction is declared in two halves, split along what changes between scenarios and what does not.

map.signal_groups is the road. Which signals change as one, and which movements cross each other, are facts about the junction: every scenario that runs here inherits the same ones. Naming a group is also the only way a phase table stays writable — one approach of three lanes is three regulatory elements, and nishishinjuku declares 164 of them.

map.traffic_signal_controllers is this scenario's timing. A test of an ego creeping into a long amber and a test of the same crossing on a short cycle are two scenarios on one road, so the durations are the scenario's to choose. OpenSCENARIO reads the same way: RoadNetwork/TrafficSignals holds the controllers, and RoadNetwork is a section of the scenario file, beside the LogicFile that names the map rather than inside it — scenario_simulator_v2 builds its TrafficSignalController from that scenario XML too.

map:
  signal_groups:                        # the road: no colours, no durations
    - name: ns
      lanelet2_regulatory_element_ids: [1001, 1003]
      conflicts_with: [ew]              # read symmetrically
    - name: ew
      lanelet2_regulatory_element_ids: [1002]

  traffic_signal_controllers:           # this scenario's timing
    - name: crossing
      phases:
        - name: ns_green
          duration_seconds: 20.0
          states:
            - {group: ns, state: green}
            - {group: ew, state: red}
        - name: ns_amber
          duration_seconds: 3.0
          states:
            - {group: ns, state: yellow}
            - {group: ew, state: red}
        - name: all_red
          duration_seconds: 1.0
          states:
            - {group: ns, state: red}
            - {group: ew, state: red}
    - name: next_junction
      reference: crossing      # a green wave along a corridor is declared,
      delay_seconds: 8.0       # not timed by a chain of actions
      phases: [...]

A state may name a lanelet2_regulatory_element_id instead of a group, which is the escape hatch for a single light — including the case below, where the junction's impossible state is the thing under test.

autoware_carla_scenario.signals turns those declarations into running SignalController objects at scenario setup. Each is registered as a pre-tick callback and cycles on its own: a phase holds for its duration_seconds and then hands over to the next, looping. No runner change was needed — durations are differences, so the controller reads the world's own simulated elapsed seconds directly.

The action jumps to a named phase and the cycle carries on from there, so a junction forced green does not thereby stay green; holding it is a separate decision, made by declaring a phase long enough to hold. The condition reads the phase off the controller, not off the lights: the controller is what decided them, so a junction that some other actor happened to set to the same colours does not read as that phase.

A reference offsets one controller's start from another's, which is how a progressive system — a green wave — is written. The offsets are declared; nothing has to time them.

Groups are what make the original problem checkable. Two conflicting approaches green is the state a junction assembled one light at a time can reach and a real road cannot; while a phase was a list of regulatory element ids, nothing could tell. Now conflicts_with says which movements cross, so the validator rejects any phase that shows green or amber to both — amber included, because a junction showing amber to one movement still has vehicles in it, which is why a real one puts an all-red clearance between them. A scenario whose subject is a junction in that state names the regulatory elements directly and is left alone: naming a group is how an author invokes the map's statement about that movement, this rule included.

The validator also rejects a delay with no reference, a reference to a controller the document does not declare, a loop of them, duplicate controller, phase or group names, a signal in two groups, a group that drives nothing, a conflict naming an undeclared group, a phase state naming both a group and an element or neither, an unknown state, and any action or condition naming a controller or phase that does not exist — all while the document is being edited, because a misspelt phase name is invisible at runtime: the junction cycles normally and the scenario just waits forever.

Build session lists and condition trees. runner.py ui/runner.py Execute uv run scenario as subprocesses in a background thread.
