  • conditions.codon: beside its exports, ActionStateCondition, LaneChangeSettledCondition, compare, beside_lane_id, and ConditionStatus, all but its details (a dict[str, Any], which Codon cannot express: _OMITTED_PARAMETERS), and no other name it defines (find_actor_in_list it imports from entity_role.codon, as Python's conditions.base does). ActionStateCondition's state is an ActionState or its OpenSCENARIO name, and its actions any dict of action ids to actions: actions.codon imports conditions.codon, so an action is checked by what BaseAction declares.
  • entity_role.codon: beside EntityRole, find_actor_in_list (a carla.ActorList or a list of actors, as Python's) and find_actor_in_world.
  • kinematics.codon: beside its exports, normalize_angle_deg, and frame_of and FrameMismatchError as coordinate.codon declares them.
  • coordinate.codon: AnyPose, the Union alias, by its members' names, in order, for a scenario's own annotations (no model function takes it: a Union parameter crashes Codon 0.19, so each is generic or overloaded).
  • constants.codon: every constant, by value (EGO_ROLE_NAME as EntityRole.ego()), and no name constants.py lacks.
  • route.codon: every name it declares -- parse_anchor, scenario_route, scenario_route_frame, RouteFrame, RouteMatch, and APPROACHES, CROSSWALK_LEGS and SIDES by value. RouteMatch's constructor is generic: Python's is a frozen dataclass of variadic tuples (tuple[int, ...]), which Codon cannot express, but the model's takes the same parameters, and an overload of none is a compile_error (Codon builds a class without fields with no arguments otherwise; see What Codon builds by the fields below), so a call Python refuses fails the check too.
  • trajectory.codon: beside its exports, ResolvedTrajectory, TrajectorySample and the TrajectoryPosition Union, by its members' names, in order, and no other name.
  • traffic.codon: every name it declares -- TurnDirection, LaneChangeDirection, TrafficContext and traffic.registry's functions and TRAFFIC_BACKEND_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP (by value). TrafficBackendFactory differs on purpose (_DIFFERING): a Callable alias in Python of a mapping of any values (Hydra's options), which Codon has no type for, and an empty class in the model, there only so the checked traffic package's re-export resolves; a test checks that it stays empty.
  • utils/traffic_light.codon: its three functions, and no other name.
  • coverage.codon, entity.codon, odd.codon: the names the checked modules import (_BOUNDARY), COVERAGE_SCHEMA and CoverGroup by value.
  • The models of one framework module each (_MODULE_MODELS): _bridge_pose, action_state, carla_install, debug_markers, trajectory_recorder, environment, autoware_bridge/grpc_server, autoware_stack/launcher, autoware_stack/devcontainer (and its values), driver/egodriver_client, _map_source, maps/cache, maps/z_offset_cache, maps/road_network_cache, ui/models, _ros2, metrics, measures and utils/traffic_light, each declaring exactly the names compared; ros2/cyclone where cyclonedds is installed.
  • Every public name of a modelled module: each name a module the model has exports in Python (its __all__, or the public names it defines when it has none) is declared by the model or listed, with the reason, in typecheck/not_modelled.py (NOT_MODELLED), and a name listed there must be neither declared nor gone from Python. Each declared one is compared as above, re-exports included (kinematics.frame_of). OddSample and OddCase differ on purpose (_DIFFERING): an opaque, unbuildable stand-in for openodd's sample, and the @tuple of the pair Python's alias names.
  • Every public member of a compared class (#265): the comparisons above check that what a model class declares exists in Python; this checks the converse. For every class they compare, enums included, each public method, property, class attribute, dataclass field and instance attribute the package's Python, or openodd's, defines on the class or a class it derives from (VehicleEntity.set_desired_speed() is BackendDriven's) is declared by the model class or one of its model bases, or listed, with the reason, in NOT_MODELLED_MEMBERS (typecheck/not_modelled.py), under the class or the Python base that defines it (BaseCondition.get_details for every condition). openodd's classes, which the package re-exports (OddAttribute, OddModule, OddDefinition, OddCondition, CoverItem, CrossItem, CoverageReport), are compared as the package's are (#298), each listed under the name the package gives it (openodd's Condition is OddCondition). A listed member must still be public in Python and absent from the model. A dataclass's public field is a member too, beside the constructor's parameter it is compared as (#298): the model declares it as a field or, where a field would change the constructor Codon generates (What Codon builds by the fields, below), as a read-only property (RouteMatch.lanelet_ids, a List[int] for Python's tuple[int, ...]; TrajectoryVertex.position, the union of the ten poses, which narrows with isinstance and passes on to a new TrajectoryVertex, and which the None check's pass refuses un-narrowed where one pose is expected, #309; CoverItem's fields). A frozen dataclass's field is read-only in Python too; writing a CoverItem's is refused, which Python allows, and a scenario, which registers its items with register_cover(), has none to write. An attribute a method sets on the instance (self.<name> = ... or setattr(self, "<name>", ...), read from the class's source, __init__'s and the others', openodd's included; one set under a name computed at run time is not found) is a member too (#307), as Python reads it like any other: the model declares it as a read-only property, since a field would change the constructor Codon generates (TimeoutCondition.timeout_seconds, OddDefinition.attributes, OddAttribute.target and item, TrafficSinkAction.removed, RouteFrame's match, map, graph and lanelets). Writing one is refused, which Python allows ('TimeoutCondition' object has no attribute 'timeout_seconds'), except in the __init__ of a scenario's own subclass, where the assignment declares the subclass's own attribute. An enum is compared beyond its members (#307): a model enum is a @tuple of its value, so Codon gives it no Enum, and it declares Enum's name as a property, a chain of if self == Rule.MEMBER: return "MEMBER" that test_typecheck_model.py compares with each member's Python name, in order (it also compares each member's value), and its own methods and properties (ComparisonRule.text, CollisionTargetType.matches(), LaneChangeDirection.to_carla_bool()). A scenario's own enum gets its name from the check's rewrite (below). The scenario check adds the reason to Codon's error:
scenario.py:68:19: error: 'CaseScenario' object has no attribute 'traffic_backend': BaseScenario.traffic_backend is not part of the Codon model, on purpose: takes or returns the run's TrafficBackend, ...

Left out are what returns or takes a value Codon has no type for (a dict[str, Any]: a condition's get_details() and to_summary_dict(), to_dict(), describe(), RouteMatch.to_config() and from_config()), the run's traffic backend (set_traffic_backend(), traffic_backend), RouteMatch.junction(), junctions and segments (a RouteSegmentMatch), a field of Any (ConditionStatus.details, RouteLanelet.values, OddModule.metadata, SweepConfig's Hydra mappings, CoverItem's expression, ignore and values, OddAttribute.probe), a class held as a value (BaseScenario.ego_type: a scenario reads ego_requires_goal and calls create_ego()), RouteFrame.features (route.geometry's queries, which the library check compiles from their source), openodd's evaluation, sampling and archive of an ODD (OddDefinition.evaluate(), sample(), archive(), ..., OddCondition.evaluate()) and its report's rows (CoverageReport.entries, ...), and the members of the classes the model declares for the library check alone (CarlaDriverEntity, the egodriver and bridge servers, the ROS 2 transport and its config, the map cache's MapSource, RunEnvironment). An ODD's members compile as they run:

roads = OddModule("roads", include_and=[location.is_in(["urban"])], labels=["fair"])
roads.as_situation(cover_by="meters", target=100.0)
text = roads.conditions()[0].describe() + roads.labels[0] + location.cover_by
for attribute in odd.attributes:
    text += attribute.name + str(attribute.target)

So do an instance attribute and an enum's name and methods:

timeout = TimeoutCondition(cfg.timeout_seconds, label="timeout")
logger.info("limit %f, %s", timeout.timeout_seconds, ComparisonRule.LESS_THAN.name)
logger.info("%s %s", ComparisonRule.LESS_THAN.text, LaneChangeDirection.LEFT.to_carla_bool())
- Every model file: each .codon of the package's model is in one of the tables above or exempt with the reason (_UNCOMPARED_MODEL_FILES: the model's helpers, the modules coordinate.codon and entity.codon re-export, and the __init__ of a checked subpackage, which models nothing), so a model file no test compares fails the suite. - Third-party models: carla_driver_interface's geometry, python-dotenv's load_dotenv, pyxodr's RoadNetwork and lxml's element.

A constant whose model value is a literal (a str, int, float or a tuple of them) is compared by its value and type (a tuple's items' too: 1 is no 1.0 or True) wherever it is compared, and a Literal alias (ui.models.Status) as the type of its values. Any other constant fails the comparison unless a test of its own compares it (EGO_ROLE_NAME, BUILT_IN_METRICS, BUILT_IN_MEASURES).

What Codon builds by the fields. Codon 0.19 gives every class a constructor of its fields, its bases' first, by position or by name, beside the __init__ it declares: a class without fields is built with no arguments (VehicleEntity(), #225), a condition or an action with the label it inherits alone (TimeoutCondition("10"), TurnAction("npc1"), #236), and any class by fields its constructor does not take (DebugMarkers([]), CoverItem("speed"), RunProgress(1, 2, "case", "running"), #244), where Python refuses each. A class that derives from one of Codon's exceptions (Static[Exception]) also takes its bases' constructors, and its fields start with BaseException's eight: FrameMismatchError("x") passed by Exception(typename, msg="") (#244). A class that derives from a model class plainly does not take its base's __init__.

Codon tries the __init__ overloads a class declares from the last one up, and those it generates or inherits only after them, so the model declares, ahead of the constructor, an __init__ of as many arguments whose body is a compile_error:

class TimeoutCondition(BaseCondition):
    def __init__(self, label):
        compile_error("TimeoutCondition(): no constructor takes these arguments "
                      "(required: keyword label)")

    def __init__(self, timeout_seconds: float = 60.0, *_kw, label = _Required()):
        ...

The constructor, declared last, still wins every call it takes (TimeoutCondition(label="t"), TimeoutCondition(10.0, label="t")); the refusing overload only takes what would reach Codon's own. The one of as many arguments as the class has fields takes the fields' names, so a call by them (CoverItem(name="speed")) is refused too.

test_typecheck_model.py compares the last __init__ with Python's and finds the overloads needed. For every compared class that declares an __init__, it counts each number of positional arguments the constructor Codon generates (the fields, _codon_fields) or an exception base's (_inherited_inits, Codon's own read from _CODON_EXCEPTIONS, which a test compares with Codon's standard library) would take, and asks Python whether its constructor binds as many placeholders (inspect.signature().bind). Where Python refuses and the model's constructor does not take them either, the model declares the refusing overload of that many; where the model's constructor takes them through *_kw, its _keyword_only(_kw, ...) refuses them (OddModule, OddAttribute, BaseScenario). The classes it finds:

Arguments Classes none RouteMatch, RouteFrame, VehicleEntity, PedestrianEntity, CoverageCollector, CoverageReport, EgoDriverGrpcClient, Ros2EgoTransport (and CycloneRos2Transport, compared apart) the label the conditions and actions whose constructor Python refuses one argument (SpeedCondition, TurnAction) the fields DebugMarkers, CoverItem, OddCondition (one), RunProgress (four) an exception's FrameMismatchError (one, two, ten), DevContainerError, MapCacheError (none, two, eight)

RouteCoverage declares Python's fields in Python's order (#298), so the constructor Codon generates of them takes no call Python's refuses, and the one it declares refuses each.

Every condition and action declares the overload of one, its label, even where Python takes one argument by position: a call the constructor refuses by its type (TimeoutCondition("10")) would still reach the one Codon generates.

Those constructors take their parameters by keyword too, and a call by keyword Python refuses passes where no guard takes those names: an exception's base parameters (DevContainerError(typename="x"), FrameMismatchError("x", message="y")), or a class's field names (OddAttribute(name="speed", unit="m", text="t"), EntityRole(_value="x")). So the test also enumerates every call, by position and by keyword, the constructor Codon generates or an exception base's would bind, and requires, for each one Python and the model's constructor refuse, a refusing overload that binds it too: an __init__ of the fields' names (OddAttribute, OddDefinition, EntityRole, TrajectoryVertex, EgoConfig, BaseScenario, RunEnvironment), and of typename and typename, message (DevContainerError, MapCacheError; FrameMismatchError takes one positional typename already). A class whose __init__ takes its fields by position and by name needs none: the constructor Codon generates is its own.

A scenario that imports a module with no model (lanelet2's matching, say, or a framework module outside the public API) is refused with a message naming the module. For a framework module, the message says where the model declares the names imported as Python exports them, and only where Python's module has the same object, so the import it suggests runs too; a name the model leaves out on purpose is refused with its reason, whichever module it is imported from (#237):

scenario.py:3: error: autoware_carla_scenario.actions.base is not part of the Codon model; import ActionState from autoware_carla_scenario.action_state instead
scenario.py:4: error: autoware_carla_scenario.route.parse_route_search is not part of the Codon model, on purpose: the route search, parsed from a document's YAML ...

Third-party packages the framework reads are modelled as far as it reads them (lanelet2, pyxodr, carla_driver_interface, python-dotenv; see Making a module compile), and a scenario may use what those models declare.

docs.title: Writing a scenario that type-checks
docs.text:
A scenario is ordinary typed Python. Codon is stricter than Python in a few places, and the checker smooths over most of them (it rewrites X | None into Optional[X], drops @dataclass (and appends the ==, ordering and hash it generates) and resolves field(...) defaults, accepts keyword-only parameters, required ones after a default included, gives a list of different conditions the type list[BaseCondition], checks a tuple[X, ...] return annotation as a List[X], drops a parameter or return annotation naming a class the module defines further down, which Codon cannot name yet, gives a subclass that keeps its base's __init__ that __init__, and types the return None of a function returning Optional[X]; see below). What a scenario has to do itself:

  • Import its own modules from its own package. A module of the scenario's package imported as a module works (#310): Codon 0.19 resolves from X import name only as a name X/__init__ defines, and an absolute import a.b only from the importing file's directory, so the checker rewrites, on the same line, from . import helpers, from pkg import helpers and import pkg.helpers as helpers in pkg/scenario.py into import helpers as helpers, and from .sub import mod into import sub.mod as mod. A module outside the importing module's package (from .. import helpers in pkg/sub/scenario.py, or import pkg as p) has no such form, and neither has one imported without a name (import pkg.helpers, which binds pkg): each is refused at its line, naming the form that works, which is to import the names (from ..helpers import speed_kph) or to name the module (import pkg.helpers as helpers):
scenario.py:3: error: `from .. import helpers` imports the module pkg.helpers as a module, which Codon 0.19 resolves only inside the importing module's own package (pkg.sub): import the names instead (`from ..helpers import name`)
  • Import a name once. Python accepts from autoware_carla_scenario import ComparisonRule in the import header and again further down, and so does the check (#354): Codon 0.19 leaves a module-level name imported twice undefined in every module but the one it compiles first, so a use of it failed the whole function with a bare "cannot typecheck". The checker drops a module-level import that repeats an identical earlier one (the same module and name, under the same alias), on its line: the repeat becomes pass, or loses just the repeated names. An import in a function or an if is left as written. A name imported from two different places (from a import X, then from b import X) means the later one in Python: the checker drops the earlier import when nothing reads the name in between, and refuses the later import, naming the first, when something does:
scenario.py:12: error: `ComparisonRule` is imported again from somewhere else (first on line 5) after it was used, which Codon 0.19 cannot compile: import each name once, under its own name (`import ... as other` to tell two apart)
  • Declare the attributes it assigns on self, at class level, with their type:
class MyScenario(BaseScenario):
    _config: MyScenarioConfig

    def __init__(self, ego_config, spawn_pose, config=None, ground_projection=None):
        super().__init__(ego_config, spawn_pose=spawn_pose, ground_projection=ground_projection)
        self._config = config or MyScenarioConfig()

A bare annotation is ignored by Python, so this changes nothing when the scenario runs; Codon needs it to type an attribute of a subclass. The check names each undeclared attribute and suggests its type.

Declare them in every class of the scenario's modules, helper classes included (#218). The check refuses an undeclared attribute of a class with a base, a subclass, or at least one class-level annotation: once a class declares one attribute, Codon gives it only those it declares. A plain class that declares none has its attributes inferred from its __init__, which Codon cannot always do: not for self._samples = [] (a list of nothing yet), and not in a method the scenario check calls on its own (What is checked), on a value its __init__ did not build ('int' does not match expected type 'NoneType', during the realization of get(self: Counter[NoneType])). Codon's error is then at a line of the helper, or names the attribute holding the helper, not the helper (type of attribute '_tracker' of object 'GapCondition' cannot be inferred), so the check adds, for that helper, each attribute it assigns without declaring it, at its line, with the type to declare:

scenario.py:34: error: GapTracker._samples is assigned without a type: declare it in the class body, e.g. `_samples: list[...]` ...
- Use only the public API from autoware_carla_scenario and its listed subpackages, and the BaseScenario attributes meant for subclasses (ego_config, ego_entity, world, _ground_projection, ...). An import from a modelled framework module must also work in Python (#214): the model declares a few names the Python module does not have (coordinate.RoadNetwork, entity.EgoConfig, actions.ActionState: import it from autoware_carla_scenario.action_state, as Python does) and model-only helper modules (autoware_carla_scenario._tc, _lists), and an import of one inside a function would compile and raise ImportError when the function first runs. So the check imports each modelled module a scenario imports from, in Python, and refuses each name it lacks, as an attribute and as a submodule, at the import's line:

scenario.py:118: error: autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate has no RoadNetwork in Python, whatever its Codon model declares: `from autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate import RoadNetwork` raises ImportError when the scenario runs

An import under if TYPE_CHECKING: is exempt: Python never runs it. - Define every abstract method of what you build (#215). Codon has no @abstractmethod, and the model gives BaseScenario.is_done(), BaseCondition.check() and BaseAction.execute() bodies (its built-in conditions and actions inherit them), so a scenario whose is_done was renamed, or a condition that defines only _check, compiles, and Python refuses to build it (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class). The check asks Python (inspect.isabstract) about each class of the scenario's modules that is built, the scenario class (the runner builds it) or a class the modules call by name (GapCondition(...)), and refuses one still abstract at its class line:

scenario.py:46: error: GapCondition is built (at scenario.py:99) but leaves abstract check undefined: define it in GapCondition, or Python refuses to build it (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class)

A class only derived from, such as an abstract base of the scenario's own conditions with an @abstractmethod of its own, is never called and may stay abstract. - Pass numbers of the declared type. An int is accepted for a float, but not inside a container: a list[float] parameter wants [1.0, 2.0]. YAML values are converted for you. - An empty [] or () is any sequence (#264). Codon gives an empty display no element type ([] is a List[NoneType], () a tuple of no items), so the model takes one wherever Python takes a Sequence[X] (RoutingAction(EGO_ROLE_NAME, goal), whose waypoints default to (), waypoints=[], self.waypoint_poses = [], derive_goal_from_route(()), AndCondition([], ...), an ODD's all_of([])) through _acs_sequence (_tc.codon), and checks the elements of any other: waypoints=[460, 265] and waypoints=[None] are refused, in EgoVehicle.route_to() too. - A sequence of names is a list or a tuple, not a str (#299). Python's typing takes a str as a Sequence[str], and the framework then reads each of its characters as a name (roots="roads" fails at run time with "no root module ['r', 'o', 'a', 'd', 's']"). Here the check is stricter than mypy, on purpose: _expect_str_sequence (_tc.codon) refuses a str (or an Optional[str]) where a sequence of names is taken, the items of BaseScenario.register_cross(), OddModule's labels and OddDefinition's roots, and takes a list or a tuple of str, an empty one too:

scenario.py:41: error: BaseScenario.register_cross(): items: expected a sequence of names (a list or a tuple of str), not a str: wrap it in a list

OddAttribute.is_in("urban") still passes: it takes an Iterable[Any] of values, and CPython takes a str's characters as values. - Call a manoeuvre your own entity class overrides with every argument, by position. VehicleEntity and EgoVehicle declare the manoeuvres they take from traffic.driven.BackendDriven (set_desired_speed(), change_lane(), lane_change_finished(), turn_at_junction(), release_from_traffic(), ...), and an EgoVehicle subclass's override of one is checked as a hook. Codon 0.19 calls a method a subclass overrides through a dispatch thunk, which takes no keyword argument, fills in no default (set_client(client) needs its tm_port then), and cannot call turn_at_junction(world, direction, **kwargs) at all: once a class of the scenario overrides it, a call of it does not compile ("cannot typecheck"), on the subclass as on its base; turn with a TurnAction instead. A class that only defines the override, and never calls it, compiles. (Declaring Python's **kwargs as TurnAction's three keywords would not help: the thunk fills in none of their defaults, so even turn_at_junction(world, direction) would fail, and a backend's own keywords would be refused.) - A dict of different actions (or conditions) is a dict of their base. Codon types a dict display by its first item, so the check rewrites one whose values are not evidently of one type, as it does a list display: {"turn": turn, "lane_change": lc} (a TurnAction and a LaneChangeAction) becomes {"turn": _acs_base(turn), "lane_change": _acs_base(lc)}, which makes each action a BaseAction (each condition a BaseCondition): a dict[str, BaseAction] as in Python, which passes as ActionStateCondition's actions. Assigned to an annotated variable, actions: dict[str, BaseAction] = {...}, it becomes a dict of the annotated type (_acs_dict_into, when the key and value types are plain names). A value of another type is still refused at the display's line:

scenario.py:73: error: 'int' does not match expected type 'BaseAction'

Any other value is left to Codon's display, which types it as before ({"a": 1, "b": speed} is a dict[str, float], a value with None is optional). Values evidently of one type (all literals, all calls of the same name, all members of one enum) are left as written. Building the dict one item at a time into a dict[str, BaseAction] stays valid. - Convert nested mappings in the config. The runner passes a YAML mapping to the config class as a dict, so a field annotated with a dataclass (goal: Goal) holds one at run time unless the config's __post_init__ turns it into a Goal, as the built-in configs do for their NPC lists. The check builds the config the same way and refuses an unconverted mapping at its scenario.<key>.

  • Annotate every parameter of every function and method, helpers and hook overrides included. Every function of the scenario's modules is compiled, whether setup() reaches it or not, with a value of each parameter's annotated type (What is checked). A function with a parameter that has no annotation, one Codon cannot express or one naming a TypeVar, is only compiled where setup() and is_done() call it, and the check warns about it, at the parameter's line; so is one returning Any, with the warning at its def.
  • Give each class-level default a value of its annotated type (RETRIES: int = 3): it is compiled against the annotation.
  • Return what the framework reads from a hook you override: a bool from is_done(), a ScenarioResult or None from a condition's check(), a dict[int, float] from initial_speeds_mps(), None from setup() and an action's execute() (What is checked).
  • Test an Optional for None before using it: a float | None config field, goal_pose, find_actor_by_role_name(...), and CARLA's Optional results (get_waypoint(...), get_actors().find(...), world.get_actor(...), actor.parent).
  • Read **kwargs by name with kw.get(), and test *args, like any tuple, with len() (#266). Codon makes **kwargs a NamedTuple of the keywords passed, not a dict, and *args a Tuple, and gives no tuple a truth value (#278). Codon refuses this valid Python, and the message says what to write instead:
Python Codon's error Write instead for k, v in kw.items(): (.keys(), .values(), for k in kw, len(kw)) 'NamedTuple[a=float]' object has no attribute 'items' kw.get("a", default) for each name, or keyword parameters (def f(*, a: float = 1.0)) if args: / x if args else y, or if window: of any tuple 'Tuple[float,float]' object has no attribute '__bool__' if len(args) > 0: (if len(window) > 0:)

kw["speed"] and "speed" in kw compile for a keyword the call passes; kw.get("speed", 1.0) compiles whether it does or not. A helper taking **kwargs or *args that the scenario calls and that reads them by key or position is compiled through its callers' calls, so it is checked with the keywords and values they pass (What is checked). - Give your own helper an Optional of the class it gets, not of its base. Codon 0.19 does not convert an Optional of a subclass to an Optional of its base (#278). A helper def gap(actor: carla.Actor | None) refuses an Optional[carla.Vehicle], and a plain carla.Vehicle too, which Codon wraps in an Optional first ('Optional[Vehicle]' does not match expected type 'Optional[Actor]'). Python accepts both. A parameter of carla.Actor alone takes a carla.Vehicle, and the framework's own Optional[carla.Actor] parameters take either (What is checked). Annotate the helper with the subclass (carla.Vehicle | None), or test for None before the call and pass the unwrapped value to a carla.Actor parameter. - Build an object of a class you hold in an Optional, when the class has subclasses and nothing else builds one. Codon 0.19 checks x: X | None = None (or a parameter defaulting to None) of such a class, then generates code that LLVM refuses ("LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type 'ptr'"), when the program builds no X nor any subclass of it, or defines a subclass after Codon compiled X (#263). The model builds its own such classes once, after their subclasses: BaseCondition, BaseAction and lanelet2's ConstLanelet, ConstLineString2d, ConstLineString3d, ConstPoint3d and RegulatoryElement (the others are built by the scenario check anyway). So a scenario that builds actions but no condition compiles, though each action's condition = None is an Optional[BaseCondition], whether it registers the actions or keeps them in a list or dict of BaseAction. A class of your own, or your subclass of a framework class that nothing builds (class MyResult(ScenarioResult)), can still meet it; the check then names the class and what to do, at the class line of it or of its subclass, and keeps no verdict, as for any crash:

scenario.py:73: error: Codon 0.19 generated code it cannot compile for autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.ScenarioResult, a class with subclasses: a bug of Codon's rather than an error of the program (#263). It does so for an Optional of such a class (`x: ScenarioResult | None = None`, a parameter that defaults to None) when the program builds no object of the class or of a subclass, or defines a subclass after Codon compiled the class. Build a MyResult where setup() reaches it, or hold the value without Optional
    LLVM: error: '%obj' defined with type 'ptr' but expected '{ ptr, ptr }'

Annotations Codon cannot express (Union of two types, Any, Callable, Sequence, type[...]) are dropped from parameters, which become generic: Codon then checks each call with the arguments it is given. The appended calls give a union parameter (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose) each of its members in turn, and a Callable[[A], R] of types Codon can express a value of that signature; Any, object and Callable[..., R] give them nothing to call with, hence the warning.

The checker also rewrites what Codon spells differently: an Enum class (its members become instances with a name and a typed value; a lookup by value, ActionState("completeState"), takes a value of that type and is typed but not resolved to the member; looking a member up by name and iterating over the class work for a scenario's own enum, see Iterating an enum), a class deriving from an exception, a @classmethod (a static method of its class: cls names the class it is defined in), and an annotation naming one of CARLA's integer enumerations (carla.TrafficLightState), which typesafe_carla's Codon library has as a value whose members are int, not as a type: it becomes int.

Two things Python does that Codon 0.19 does not are filled in for you:

  • A subclass that inherits __init__. Codon 0.19 inherits no __init__: it gives a class without one a constructor taking each of its fields, which refused a scenario deriving from another scenario and keeping its constructor ("'config' is an invalid keyword argument for __init__()", #201). The check appends one to such a class, after the module, so no line moves:
@extend
class MyDerivedScenario:
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

It is added only where a base really defines an __init__ (a class of the scenario's modules, its own or one it inherits, or one of the model's, such as BaseScenario's), and never to a dataclass, an Enum or an exception, which are built as before. When the __init__ is a later base's (class MyDerivedScenario(MyMixin, MyScenario), the mixin having none), it is called through that base, MyScenario.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs), as Python does: Codon's super() is the first base's. The base's __init__ still checks every argument: a wrong one is reported at the class line of the subclass, with the call that passed it in the trace:

scenario.py:52:9: error: no function 'MyScenario.__init__' with arguments (Super[MyScenario], EgoConfig, Lanelet2Pose, str)
    during the realization of __init__(self: MyDerivedScenario, ...) [scenario.py:58]

A literal None passed through it is refused, though Python takes it (MyDerivedScenario(ego, pose, None), or config=None): forwarded through *args or **kwargs, it reaches the base's __init__ as an Optional[NoneType], which no Optional[X] parameter takes. Leave the argument to its default, pass a variable declared Optional[X], or give the subclass an __init__ of its own.

  • return None from a function returning Optional[X]. A bare None is Codon's NoneType, so a function whose only return is return None could not be typed ("cannot typecheck 'None'"), and, when nothing else in the program used X (carla.Actor in a scenario), Optional[X] failed in code generation ("value doesn't match function result type 'ptr'", #202). The check makes each return None (and bare return) of the function itself return Optional[X](), the None of its type (a nested function is rewritten for its own annotation), and the appended calls realize X (_acs_value(X)) before they call it. So
def _find_npc(self) -> Optional[carla.Actor]:
    return None

compiles as written, and so does a local found: Optional[carla.Actor] = None returned at the end.

  • Your own dataclasses, enums and named tuples keep what Python gives them (#365), with these limits:
  • A @dataclass compares, orders and hashes as Python's does: the check appends == and != (eq=True, the default), <, <=, > and >= (order=True) and hash() (frozen=True, or unsafe_hash=True) after the module, comparing the fields in order (a dataclass base's first; field(compare=False), ClassVar and InitVar are left out). A method the class defines itself is kept. This holds for a dataclass whose bases are dataclasses of the same module (or none): one deriving from a class the check cannot see the fields of, such as a framework dataclass, gets none, and == on it is refused. eq=False (identity comparison) is not modelled either: write a is b. Python refuses < without order=True and hash() of a non-frozen dataclass, and so does the check, with a hint naming the flag.
  • An IntEnum (also IntFlag, class M(int, Enum)) member compares with its value (M.A == 1), orders against a member or an int (M.A < M.B) and converts with int() and float(). A StrEnum or class M(str, Enum) member compares with its string (M.A == "a") and does nothing more: ordering and int() are refused, as in Python for a plain Enum, a Flag and a (str, Enum). A plain Enum member equals only members (M.A == 1 is False, as in Python). An enum member is not an int or a str otherwise: passing it to an int / str parameter or doing arithmetic on it (M.A + 1) is refused with a hint. Write M.A.value.
  • A class Pt(typing.NamedTuple) is checked as a Codon @tuple class: its fields, defaults and methods, ==, ordering, hash(), iteration and len() work. Codon indexes and unpacks it (p[0], x, y = p) only when all its fields have one type: otherwise read p.x, p.y. It has no _replace(), _asdict(), _fields or _make(): build a new Pt(...). Only the class syntax is covered (not NamedTuple("Pt", [...]) or collections.namedtuple).

docs.title: Python the check rewrites for Codon (#376)
docs.text:
Each of these is valid Python that Codon 0.19 refuses or crashes on. The check rewrites the checked copy of your module (on the same lines; what runs is your code as written), so you write the Python you would anyway. A form the rewrite cannot express is refused at its line, with what to write instead.

You write The check compiles Refused when class MyError(Exception): ... the same with pass for ... {**a, "k": v, **b} (a \| {"k": v} \| b); {**a} is dict(a) the values of the parts have other types (Dict[str, int] and Dict[str, str]) "{:>5}\|{a}".format(1, a=x) on a string literal the f-string f"{1:>5}\|{x}" (a complex argument is bound once by a lambda) *args / **kwargs, a field inside a format spec ({:>{}}), a missing argument, mixed auto and manual numbering, a template that is not a literal (write an f-string) zip(a, b, strict=True) zip(a, b): the check types the loop, it does not run it sorted(xs), xs.sort(), min / max of a class that defines __lt__ only the class gets __gt__ (other < self) and __ge__ (not self < other), which Codon's sort calls the class defines no ordering (use @dataclass(order=True) or key=) @functools.total_ordering the decorator and its import are dropped, and the class gets the comparisons it would add from its __lt__, __le__, __gt__ or __ge__ (and ==, or identity without __eq__) the class is not at module level, or defines none of the four lambda x, k=k: x + k (a default that is not a literal) (lambda k: lambda x: x + k)(k): the default is bound by a call, once, as in Python a class constant read in its own class body (#433): DOUBLE = LIMIT * 2, x: int = SIZE (a dataclass default), def f(self, n=LIMIT), @register(LIMIT) Class.LIMIT (Outer.Inner.LIMIT in a nested class) the constant is annotated and not a single-line literal (LIMIT: int = 2 * 3), it is assigned again later in the body, the class is defined in a function, the read is a NamedTuple field default, or it is an Enum member with a non-literal value

Notes:

  • __ge__ of a class that defines __lt__ only is more than Python gives it (a >= b is a TypeError there): the check accepts it because Codon's sort needs it. It does not change what runs.
  • A rewritten lambda no longer takes the captured parameter: fs[0](1, 5), which passes k, is refused (with a hint naming this). A default after a non-literal one is bound the same way, so positional calls keep their meaning. Use functools.partial where you pass the captured value.
  • Codon's f-strings have no {{ / }}: a literal brace becomes a string joined with +.
  • A class constant read in the class body (#433): Python resolves the name in the class scope, Codon in the module's (name 'LIMIT' is not defined), so the check writes Class.LIMIT. It rewrites exactly what Python resolves there: a name an earlier assignment of the same body bound, read by another statement of the body, a dataclass field default, a method's parameter default or a decorator. A method body, a lambda body and a comprehension (but for its first iterable) do not see the class scope, so a bare LIMIT there is the module's and stays; a nested class sees only its own body; a parameter or comprehension variable named LIMIT shadows nothing at the default, which is read in the class scope. In an Enum a member read by a later statement is its value in Python (B = A makes an alias), so the check writes the literal; any other name of the body is qualified as above.
  • The constant has to be a class attribute in Codon. A name annotated at class level (LIMIT: int = 5, Final[int], ClassVar[int]) is a typed field of the instance, not an attribute of the class, so a read of it cannot be qualified: when its value is a single-line literal the check writes that literal where the name is (n: int = 5; Python reads the same value), and otherwise the read is refused with a hint: write LIMIT: Final = 5 (a bare Final is dropped, leaving a class attribute) or no annotation, or use a module-level constant. A NamedTuple field default cannot read its own class constant either (x: int = LIM is "no module named"): its other statements and methods can.

docs.title: The names of typing a scenario may import
docs.text:
Codon has no typing module of its own beyond a few names, so the check brings a shim (typecheck/codon/typing.codon). A scenario may import these names from typing (#364); test_typing_names keeps this list and the shim in step:

TYPE_CHECKING, Sequence, MutableSequence, Iterable, Collection, Mapping, MutableMapping, AbstractSet, FrozenSet, Any, TypeVar, Protocol, runtime_checkable, Literal, IO, Iterator, Deque, DefaultDict, Counter, Final, Annotated, NoReturn, Type, Sized, Hashable, cast, Optional, List, Dict, Set, Tuple, Callable, Union, ClassVar, Generator, overload

  • Final and Annotated are read as what they wrap (Final[int] and Annotated[int, "m"] are int; a bare Final is dropped). NoReturn, Type, Sized, Hashable, Any and Callable annotations are dropped, so they are not checked.
  • cast(T, x) is x typed as T (as in Python, nothing checks that x is a T); when T cannot be named in Codon (a Callable, a class defined further down) it is x as it is.
  • A class-level Y: Final[int] = 4 stays a typed field, not a class attribute, as any annotated class-level name does; write Y: Final = 4 for a class attribute read as C.Y.
  • Iterator is Codon's generator type, and Deque, DefaultDict and Counter are collections.deque, defaultdict and Counter.
  • Any other name is refused at its import line. Generic and TypedDict cannot be modelled: leave the type parameters of a class or function unannotated (Codon makes it generic over them) instead of subclassing Generic, and write a @dataclass (or a Dict[str, X]) instead of a TypedDict.

docs.title: Python constructs Codon refuses (#379)
docs.text:
Each of these is valid, mypy-clean Python that Codon 0.19 cannot compile and that the check cannot cheaply rewrite. The check refuses it at its line with a hint, and the working spelling is below. What runs is your code as written; only the check needs the other spelling.

You write Codon says Write instead case int(n):, case Pt(x=x, y=y):, case Pt(a, b): (a class pattern with arguments), or case Pt(): of a class of your own name 'n' is not defined, or it reads the pattern as a call of Pt (__init__() missing 1 required positional argument) if isinstance(v, Pt):, then read the attributes (v.x, v.y); case int():, case str(): and the other builtin types compile case {"k": v}:, case {"k": _}:, case {**rest}: (any name or _ inside the mapping) name 'v' is not defined if "k" in d: and read d["k"]; a mapping pattern whose values are literals, values or or-patterns (case {"k": 1 \| 2}:) compiles case [a, *rest]:, case [*_]: unexpected star expression a fixed length (case [a, b]:), or test len(xs) and slice case [a, b] as whole: unexpected indentation match without as and use the name the subject already has def show(h: HasArea) called with a class that has area() but does not derive from the Protocol HasArea 'Sq[float]' does not match expected type 'HasArea' (also List[Sq] against List[HasArea]) derive from it (class Sq(HasArea):), give the classes a common base class, or annotate Union[Sq, Circle]; Codon lists are invariant: annotate a list with the class it holds (list[Sq]) f(*xs) with a list, f(**d) with a dict argument after * must be a tuple, not 'List[int]' / argument after ** must be a named tuple, not 'Dict[str,int]' pass the elements (f(xs[0], xs[1]), f(a=d["a"], b=d["b"])), or make the parameter a list or dict; a tuple (f(*(1, 2))) is accepted

Plain value, or-pattern, guard, sequence (without *) and enum-member (case Mode.A:) patterns compile, as does case int(): of a builtin type.

A Protocol is not structural in the check: Codon compares class names, so a class is a HasArea only if it lists HasArea among its bases. Python runs the same code either way, because a Protocol base is only a marker there.

docs.title: Standard library names Codon lacks
docs.text:
Codon ships its own functools (only partial), itertools and collections, and a name it lacks fails with a bare "cannot import name". The check supplies these (#378); test_stdlib_names keeps this list, the check's additions and the tests in step:

functools.reduce, functools.lru_cache, functools.cache, functools.cached_property, itertools.pairwise, collections.OrderedDict

  • functools.reduce (with or without an initial value) is a function of the model, which the check puts in place of the name.
  • lru_cache (with or without arguments), cache and cached_property are decorators the check drops, as caching changes no type; cached_property becomes a property. Nothing is cached, so f.cache_clear() and f.cache_info() are refused, and so is assigning to a cached_property attribute (self.area = 3 is legal in Python, not on a property). A name the module binds again (a parameter reduce, a def cache) is left alone. The names are handled where the module imports them, not in a function.
  • The initial value of reduce must have the type of the accumulator the function returns: reduce(add, [1.5, 2.5], 0) is refused (write 0.0).
  • itertools.pairwise is added to Codon's itertools, and collections.OrderedDict is a dict, which keeps its insertion order; move_to_end() and popitem(last=...) are not declared, and are refused when called.

These are refused at the import line, with a hint saying what to write instead:

dataclasses.asdict, functools.wraps, contextlib, warnings, json, types, textwrap, traceback, io

  • dataclasses.asdict returns a dict[str, Any]: build the dict from the fields you need. The dataclasses shim declares only dataclass, field and replace.
  • functools.wraps (and any other name of functools, itertools or collections not listed above) is not modelled.
  • contextlib: write a class with __enter__ and __exit__ for contextmanager, and try/except X: pass for suppress. warnings: log with logger.warning. json: read into a @dataclass. types: name the type itself. textwrap: build the string with str methods. traceback: log with logger.exception. io: use a str, or a pathlib.Path opened with open().

docs.title: Iterating an enum
docs.text:
For a scenario's own Enum class (any of Enum, IntEnum, StrEnum, Flag, IntFlag, (str, Enum)), the check rewrites, as Python reads it:

  • for m in Mode and a comprehension over Mode, and *Mode;
  • list(Mode), tuple, set, frozenset, sorted, len, reversed, enumerate, iter, min, max, zip, map and filter (with a function) of Mode;
  • x in Mode and x not in Mode;
  • Mode["A"], a member looked up by name.

Iteration yields the members in definition order. A member whose value repeats an earlier one is an alias, and is skipped, as in Python. Only the bare name of the class is rewritten, so a parameter or local called like the class is left alone, and the enum may be defined in another module of the package.

What does not work (Flag operators and the model enums are tracked in #437):

  • the framework's own model enums (TurnDirection, ...) are not iterable;
  • the class passed as a value, f(Mode), or Mode.__members__: both stay as written, which Codon does not resolve (no function 'List.__init__' with arguments (List[T], type[Mode]) for list(e) in f, and 'Mode' object has no attribute '__members__');
  • sum, any and all of the class, and filter(None, Mode): Codon needs __bool__ or + on the member (sum(int(m) for m in Mode), any(m == x for m in Mode));
  • the operators of a Flag (A | B: unsupported operand type(s) for |);
  • an enum with no member ('Empty' object has no attribute '_acs_members').

docs.title: What the check does not catch
docs.text:
The check compiles the scenario and never runs it, so it says nothing of what a value is at run time (a division by zero, a missing key, an actor that is not spawned yet), and it accepts some code that fails in Python. The known gaps:

  • An Optional unwrapped implicitly, where mypy cannot see it. Codon unwraps an Optional[T] wherever a T is needed (arithmetic, an attribute, an argument), and mypy's pass (#239, What is checked) catches what mypy can type, CARLA's results included (from stubs of typesafe_carla's Codon library, #267). It does not see a value mypy reads as Any: one from a package with no type information (an import it cannot follow, which it ignores, such as lanelet2), a CARLA result whose type the stubs leave Any (an enumeration, carla.command, a pointer, a method whose overloads return different types), or the result of a function with no return annotation. Neither does it check the arguments of a CARLA call: an Optional passed to one is Codon's to unwrap (world.get_actor(maybe_id) compiles).
  • A union of the scenario's own classes used as one of its members. The None check's pass refuses only a union made of the members of one of the framework's (#309, What is checked): a union of classes the scenario defines (a class-level tuple[A | B, ...], held as List[Union[A, B]]) is converted at run time as Codon converts any union, and an un-narrowed use of one member's attribute compiles.
  • A helper with **kwargs or *args that nothing calls and that reads **kwargs by key is not compiled, with a warning: the check has no keyword to call it with (#266). One the scenario calls that reads them is compiled only with the keywords and the number of values its callers pass, and, as a call is known by its name only, not at all when the only calls of its name are another's (d.update(...) for a helper update) or are in a function the check does not compile.
  • A value converted by an annotated assignment. Codon 0.19 converts any value with __bool__ in an annotated assignment: done: bool = "no" compiles, and is True. The check binds hook results strictly (#238) and class-level bool defaults through _expect_bool (#190), but an annotated local of the scenario's own code is converted as written. A local x: bool = some_str is no bool in Python.
  • An int where a float is expected is accepted, in a call and a hook result alike, as Python's typing takes it; not inside a container ([1, 2] for a list[float] is refused).
  • A function the check cannot call (a parameter with no annotation, or one of Any, object, Callable[..., R] or a TypeVar, or a return annotation naming Any) is compiled only where setup() and is_done() reach it, with a warning (What is checked).
  • A hook a class takes from a mixin listed before its framework base (class Gap(CheckMixin, BaseCondition), with check() defined in CheckMixin) is compiled as the mixin's own method, not checked against the hook's return type: define the override in the class itself.
  • A None default is not checked against its annotation: speed: float = None is an Optional[float] to Codon (mypy, in the scenario package's own pre-commit, reports it; the None check reports only its uses).
  • What only a tuple does: a tuple[X, ...] is checked as a List[X], so its hash, its equality with another tuple and its immutability are not checked.
  • bytes is read as str: path.read_bytes() + "text" compiles, and CPython refuses it.
  • A values= that only Codon iterates (register_cover(), OddAttribute, #279). Codon 0.19 cannot tell a class passed as an argument from one of its objects, so an enum member passes where an enum class is meant (values=TurnDirection.LEFT). A frozen dataclass of the framework (a @tuple, so iterable to Codon) passes too, and so does an element type expression never returns.
  • An enum member looked up by value (ActionState("completeState")) is typed, but not resolved to the member. Lookup by name and iteration work for a scenario's own enum, within the limits of Iterating an enum.
  • typesafe_carla's Python-API compatibility shortcuts (a Vehicle method called on a plain Actor) compile, as they do outside its strict mode.
  • A scenario registered with register_scenario_builder() is not checked at all: only its builder knows how it is built.

docs.title: Checking the framework itself
docs.text:
The scenario check trusts the model: it never compiles the framework's own source. The library check does, a module at a time, as each is made to compile:

uv run scenario-check --library                                   # every checked module
uv run scenario-check --library autoware_carla_scenario.kinematics.vector

from autoware_carla_scenario.typecheck import typecheck_library

result = typecheck_library()  # the modules typecheck/library.py lists as checked
assert result.ok, result.format()

test_typecheck_library.py makes the same check in the test suite.

The checked modules get the None check too (#277), as a scenario's modules do: after the compile, mypy runs over every module the run compiled, with the CARLA stubs, and an Optional used without a test for None fails the check at its line. Codon unwraps an Optional in the framework as it does in a scenario, so the compile alone accepted CollisionCondition reading CollisionEvent.other_actor (None for a collision with map geometry) as a carla.Actor, and the sensor callback raised in Python:

conditions/collision.py:158:32: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "Actor | None", variable has type "Actor"): Codon unwraps an Optional implicitly, so test the value for None before this use, or Python fails here when it is None (mypy: assignment)

It adds about 11 seconds to a run with mypy's cache cold, and under a second with it warm, to a compile of about a minute. A verdict kept between runs (below) holds the None check's too: the key already covers what it reads. test_typecheck_none_check.py runs the same None check over CHECKED without Codon, so a machine without a Codon compiler catches it as well.

A run that names modules is a slice of the full run. With the named modules, it compiles from their source the CHECKED modules they import, transitively. It does not follow an import that MODELLED_IMPORTS routes through the model, or one inside an UNCALLED function. It also brings the other modules of a REPLACED_MODELS entry once one of them is in, so that the model re-exports the checked definitions, as it does in the full run. scenario_base, for example, imports register_vehicle_entity from the checked entity.registry, which the model does not declare, and entity._spawn holds the checked GroundProjectionConfig, which the model VehicleEntityConfig must share. The modules it imports are checked as fully as the named ones: their functions and methods are called too, and errors are reported for every compiled module, not only the named ones. An error in a module the named one imports is an error the full run reports as well, and it would stop the named module from compiling anyway. Hiding it would only make the run fail without a reason. The result's title gives both counts (1 checked modules, 44 more they import for scenario_base, at the time of writing). Run without names, the check compiles exactly CHECKED, as before. Every checked module passes on its own.

The check's driver imports the model before any checked module, whichever module it names first. The model reaches the checked coordinate.frames through _poses.codon, and a run that started at coordinate.frames would reach the model, and come back to coordinate.frames, before that module defines anything.

docs.title: The manifest: typecheck/library.py
docs.text:
CHECKED lists the modules compiled from their source; EXCLUDED maps every other module to the reason it is not. "not yet checked (#45)" marks a module nobody has made compile yet; any other reason names what keeps a module out ("imports omegaconf, hydra": a package or a standard module Codon cannot compile). numpy is not one: Codon ships its own, and a module's numpy calls compile. Every module of the package except typecheck/ is in exactly one of the two, which the test suite checks, so a new module needs an entry.

UNCALLED names the few functions and methods of a checked module the check leaves out (module.Class.method, or module._helper for a protected one), each with its reason: one whose job Codon cannot express, in a module that otherwise compiles. Today that is what builds a condition's details (get_details(), to_summary_dict(), to_dict(): a dict[str, Any] of mixed value types) and what serialises them (ScenarioResult.to_json(), with json), and what reads the authoring package's pydantic specs, typed Any (signals.build_controllers()). Codon compiles a function only when something calls it, so neither its body nor an import made inside it is compiled: a module that needs a standard module Codon lacks for one function imports it inside that function (import json in to_json()) and lists the function here. A test checks that every entry names a function or method of a checked module.

To check one more module:

  1. Move its entry from EXCLUDED to CHECKED.
  2. Run uv run scenario-check --library and fix what it reports, in the module. Only annotations and Codon-friendly rewrites: the module must behave exactly as it did.
  3. Run uv run pytest autoware_carla_scenario/test/carla_scenario/test_typecheck_library.py.
