docs.text:
Every module now has an entry other than "not yet checked (#45)". 196 of the package's 288 modules (68%; about 47,300 of 84,200 lines) are CHECKED: the kinematics, the coordinate frames and poses, the conversions between Lanelet2, OpenDRIVE and CARLA world poses (coordinate.transform), the stop lines read off a Lanelet2 map (utils.stop_line, coordinate.stop_line) and the lane arithmetic of a relative lane pose (trajectory.relative_lane), the map manager that loads the Lanelet2 map and the OpenDRIVE road network (coordinate.map_manager) and the sweeper's lighter loader of the Lanelet2 map (sweeper.map_loader), with the projection and origin both read a map with (coordinate.projection; not how it reads map_projector_info.yaml, whose YAML values are of any type, nor how it moves a Local map's points to their local_x/local_y tags), what places a trajectory's vertices in CARLA world coordinates (trajectory.resolve), the sweeper's lanelet constraints and parameter bindings (sweeper.constraints, sweeper.bindings) and the route's map questions, frame, poses and search (route.geometry, route.frame, route.positions, route.search), all against the lanelet2 model, the condition base and every condition, the action base with the environment, follow-trajectory, traffic-signal, signal-controller, lane-change, routing, set-speed, turn and walk-straight actions, the stalled object (actions.stalled_object) and the background-traffic source and sink (actions.background_traffic), the logical scenario's route search and matches (route.model) and the scenario's route (route.active), the signals package (the signal controllers and their registry), the ego, NPC vehicle and pedestrian entities, the base of the externally driven egos (entity.externally_driven), the ego that takes its mission over the bridge (entity.bridged_ego) and the Autoware ego on it (entity.autoware_entity), the ego driven by ROS 2 nodes over DDS (entity.ros2_entity) with its configs, commands, arbitration and transport interface (ros2, ros2.config, ros2.commands, ros2.transport), the entity registry and the policy warm-up with the Chaos powertrain model, BaseScenario, the scenario runner's run loop and the queue that runs scenarios one after another (scenario_runner, scenario_queue), the UI's runner, which runs them in a subprocess on a thread (ui.runner, over a model of the pydantic ui.models), the traffic backend interface and its run context with the TrafficManager backend and the SUMO backend's options, the map source URIs and what resolves them to files on disk (maps.resolver, with the repository listing of maps.catalogue, the map config's paths of maps.config and the OpenDRIVE taken from CARLA by maps.opendrive), what an exported scenario package pins the framework to and how it runs uv (authoring.framework_pin, authoring.uv_tool), the CARLA server manager (server), the markers an ego entity hands the runner for the trajectory log (debug_markers), the Autoware launcher that runs a stack as a process group (autoware_stack.launcher), the scenario_bridge node's command and Python root beside it (autoware_stack.bridge_node) and the one that runs a workspace in its dev container with Docker (autoware_stack.docker, over a model of autoware_stack.devcontainer, which reads JSON and YAML), the Autoware bridge interface and its fake, the trajectory model, the adversity math, location gate, observation, commands and triggers (adversity, NADE and its avoidance included, the actions' _adversarial_execution, adversarial and adversarial_traffic, conditions.adversity_feasible), the measures and the metrics, the ODD unit names (odd.unit_names), the ODD's probes, which read its attributes off the world and, for those the Lanelet2 map decides, off a lanelet (odd.probes), the placement of a road user so a scenario measure reads a given value (placement), the planning of a scenario's route on the Lanelet2 map that the ODD's route check starts from (odd.route_plan), the CARLA-only helpers, the traffic-light lookups included, and the scenario configs (scenario_config, examples.configs), the camera and LiDAR sensors (sensor), the six example scenarios, and the external driver's configs and client interface, trajectory follower and observations (driver.base, driver.control, driver.observation, over driver.geometry), and the autoware_bridge, autoware_stack, entity, driver, maps and coverage packages themselves, whose __init__ re-exports what is not checked through models of it (see A class a checked package only re-exports below). 95 functions and methods of those modules are UNCALLED (21 of them protected helpers, see What is compiled below): most of them a condition's get_details() or a backend's describe(), what takes a traffic backend's options node (Mapping[str, Any]), what reads a route search, a match, a constraint or a binding from YAML values of any type (Range.parse(), parse_route_search(), RouteMatch.from_config(), parse_constraint(), parse_binding()), the [tool.uv.sources] entry of a framework pin, a dict of str and bool values (Pin.uv_source()), the two members of BaseScenario built on the ego's class (create_ego(), which instantiates ego_type, a type[EgoVehicle]) or on cover expressions of any value (register_cover()), the run-time wrapper of TrajectoryVertex.__init__ (_refusing_vertex_times), the road-marking pattern of the stop lines, which returns a refers parameter (any of lanelet2's primitives) as a line string (utils.stop_line._road_marking_stop_lines()), what moves a Local map's points to their local_x/local_y tags and rebuilds the map, which the lanelet2 model has no setters for (coordinate.projection._read_local_tags()), signals.build_controllers(), which reads the authoring package's pydantic specs, what builds the scenario_bridge node's command from its ROS parameters (bridge_ros_args(), bridge_command(): a Mapping[str, Any] of bool, int, float and str values; Codon 0.19 fails on a Union in a parameter annotation, union already sealed, so the checker drops one and the check has nothing to call with), what the runner does with json or a condition's details (writing the result and its environment, _write_result(); collecting the condition statuses, _collect_condition_statuses()), the queue's pytest fixture (ScenarioQueue.as_fixture()), maps.config.resolve_map_paths(), which reads the map config node of any shape (Any), the driver and ROS 2 configs' from_mapping() (a Hydra node, Mapping[str, Any]), what builds the ROS 2 ego's published cameras (entity.ros2_entity._publishing_camera(), which imports ros2.camera inside it), encode_frame_jpeg() (cv2), and protected helpers of the same kinds: what reads a map setting, a route search's segment, a signal group or phase, or a TrajectoryVertex call's arguments, each of any type (Any), walks or binds a sweeper constraint of any kind, builds a condition's status (its details), or takes the list a plain tick callback goes into (BaseScenario._register_tick(), a List[Callable[[carla.World], None]], which the check has no value of). The 92 EXCLUDED modules fall in four groups. Many fit more than one (about 69 import what Codon cannot compile, 29 build on an excluded module and 20 hold values Codon has no type for), so each is counted once, in the first group that fits it:

  • 69 import what Codon cannot compile: pyxodr, pydantic, pickle, lxml, grpc, omegaconf and hydra, yaml, openodd (a Rust extension), cyclonedds (ros2.cyclone and ros2.messages, the ROS 2 ego's DDS transport and its message types), or a standard module Codon lacks (json, inspect, concurrent.futures, importlib beyond importlib.metadata, or more of os, pathlib, shutil, signal, subprocess, tempfile, threading, dataclasses, importlib.metadata or urllib.parse than their shims declare), at module level or inside a function the check calls. This is the tooling around a run (the editor, the UI, authoring, the sweeper's expansion, Hydra sweeper and map loader, the map caches (the map repositories, the Lanelet2 z offset and the pyxodr road network), the Autoware stack's dev container, the record of a run's environment, the SLURM launcher's submitting side, its worker and its manifest, the batch summary they share, and the Rerun recordings of a run's logs), the ODD and coverage modules that wrap openodd, and the rest of what reads Lanelet2. A reason names pathlib only where the module uses more of it than the shim declares, and the other shimmed modules likewise; test_typecheck_library.py holds every reason to that.
  • 19 build on an excluded module, and import nothing Codon lacks themselves: they import a module that is neither checked nor modelled, or names that its package's model does not declare. Among them are the packages that re-export one (authoring, odd, sweeper, examples, scaffold, slurm), slurm.collect, the authoring compiler, builders and validator, odd.route, the coverage half of the route check (names of odd.model and coverage.items that the odd and coverage models do not declare, such as OddDefinition.evaluate() and value_label(); it also holds each lanelet's attribute values, dict[str, Any], which it hands to openodd, and finds a probe's on_lanelet reader on any callable) and traffic.registry (the registry, in its plugin loader); 4 of the 19 also hold values Codon has no type for.
  • 3 hold values Codon has no type for, and nothing else keeps them out: Any (trajectory.authoring, authoring.registry's field defaults), or a class as a value (utils.config, which traffic.config, traffic.fidelity and traffic.sumo.config import only in their uncalled from_mapping()).
  • 1 has a callback the check cannot type: ros2.camera, whose camera hands each frame back to the ROS 2 ego from a CARLA sensor thread through CarlaCameraSensor's listen callback.

The scenario check is not limited by this: it compiles every scenario against the model. The model does not declare the whole public API: what test_typecheck_model.py guarantees is that every public name of a modelled module, and every public method, property and class attribute of a class the model declares, is either declared or listed with the reason it is left out in typecheck/not_modelled.py (NOT_MODELLED, NOT_MODELLED_MEMBERS), and the check refuses a use of a listed one with that reason (#249, #265). Attributes a class only annotates (set on the instance) are outside that guarantee.

docs.title: What is compiled
docs.text:
Codon checks a function only when something calls it, so the check appends a function to each checked module that calls every function and every method of every class (constructors, static and class methods, properties and their setters, dunder methods, protected _ ones and those of _ classes included) with a value of each parameter's annotated type:

def _acs_library_check():
    normalize_angle_deg(_acs_value(float))
    Vector3(_acs_value(float), _acs_value(float), _acs_value(float))
    _acs_value(Vector3).dot(_acs_value(Vector3))

_acs_value(T) is a T Codon cannot tell from a real one; nothing compiled is ever run. A parameter annotated with a union (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose, Union[BaseAction, Callable[[carla.World], None]], or an Optional of one, Optional[Union[EntityRole, str]]) is called once with each member, so the body is checked for every type it accepts. A parameter with no annotation, or one Codon cannot express (Any, object, Callable[..., R], Callable[[Any], Any], ...), gives the check nothing to call with and is reported as a problem of the module, at its line: annotate it with the type its callers pass. The exceptions are other: object in __eq__ and __ne__, which Python requires, called with the class itself, and a parameter Codon cannot express that has a default: a function whose every such parameter has one is called only leaving the defaults out (Defaults are compiled too, below), so its body is compiled with them (#199). A Callable whose argument and result types Codon can express (Callable[[carla.World], Optional[float]], a dataclass field too, or an Optional of one) is called with a value of Codon's Callable type, which a function of that signature converts to. One with a union among its argument types (Callable[[Optional[Union[EntityRole, str]]], CarlaWorldPose], the reference lookup of trajectory.resolve) is no type Codon 0.19 can hold: it crashes on it ("union already sealed"). Such a parameter is called with _acs_Returning[R, N] (_tc.codon), a callable that takes N arguments (as many as the Callable does) of any type and returns an R, so the body is compiled with the number of arguments it passes checked, their types unchecked, and with what it gets back checked.

A *args: T is given one T (run_uv(cwd, *args: str, ...) is called with one str), so the body is compiled for it; one with no annotation, or of object or Any (__exit__(self, *args: object)), is given nothing.

A method with keyword-only parameters or **kwargs is called through its class (TrafficBackend.start(_acs_value(TrafficBackend), ..., skip_actor_ids=...)): Codon 0.19 calls a method a subclass may override through a dispatch thunk, which takes neither a keyword argument nor **kwargs, and the call through the class checks the same body.

Defaults are compiled too (#183). The calls above pass every argument, so no default was ever compiled: find_nearest_traffic_light(..., max_distance: float = "far") passed the check. A function or method with a defaulted parameter is now called once more, with only the arguments that have no default, each of its first type:

    find_nearest_traffic_light(_acs_value(carla.World), _acs_value(Lanelet2Pose))
    AutowareBridge.configure(_acs_value(AutowareBridge), _acs_value(BridgePose), _acs_value(BridgePose))

A method is called through its class (AutowareBridge.configure(...), not _acs_value(AutowareBridge).configure(...)): a dispatch thunk fills in no default, and through it AutowareBridge.configure() and FakeAutowareBridge.configure() do not compile. A *args: T is still given one T (run_uv(cwd, *args: str, timeout: int, env=None) with one str and timeout), so the positional parameters before it are passed, defaulted or not: without it run_uv() does not compile. A function with no default gets no such call. An error in a default is reported at the call, which names it (<library check: find_nearest_traffic_light(world: carla.World, location: Lanelet2Pose), with the default ofmax_distance>: error: 'str' does not match expected type 'float').

That was 169 calls more, beside the 1525 others (1694 in all), when it came in. Measured before any fix, 13 of them failed, and all 13 are fixed by the transform, with no change to a module:

  • 11 had a () default on a Sequence[X] or Collection[X] parameter (RoutingAction.__init__'s waypoints, set_mission() / route_to() of BridgeHandshake and BridgedEgoEntity, EgoVehicle.route_to(), the skip_actor_ids of the three traffic backends' start(), utils.vehicles.hold_vehicles_still() and scenario_runner._hold_vehicles_still()). The parameter's annotation is dropped, so the () made it Codon's empty tuple ("'Tuple' does not match expected type 'List[Lanelet2Pose]'"). The transform makes such a default List[X](), as it does a dataclass's field(default=()).
  • 2 had a None default on an Optional parameter whose annotation the transform drops: EgoConfig.__init__'s waypoint_poses: Optional[Sequence[Lanelet2Pose]], and the Callable parameters of trajectory.resolve.resolve_trajectory(). None alone is Codon's NoneType, which has no elements and no call, and a body that tests it for None first is compiled with it all the same. The transform makes such a default the None of the Optional the library check calls with: Optional[List[Lanelet2Pose]](), Optional[Callable[[float, float], Optional[float]]](), and for a Callable with a union among its arguments Optional[_acs_Returning[CarlaWorldPose, 1]]() (the transform's prelude imports _acs_Returning; the check's own function does not import it again, which Codon 0.19 cannot type: "cannot typecheck").

So are the field defaults of a dataclass (#188). The check drops @dataclass, and Codon gives the class a constructor that takes each field, with its default; every constructor call above passes every field, so no field default was compiled: stop_timeout_s: float = "far" on CommandAutowareLauncher passed the check. A dataclass with a defaulted field is now constructed once more, with only the fields that have no default, each of its first type:

    DockerAutowareConfig(_acs_value(Path), _acs_value(Sequence[str]))
    DriverClientConfig()

A field without a default after one with (a field(kw_only=True)) is passed by keyword. A field with no default of its own (field(), or field(init=False), which the constructor leaves out anyway) is not one with a default, and neither is a field "defaulted" to OmegaConf's mandatory-value marker (spawn_lanelet_id: int = MISSING, the string "???"): the marker is no value of the field but a placeholder for one the config must supply, so the call passes the field, and the marker is not compiled against the field's type. Nothing enforces that in Python: reading the field from Hydra's config raises MissingMandatoryValue, but OmegaConf.to_container() returns "???" for it, and a dataclass built without it (NpcVehicleConfig()) holds the string, which the check does not see. A field the call leaves out because its annotation names Any (A dataclass field may hold a union or a free-form mapping, below) is left out of this call too. An error is reported at the call, which names the defaults it leaves out (<library check: CommandAutowareLauncher.__init__(argv: Sequence[str]), with the default ofenv,log_dir,stop_timeout_s>: error: 'str' does not match expected type 'float').

That is 96 calls more, beside the 1694 others (1790 in all, 265 of them leaving defaults out), at the time of writing. Measured before any fix, 5 of the 96 failed, at the first error of each. Those 5 classes have 10 defaults Codon refused, of four causes; all are fixed in the check, with no change to a module and nothing UNCALLED (9 by the transform, whose output changes at those 9 defaults alone, and 1 by the call):

  • 3 had a tuple display default on a Sequence[X] or tuple[X, ...] field (DockerAutowareConfig.colcon_args, DriverClientConfig.cameras and map_formats). The field is declared as a List[X] (the typing shim's Sequence is List), and the display is a fixed-length Codon tuple ("'Tuple[str,str,str]' does not match expected type 'List[str]'"). The transform makes it List[X]([...]), a list of the field's element type, replacing only the brackets, so the elements are rewritten as anywhere else.
  • 4 had a plain () default on such a field (DockerAutowareConfig.ros_domain_ids and docker_args, DriverClientConfig.lidars, PlannedRoute.via), which only a field(default=()) of a tuple[X, ...] was typed for. The transform makes it List[X](), written directly or through field(default=()), for a Sequence[X] as for a tuple[X, ...].
  • 2 had field(default_factory=dict) on a Mapping[str, str] field (env of DockerAutowareConfig and of CommandAutowareLauncher): the factory is typed only for a dict[K, V] field, so it was a bare {}, a dict of None ("'Dict[NoneType,NoneType]' does not match expected type 'Dict[str,str]'"). The transform makes a list, dict or set factory of an abstract collection the concrete one the typing shim maps it onto, of the field's types (Dict[str, str]()).
  • 1 was the OmegaConf marker on an int field (NpcVehicleConfig.spawn_lanelet_id: int = MISSING, "'str' does not match expected type 'int'"), which the call now passes, as above.

So are class-level defaults (#190). On a class with a constructor, its own or a base's, Codon makes a class-level x: T = v a field and drops v: no call compiles it, and BackendDriven._tm_port: int = "x", BaseScenario.STABILIZE_TICKS: int = "a" and AutowareEgoEntity.stack_name: str = 1 passed the check. The check's function now assigns each such default to a local of its type, which compiles the value against the annotation:

    _acs_cls_default_10: int = DEFAULT_TM_PORT
    _acs_cls_default_13: bool = _expect_bool(True)

Each local is named after its line in the function, and an error is reported at it, labelled with the member (<library check: class-level default of BackendDriven._tm_port>: error: 'int' does not match expected type 'str'; Codon names the two types the other way round in an annotated assignment). A bool default goes through _expect_bool() (_tc.codon): Codon converts any value assigned to a bool local with its __bool__, so ready: bool = "x" would compile, and a call converts nothing. A default written without an annotation, overriding one a base declares (REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT = True on FollowTrajectoryAction, whose base declares REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT: ClassVar[bool] = False), is checked against the base's annotation, a ClassVar[T]'s T; the base is found by name among the classes of its module and the other checked modules, depth first. Left out:

  • the defaults of a dataclass, compiled by the constructor call that leaves them out (above), and the members of an enum, which are its values;
  • a ClassVar, which Codon keeps as a class variable, with its value;
  • every default of a class that has no __init__, its own or a base's, and that its module's top level constructs with no argument (_CACHE = _Cache() in measures): Codon's generated constructor takes each field with its default, and that call compiles them already (an error is reported at the call);
  • a default without an annotation that no base declares (a base outside the checked modules), a dunder (__slots__), and one over a bare ClassVar;
  • an annotation Codon cannot express or naming a TypeVar, and a value or annotation naming anything else the class body binds (TWICE: float = LIMIT * 2; a member unpacked, LOW, HIGH = 0.0, 1.0; a method; a nested class), which at the function's scope names something else, or nothing.

That is 22 defaults, at the time of writing: 20 annotated ones, in 10 classes (BaseScenario, the five ego entities, TurnAction, CollisionCondition, DrivenEntity and BackendDriven), and the 2 unannotated overrides of BaseAction.REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT (FollowTrajectoryAction, _BackendAction). Of the 34 non-ClassVar class-level defaults outside dataclasses and enums, the other 14 are those of measures' _Cache, _Lines and _FrameMemo, which the module constructs; the 7 ClassVars are left out. None failed when it came in.

So are the values a function returns as a tuple[X, ...] (#191). Codon's tuples have a fixed length, and the transform dropped such a return annotation, so nothing checked what the function returns: signals.registry.registered_signal_controllers() returning 1 passed the check. A class-level tuple[X, ...] is a List[X], and tuple(x) of a list is one, so the transform now writes the return annotation as List[X] (Optional[List[X]], dict[str, List[X]] inside another type), and the error is reported at the return. It stays dropped when it names an abstract collection (a parameter's is dropped, so the function may return it as it got it), a class defined further down the module or a TypeVar, and so does a Union, Any or Callable return (a Callable return kept fails for a nested function). That is 10 return annotations, in 6 modules, at the time of writing: actions.routing, maps.resolver, route.model, signals.registry, 3 in ros2.config and 3 in signals.controller (one of them dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]). None failed when it came in.

Protected functions and methods are called too (#175). A _ method is often a hook a subclass or another module uses: six example scenarios call BaseScenario._setup_ego_spawn(), and the model's BaseScenario is what a scenario compiles against, so before the driver called it, nothing compiled its real body, and an error injected into it passed the check. The check now calls every _ function of a checked module and every _ method of its public classes, as it calls a public one: about 340 of them, beside about 920 public ones. Measured before any fix, 25 of them failed: 15 had a parameter the check cannot call with, 8 a bare np.ndarray parameter, and _setup_ego_spawn() and scenario_runner._build_condition_status() did not compile. 12 were fixed in the module (shape-typed arrays, an annotated local, an lxml element type for coordinate.transform._cubic(), and the driver taking Optional[Union[A, B]]), and 13 are UNCALLED, each with the reason, most of them because they take Any and only an UNCALLED function calls them.

The methods of _ classes are called too (#182). A _ class is a module's own helper, and was left to be compiled through what uses it, but what uses it does not always compile it. Of the 42 methods of the 20 _ classes of the checked modules, an error injected into each found 4 that nothing compiled: _Never.__init__ and _BackendAction.__init__ (actions.background_traffic), reached only from constructors that are UNCALLED; _BackendAction.set_traffic_backend(), which BaseScenario._hand_backend_to() calls behind a hasattr() on a BaseAction, which Codon decides statically as false; and route.search._Search.__post_init__(), which Codon's constructor does not call. The check now calls them as it calls a public class's: 53 calls (for the 48 methods of the 21 _ classes there are since #180), beside about 1470 others, none with a parameter the check cannot call with. Measured before any fix, 3 of the first 47 failed, and all 3 were fixed in the module: _ScenarioClock declares the _world and _simulated_start it assigns on self, and _BackendAction.__init__ branches into a BaseCondition local instead of choosing between until and _Never() with a conditional expression, which Codon 0.19 cannot type. Each of the 4 now reports an injected error. Two things are left out:

  • a module's dunders (PEP 562's __getattr__), which are Python's hooks, not the module's code; a class's (__eq__, __enter__) are called, as before;
  • what UNCALLED names, as for a public function.

A protected member that calls an UNCALLED one calls it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, as a public one does (see A call into a module Codon cannot compile, from a function it must below). _setup_ego_spawn() needs no such branch: the register_route_to_goal() it ends with is checked (#174).

A constructor is compiled with the defaults of what Codon cannot express (#199). BaseScenario.__init__ takes the ego's class (ego_type: type[EgoVehicle] | None = None), and Codon cannot hold a class as a value, so the whole constructor was UNCALLED, though only one line stores it: its other ~25 lines were compiled nowhere (the example scenarios compile against the model's BaseScenario), and an injected self._tm_port = "x" passed every run. A function some of whose parameters Codon cannot express, each with a default, is now called once, leaving out every defaulted argument, instead of being a problem:

    BaseScenario(_acs_value(EgoConfig))

and the one line that stores the class is under if not TYPE_CHECKING:, which Python runs and Codon does not (ego_type stays declared at class level, so ego_requires_goal still reads it). The error is reported at its line, through the call that leaves the defaults out (<library check: BaseScenario.__init__(ego_config: EgoConfig), with the default ofspawn_pose,ground_projection,random_seed,ego_type,ego_entity>). A parameter Codon cannot express with no default is a problem as before, and so is a defaulted one that call would still pass (one before a *args: T, which is given one T). ConditionStatus.__init__ (its details: dict[str, Any]) and TrafficConfig.__init__ (a backend's options, dict[str, Any]) are compiled the same way, with no UNCALLED entry, so a wrong default of one of their other parameters is reported (#217).

Property setters are called too (#200). Codon compiles an @x.setter only where something assigns the property, so an error injected into the setter of ScenarioRunner.xodr_path passed a run of scenario_runner alone: only the full run found it, through ScenarioQueue.start(). The check now assigns each property that has a setter, once with each member of the annotation of the value it takes:

    _acs_value(BaseScenario).goal_pose = _acs_value(Optional[Lanelet2Pose])
    _acs_value(ScenarioRunner).xodr_path = _acs_value(Optional[Path])

An error is reported at its line, through <library check: ScenarioRunner.xodr_path (setter)>. That is 3 assignments, for the 3 setters of 2 modules (scenario_base and scenario_runner), at the time of writing; none failed when it came in. A deleter is not called. The scenario check appends the same calls to a scenario's own modules (#197), so a setter of a scenario nothing assigns is compiled too.

docs.title: Checked modules and the model
docs.text:
The checked modules are compiled next to the same model the scenario check uses. Every import of the framework in a checked module is pointed at what stands in for it in the check's workspace:

  • another checked module: its own (rewritten) source;
  • any other module: its model, the codon/autoware_carla_scenario/ module of the public package it belongs to (coordinate.poses is modelled by coordinate.codon), or, for a module of a package that is itself checked, a model of that module alone (utils/traffic_light.codon, autoware_bridge/grpc_server.codon, driver/egodriver_client.codon, maps/cache.codon, autoware_stack/devcontainer.codon, ros2/cyclone.codon), or, for a module of the top-level package, a model of that module (carla_install.codon, for server, declares installed_executable(); trajectory_recorder.codon, for scenario_runner, the TrajectoryRecorder it starts, records and closes, whose JSON lines hold values of mixed types; environment.codon, for scenario_runner, capture() and the id of the RunEnvironment it returns). A module with no model (utils.config) cannot be imported by a checked module until it is checked itself.

Each checked module gets the __file__ Python sets on it (its source's path, a str), which Codon 0.19 does not, appended after the calls of the check so no line moves: autoware_stack.bridge_node finds the installed autoware_bridge package with from ..autoware_bridge import __file__. Codon has no module object, so from .. import autoware_bridge and autoware_bridge.__file__ do not compile.

Two checked modules that import each other can each need the other's types the moment Codon reads it: BaseScenario declares _measures: dict[str, Measure] at class level, and measures declares the running scenario (_MEASURED: dict[str, Optional[BaseScenario]]) as a global, so neither can be read first. MODELLED_IMPORTS in typecheck/library.py breaks such a cycle: the module it names (measures, entity.ego) imports the other (scenario_base) through its model, as it did before that one was checked. Its types are the model's, which never meet the checked module's. The egos derived from EgoVehicle (entity.bridged_ego, entity.autoware_entity) do not override EgoVehicle.spawn(), so they never name EgoConfig and need no entry: Codon 0.19 cannot call super().spawn() through an intermediate class ("'EgoVehicle' does not match expected type" in its dispatch thunk), and an override that repeated the spawn instead would take scenario_base through the model as entity.ego does. Through the checked scenario_base, a run with an example scenario in it failed in Codon 0.19's code generation (LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type '{ ptr, ptr }', in opt_ref_new of the model's BaseScenario).

A model module that stands in for unchecked code declares only what the checked modules and scenarios use of it. coordinate.codon still declares, of coordinate.projection, the map_origin(), resolve_projector() and _parse_geo_reference() that coordinate.map_manager and sweeper.map_loader import, though the library check now compiles all three from their source. Its MapManager is now the scenario check's alone: the library check compiles map_manager.py from its source, which every checked module imports, and nothing of the model takes or returns a MapManager, so it needs no REPLACED_MODELS entry.

A checked module is compiled under a name of its own (_acs_lib.autoware_carla_scenario__coordinate__frames), since Codon reads the workspace's packages only from .codon files and names a file in its errors by its base name alone; errors are reported at the line of the real source file. A type a checked module defines is not the type the model declares under the same name, so a checked module cannot hand its own value to a model function that wants the model's: check modules bottom-up, before the modules that use them.

Where the model's functions take the types a checked module defines (the poses, which to_opendrive takes and returns), the model's own declarations of them live in a model module of their own (_poses.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS in typecheck/library.py names with the modules it models. Once those are all checked, the library check compiles that model module as a re-export of their definitions, so the model and the checked modules share one Lanelet2Pose. A name the model declares that none of the checked modules defines is reported.

docs.title: Conditions: the checked base and the model
docs.text:
conditions.base is checked, so the checked conditions derive from the real BaseCondition (_acs_lib.autoware_carla_scenario__conditions__base), not from the model's. The two are different types that never meet:

  • the scenario check compiles a scenario against the model only; no checked module is in its workspace, and the model's BaseCondition, _expect_condition and _acs_list (which recognises a condition by the model-only _acs_condition marker) are unchanged;
  • the library check compiles the checked conditions against the checked base. A checked module that hands a condition to a model function (an unchecked action) cannot do so until that module is checked too (scenario_base is checked, and imports BaseCondition from conditions.base for that); _acs_list gives a list display of checked conditions the type of its first element (_acs_base leaves a checked condition in a dict display as it is), so a display mixing two checked condition classes waits for the same.

BaseCondition.__init_subclass__, which wraps every subclass's check() to record its last result for the UI, is in UNCALLED: the check sees each check() as written.

actions.base is checked the same way: a checked action takes the checked BaseCondition, so it imports it from conditions.base rather than from the conditions package, which the model stands in for until it is checked. Its BaseAction and ActionState are again not the model's, so conditions.action_state watches checked actions. An action that hands its base a condition of its own making imports that condition from its checked module too (SetSpeedAction's default SpeedCondition from conditions.composition.speed); one whose module is not checked waits for it.

docs.title: Making a module compile
docs.text:
What Codon 0.19 needs that Python does not, beyond the rewrites above:

  • Annotate what the check calls: every parameter of a function or method it calls, protected (_) ones included, with a type Codon can express. Spell a union out (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose) rather than through an alias (AnyPose); a union with object or Any in it gives nothing to call with.
  • A default must have the parameter's type (#183): the check compiles each function once with its defaults. A () default of a sequence parameter is checked as an empty List[X], so X must be a type Codon can express and name there: a class defined further down the module is not (the () is left as it is, and fails). A None default of a dropped Optional is typed only for a sequence or a Callable the check can call with; Optional[Callable[..., R]] and Optional[Mapping[K, V]] stay a bare None, so a body that uses them past an is None test fails. A tuple display default (= ("a", "b")) of a sequence parameter is checked as a list of its elements, List[X](["a", "b"]), as a dataclass field's is (#188); a fixed-length Codon tuple is no List[X]. An empty [] / {} default of a list[X] / dict[K, V] parameter (or [] of a sequence) is checked as an empty one of that type; Codon would make it a list of None. A None default is not checked against its annotation: Codon makes speed: float = None an Optional[float], which passes (mypy, in pre-commit, reports it).
  • Declare attributes on any class in a hierarchy (exceptions included) and on a class with __slots__, at class level (_value: str).
  • A class-level default is compiled as written (#190): the library check assigns it to a local of its annotation in its own function, which the transform does not rewrite. So a default the transform would rewrite in a dataclass (a tuple display or () of a tuple[X, ...] member, frozenset()) is reported: assign such a value in __init__ instead. A default naming another member of the class (TWICE: float = LIMIT * 2), or anything else its body binds, is not checked, as at the function's scope the name is not the member; neither is a None default, which Codon makes an Optional of any annotation (x: float = None compiles). An override without an annotation (REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT = True) is checked against its base's annotation only when the base is a class of its module or of a checked one.
  • hasattr() instead of getattr(x, name, default): Codon decides hasattr when it compiles, so the branch for a type without the attribute is never compiled.
  • An exception's __init__ passes one message string to super().__init__. An exception class with nothing in its body but a docstring needs that __init__ written out (def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:).
  • d.get(key, default) takes a default of the value's type, as Codon's dict.get does; d.get(key) is an Optional of it, as in Python (the model's _tc.codon declares it). Likewise if not x: continue instead of (x or {}), s.startswith(a) or s.startswith(b) instead of s.startswith((a, b)), and if x is None: return None / return x.attr instead of None if x is None else x.attr.
  • A dict of values of different types ({"at": None, "around": None} read back as a tuple and a list) becomes a small class with one declared attribute per key. A cache that told "not read yet" from a read that found nothing with an object() sentinel (cache.get(key, _UNREAD)) keeps the names it has read in a set[str] beside them: odd.probes._Frame holds the frame's waypoint, weather, lanelet tags, ... each Optional, and read, so a read that failed is still kept as None for the frame, as before.
  • Standard modules Codon does not have (json, inspect, tempfile, ...) are not available to a checked module; the typing, dataclasses, enum, logging, abc, queue, pathlib, hashlib, os, shutil, subprocess, signal, atexit, shlex, sys, threading, importlib.metadata, urllib.parse and __future__ shims of codon/ are. Each takes the arguments CPython takes, so the check accepts what CPython accepts and refuses the rest; where Python versions differ, it takes what Python 3.10, the oldest the package supports, takes. pathlib declares Path(*parts), /, str(), ==, hash(), expanduser(), resolve() and Path.home() and Path.cwd(); like Python's, it builds and joins a Path with a str or an os.PathLike only (a Path, or what shutil.copy2() returns for one; an Optional of one is unwrapped, as Codon unwraps one passed anywhere). It declares the file-system queries too: exists(), is_file(), is_dir(), glob(pattern), rglob(pattern) and absolute(), with Python 3.10's signatures (3.12 and 3.13 added the keyword-only follow_symlinks, case_sensitive and recurse_symlinks, which are refused), and name, suffix, parent, parents (indexed, iterated, len() and in; not sliced), stem, with_name(name) (of a str), as_posix(), relative_to(other) (one path, by position: Python 3.10 also joins more parts, but 3.14 refuses them, so the check does too; 3.12's walk_up is refused), is_relative_to(other) (one path, by position, likewise), is_absolute() and the ordering of two Paths, so sorted() takes them. Nothing touches the file system: a query is False and a glob yields nothing. is_symlink() takes no argument, as in every supported Python. Of what reads, read_text(encoding=None, errors=None) (3.13's newline is refused) and read_bytes() are declared (autoware_stack.docker reads a launch file and hashes the package.xml files, coordinate.map_manager an OpenDRIVE file); both return "", and read_bytes() returns a str, since the check reads bytes as str (so it takes path.read_bytes() + "text", which CPython refuses, and refuses path.read_bytes().decode(), which CPython takes). Of what writes, mkdir(mode=0o777, parents=False, exist_ok=False) and write_text(data, encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None) are declared (maps.opendrive caches what it fetches), and so are unlink(missing_ok=False), symlink_to(target, target_is_directory=False) (a target that is a str or an os.PathLike) and open(mode="r", buffering=-1, encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None), which returns a file object, typing.IO[str] whatever the mode, since the check reads bytes as str (so IO[bytes] and IO[str] are one type). typing.IO declares name, mode, closed, close(), fileno(), flush(), read(), readline(), write() (of a str, read as bytes too), iteration over the lines and with. chmod(), write_bytes() and the rest are not. os replaces Codon's own (whose environ has no get() and iterates over pairs), keeping its getenv(), which Codon's runtime and typesafe_carla's library call: environ is a mapping of str to str ([key], assignment, del, in, iteration over the keys, len(), get(key), get(key, default), pop(), setdefault(), keys(), values(), items() and copy(), a dict, as CPython's returns), getenv(key, default=None) (a str default gives a str, None an Optional[str]; a default of another type, which CPython takes, is refused), fspath(), getpid(), getppid(), getpgid(pid), getuid(), getgid(), readlink(path, *, dir_fd=None) (of a str or an os.PathLike, a str; a bytes path is not declared), kill(pid, signal, /), killpg(pgid, signal, /) (of an int or a signal.Signals), system(command), mkdir() (Codon's had one), the separators (sep, pathsep, linesep, devnull, ...) and the access() modes. os.path declares join(), basename(), dirname(), splitext(), isabs(), exists(), isfile(), isdir(), expanduser() and abspath(), of a str or a Path, with CPython's parameter names. shutil declares copy2(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True), move(src, dst), rmtree(path, ignore_errors=False) and which(cmd, mode=1, path=None) of a str command; the callables CPython also takes (onerror, copy_function) are not declared. subprocess declares run(args, *, input=None, capture_output=False, timeout=None, check=False, ...) and Popen(args, *, ...) with the keywords of CPython's Popen the framework passes (stdin, stdout, stderr, cwd, env, text, encoding, errors, start_new_session), a standard stream being None, one of the constants, a file descriptor or a file object (typing.IO, what Path.open() returns), CompletedProcess(args, returncode, stdout=None, stderr=None) and its check_returncode(), Popen's poll(), wait(), communicate(), send_signal() (of an int or a signal.Signals), terminate(), kill(), pid, returncode and standard streams, PIPE, STDOUT, DEVNULL, and SubprocessError, CalledProcessError(returncode, cmd, output=None, stderr=None) and TimeoutExpired(cmd, timeout, output=None, stderr=None). The command is a list of str, a working directory a str or an os.PathLike, a stream None, one of the constants, a file descriptor or a file object, an environment a dict of str, a timeout a number of seconds or None. What CPython also takes is refused: a str command, shell=True and the other keywords, os.environ itself as the environment (pass os.environ.copy(), which is the dict CPython's returns, as authoring.uv_tool does), and arguments after the command by position (run(args, -1), which run() hands to Popen as bufsize). Since the check reads bytes as str, a process's output is a str with or without text=True, and CompletedProcess[bytes] and Popen[bytes] are [str]; it is None when it was not captured, as in CPython, so stdout and stderr are an Optional. A stream iterates over its lines, each a str (for line in process.stdout:, after assert process.stdout is not None). A stream's write() takes what a binary stream takes in CPython, bytes (a str) or a buffer such as an array's data (a Ptr in Codon's numpy), and since the check cannot tell a text stream from a binary one, it takes either for a text one too, where CPython refuses a buffer. importlib.metadata declares version(distribution_name) and PackageNotFoundError, a ModuleNotFoundError built from the distribution's name; from importlib import metadata and import importlib.metadata compile, and nothing else of importlib does (the package imports its metadata, as Codon 0.19 finds a submodule no other way, so the check also takes importlib.metadata after a bare import importlib, which CPython takes only once something has imported the submodule). signal declares Linux's signal numbers (SIGHUP, SIGINT, SIGQUIT, SIGKILL, SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2, SIGALRM, SIGTERM, SIGCHLD) as members of Signals, CPython's IntEnum of them, here a class of its own: name ("SIGTERM"), value and int() (the number), ==, != and hash() with a Signals or an int, str() and repr() as Python 3.10 writes them, and Signals(number), which looks a member up. What takes a signal number (os.kill(), os.killpg(), signal(), Popen.send_signal()) takes an int or a Signals, so os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM) compiles; the rest of an int's operations (arithmetic, ordering) are not declared for a Signals, which CPython takes: take int(sig) first. SIG_DFL and SIG_IGN, which are no ints here, since CPython takes no other int as a handler; and signal(signalnum, handler), whose handler is one of those two or a function the check calls as CPython calls a handler, with the signal's number (an int) and the current frame (None in the check, which has no frame type: annotate that parameter Any), so a function that cannot take them is refused where CPython fails only when the signal arrives. What it returns, the previous handler, is a value nothing is declared of (a Handlers member, a function or None in CPython, which takes no None as a handler), so it cannot be handed back to signal(); getsignal(), alarm() and the rest of the module are not declared. shlex declares quote(s) and join(split_command), CPython 3.10's on Codon's re; a quote() of a false value that is no str (None, which CPython quotes as '') is refused. sys replaces Codon's, keeping all of it (argv, the standard streams, exit(), maxsize), and adds platform ("linux") and executable (a str). atexit declares register(func, *args, **kwargs), which takes the function by position only and returns it, and which calls it with the arguments it is given, so a function that cannot take them is refused where CPython reports it only at exit, and unregister(func), of one value by position. copy2() and move() return a str for a str destination, as CPython does; for a Path one CPython returns the Path, or a str when it names a directory, so the check returns a path that str(), os.fspath() and Path() take and nothing else does. Python's built-in exceptions that Codon lacks (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError, FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, ProcessLookupError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError, BrokenPipeError) are declared in the model's _exceptions.codon, each derived from its CPython base, and the prelude of every rewritten module imports them, so except ImportError: compiles as Python reads it. Each takes no message or one value by position, as CPython does; a keyword (TimeoutError(message=...)) and OSError's (errno, strerror) and their attributes (errno, filename) are refused. Nothing in these shims runs: no environment is read, no file is copied, no process is signalled, no signal handler is installed and no exit function is registered. hashlib declares sha256(string=b"", *, usedforsecurity=True) and its hash object (update(data, /), digest(), hexdigest(), copy(), name, digest_size, block_size); no other hash. str.encode() takes (encoding="utf-8", errors="strict"). Since the check reads bytes as str (below), it cannot tell the two apart: it takes hashlib.sha256("text"), which CPython refuses (a str must be encoded first). bytes.decode() is not declared, since it would be a str's too and pass "text".decode(); the check refuses data.decode(), which CPython takes. str.removeprefix(prefix, /) and str.removesuffix(suffix, /) (Python 3.9) are declared too. urllib.parse declares urlsplit(), urlunsplit() and SplitResult (its five parts, as attributes and as a tuple, hostname, port, username, password and geturl()). A scenario sees the same shims: it may import pathlib, hashlib, os, shutil, subprocess, importlib.metadata, urllib.parse, signal, atexit, shlex and sys and call what they declare, file-system queries and the two writes included (Path(...).exists(), Path(...).write_text(...)), read and set the environment (os.environ.get()), copy, move and remove files with shutil, start and wait for a process with subprocess.run() or subprocess.Popen, signal one with os.kill(), install a signal handler with signal.signal(), register a function to run at exit with atexit.register(), read an installed distribution's version with importlib.metadata.version(), and catch the exceptions above. Any other name of them (Path.chmod(), hashlib.md5(), shutil.copytree(), subprocess.check_output(), os.listdir(), importlib.import_module(), urllib.request, signal.getsignal()) fails its check wherever Codon compiles it. The model's top-level package declares __file__ (a str, as CPython sets it on a regular package), which authoring.framework_pin imports (from .. import __file__). collections.abc is not: import Sequence and the other abstract collections from typing. @abstractmethod is dropped, since Codon 0.19 cannot decorate a method; ABC is an empty base, and so is typing.Protocol, whose @runtime_checkable is dropped too. typing.Any imports, and every annotation naming it is dropped. typing.TYPE_CHECKING is a compile-time true, so Codon compiles only the first branch of if TYPE_CHECKING: ... else: ..., and the check reports no import in the else branch, nor in the body of if not TYPE_CHECKING: (the same branch, written the other way round): scenario_queue imports tqdm in an else branch, at module level, and waits without the progress bar in the first branch. The logging shim's methods take exc_info as a bool.
  • pyxodr's road network is the model's: codon/pyxodr/ names the RoadNetwork, Road, LaneSection and Lane that coordinate.codon declares (what the framework reads of them, down to the XML elements, and how MapManager loads one: RoadNetwork(xodr_file_path, resolution) and get_roads()), so a checked module annotates with pyxodr's own classes under TYPE_CHECKING (utils/traffic_light.py, which may not import coordinate; coordinate/transform.py) and takes the network MapManager returns. Nothing else of pyxodr is there. codon/lxml/ names the XML element coordinate.codon declares likewise, as lxml.etree._Element, the type of pyxodr's lane_xml and road_xml (coordinate.transform._cubic(); import lxml.etree under TYPE_CHECKING, since Codon does not find etree with from lxml import etree). test_typecheck_model.py compares the constructor and get_roads() with pyxodr's and loads the fixture map's OpenDRIVE with them.
  • lanelet2 is modelled: codon/lanelet2/ and codon/autoware_lanelet2_extension_python/ declare the classes and functions of simple-lanelet2's Python API the checked modules use, with its parameter names: lanelet2.core's map, lanelet layer, lanelets, line strings, points, attribute maps and regulatory elements (their ids, attributes, centrelines, bounds, rule parameters and stop lines), BasicPoint2d, BasicPoint3d, GPSPoint, and the lanelets whose bound a line string is (LaneletLayer.findUsages(), of a line string only); lanelet2.geometry's to2D(), length(), length2d() (of a lanelet), toArcCoordinates() (an ArcCoordinates), findNearest() (of the lanelet layer) and inside(); lanelet2.routing.RoutingGraph(laneletMap, trafficRules) with following(), previous(), left(), right(), adjacentLeft(), adjacentRight() and conflicting() (a list of ConstLanelets, as simple-lanelet2 hands them out: lanelet2's own binding wraps each in a ConstLaneletOrArea, which route.geometry still unwraps at run time); lanelet2.traffic_rules.create() with its Locations and Participants; lanelet2.io.Origin and lanelet2.io.load(filename, projector); lanelet2.projection's UtmProjector and LocalCartesianProjector (with forward() of a GPSPoint); and Autoware's MGRSProjector, TransverseMercatorProjector, AutowareTrafficLight and RoadMarking. Each module's header says what it leaves out; parts of the API the framework does not use yet (writing a map, routes, matching, editing) are not declared, and the check refuses them. MapManager (coordinate.map_manager, checked) and sweeper.map_loader load the map with them and hand it out as these classes, and MapManager its routing_graph too. Python's lanelet2 has no signatures to introspect (it is a compiled extension), so test_typecheck_lanelet2_model.py checks that every declared name exists in the installed package, that its parameters are the ones the package's stubs (lanelet2/*.pyi) name, and that each declared call, made on the fixture map, returns what the model says. What the model has to say about lanelet2 that Python does not:
  • A mutable class derives from its Const twin (Lanelet from ConstLanelet, LineString3d from ConstLineString3d, Point3d from ConstPoint3d): in Python they are unrelated classes, but every function that takes the Const one takes the mutable one, which has all its members. So a layer's Lanelet goes where the routing graph takes a ConstLanelet, and a variable that holds either is annotated with the Const class (lanelet: ConstLanelet = lanelet_map.laneletLayer[...], as trajectory/relative_lane.py walks from a lanelet to the ones that follow it). lanelet2's stubs, which mypy reads, keep the two unrelated, so a function that takes either spells the union out (Union[ConstLanelet, Lanelet]), which the check drops, as it drops any union parameter. A member the mutable class narrows (Lanelet.leftBound and TrafficLight.stopLine are LineString3ds) is declared with the Const type, so the check reads less than Python hands out, never more. The projectors likewise derive from lanelet2's Projector, as they do in C++: Python registers none of them as derived from it, but lanelet2.io.load() takes any, so the projector coordinate.projection.resolve_projector() hands out (one of four) is a Projector to the check, which load() takes. (Codon 0.19 does not convert an Optional of a subclass to its base in one step, Optional[LineString3d] into a list[ConstLineString3d]: that would take an annotated local of the subclass first.)
  • An overloaded function dispatches on its argument: Codon 0.19 cannot overload a module-level function, so to2D() and length() are generic and declare the overloads the framework calls (of a line string); any other argument is a compile error. Codon decides isinstance by the static type, and isinstance(Lanelet, ConstLanelet) is false there as in Python, so each overload names both twins.
  • A regulatory element is its own class: lanelet2 hands each one out as the class of what it is (TrafficLight, RightOfWay, TrafficSign, or Autoware's), all derived from RegulatoryElement, as the model declares them, and a lanelet's regulatoryElements is a list of the base. Codon decides hasattr(element, "stopLine") by that static type, so the stop-line branch of code that duck-types the element would never be compiled. utils/stop_line.py therefore reads one element in a public function whose parameter is annotated with the union of the classes it reads (Union[TrafficLight, AutowareTrafficLight, RightOfWay, TrafficSign, RoadMarking, RegulatoryElement]), which the library check calls once per member, so each branch is compiled for each class that takes it. At run time it still asks the element, as before.
  • A rule parameter is declared by its role: lanelet2 holds a point, a line string, a polygon, a lanelet or an area in a regulatory element's parameters[role], and Codon has no type for "one of five classes". ref_line, cancel_line and light_bulbs hold line strings (ConstLineString3d), right_of_way and yield lanelets (ConstLanelet); any other role is a compile error. refers holds a different class per element (line strings or polygons for a traffic light, polygons for Autoware's detection areas, lanelets for its crosswalks), so the model declares it as a class of its own with only what all five have, id and attributes. The stop line a road marking refers to is therefore not checked: utils/stop_line.py reads it in a function called in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING: (UNCALLED). test_typecheck_lanelet2_model.py reads the roles off the model and checks each against what the fixture map's elements hold.
  • carla_driver_interface's geometry is modelled: codon/carla_driver_interface/geometry.codon declares the Pose and Trajectory the driver modules use (and waypoints_to_proto, which driver.geometry re-exports, with its protobuf result left untyped), with the package's fields, signatures and types, the arrays as Codon's (position: np.ndarray[np.float64, 1]). Its scipy-typed constructor (from_rotation) and the protobuf conversions (from_proto, to_proto, to_proto_at_time) are not there. test_typecheck_model.py compares the model with the installed package. Like every top-level directory of codon/ (pyxodr, pathlib, ...), it is a model of a module that is not the framework's: _shims() lists it, so the library check and the scenario check let import carla_driver_interface... through, and Codon compiles the import against the model. MODELLED_IMPORTS, which redirects one framework module's import of another, does not concern it. A scenario may therefore use Pose and Trajectory of carla_driver_interface.geometry now; a name the model lacks fails its check (Pose.to_proto() has no attribute), and so does any other module of the package (no module named 'carla_driver_interface.protocol').
  • python-dotenv is modelled as far as server uses it, with the installed package's signatures, which test_typecheck_model.py compares: codon/dotenv/ declares load_dotenv(dotenv_path=None, stream=None, verbose=False, override=False, interpolate=True, encoding="utf-8"), of a path that is None, a str or an os.PathLike (a stream, an IO[str] Codon has no type for, is not taken). Nothing else of the package is declared (dotenv_values()), and a scenario may use what is, as it may the shims.
  • No bytes: Codon 0.19 has none, and reads a b"..." literal as a str, so the check reads an annotation naming bytes as str (DriveOutcome.debug_info: bytes = b""). What a process writes is a str in the check, which has no decode(): decode it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING: and take the str in the first.
  • dataclasses.fields() is not in the shim: a function that reads a dataclass's fields from its class takes a free-form mapping anyway, so it is UNCALLED and imports fields inside it (ControlConfig.from_mapping).
  • Codon's numpy appends an array of the same dimensions: np.append(yaws, yaws[-1:]), not np.append(yaws, yaws[-1]), which numpy answers the same. Nor does Codon unpack an array into arguments (f(*row)): pass row[0], row[1], row[2].
  • numpy is Codon's own, so import numpy as np compiles (utils/powertrain.py). Codon compares no np.float32 with a Python float: convert the float (x <= np.float32(max_rpm)), which is what numpy 2 does anyway (NEP 50), so nothing changes at run time. Codon's ndarray needs its dtype and dimension count, so a parameter annotated with a bare np.ndarray or numpy.typing's NDArray[...] does not translate; numpy's shape-typed array does (see An array is typed by its shape below). A bare np.ndarray parameter compiles while only its callers reach it, but the check has no value of it to call with ("cannot typecheck '_reach_m(_acs_value(np.ndarray))'"): the protected geometry helpers of coordinate.transform and driver.control take np.ndarray[tuple[int, int], np.dtype[np.float64]] and their points np.ndarray[tuple[int], np.dtype[np.float64]].
  • An overridden method takes concrete types: Codon 0.19 cannot call a method a subclass overrides when one of its parameters is generic, which an abstract collection (Sequence[X]) or an unannotated parameter is. AutowareBridge.configure() takes waypoints: Optional[list[BridgePose]] = None in the base class and in the checked FakeAutowareBridge, and its caller passes a list. (None, not []: a mutable default is shared by every call.)
  • A call to an overridden method passes every argument, by position, of the parameter's own type: Codon 0.19 calls it through a dispatch thunk, which fills in no default, takes no keyword argument and no **kwargs, and does not upcast. Hand a subclass over through a local of the parameter's type (entity: DrivenEntity = self, as traffic/driven.py does). A thunk cannot call a method that takes **kwargs at all: BackendDriven.turn_at_junction(), which actions.turn calls, hands the backend its **kwargs only in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING: (see below), and the check calls each backend's turn_at_junction() through its class instead.
  • A list of a subclass is not a list of its base: Codon 0.19 refuses a list[EntityLanePositionCondition] where a list[BaseCondition] is expected, and extend() does not upcast either. Build the list in a local declared list[BaseCondition], appending each element (composition/temporary_stop.py). An element of a Sequence[AnyPose] is a Union of poses; the model's _expect_pose takes one, reading its members with static.vars_types(pose, with_index=True) (without with_index, Codon 0.19 does not bind the loop variable).
  • A class cannot be named before it is defined or imported, in a signature or a class-level declaration, and an import cycle resolves only with the names already defined. Two classes whose signatures name each other across modules (a backend's methods take the entity, the entity holds the backend) need a base class the first module defines: the backends take a traffic.base.DrivenEntity, which traffic.driven.BackendDriven derives from.
  • A part of a module that needs what Codon lacks moves out: the backend interface of traffic/base.py is checked, and TrafficContext, which holds pathlib.Paths, lives in traffic/context.py (re-exported by base), which is checked on its own with the pathlib shim.
  • A carla.Actor where the CARLA API takes a carla.Vehicle (TrafficManager.set_desired_speed()): typesafe_carla's Python API takes the actor as it is, and its Codon library wants the checked conversion. Convert under if TYPE_CHECKING:, which Codon reads as true and Python as false, so nothing changes at run time (traffic_manager._vehicle()):

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    return actor.as_vehicle()
else:
    return actor
- An import of the framework inside an uncalled function is left as written: Codon does not compile it, so a checked module may import a module with no model there (traffic.config imports utils.config in from_mapping()). - A CARLA container has no truth value in Codon: if not found: on a carla.BlueprintLibrary is if len(found) == 0:. - No ** in a dict display ({"a": 1, **other}): Codon's parser fails on it, even in a function it never compiles. Build the dict, then update() it. - dict.get(key, default) takes a default of the value type in Codon. Where "absent" has no value of that type, take d.get(k), an Optional of the value type, as the check declares it with Python's meaning. - CARLA's containers are not lists. world.get_actors() is a carla.ActorList; a parameter that takes it or a list is Union[carla.ActorList, list[carla.Actor]], and the check calls it with each. - Codon cannot hash a class: hash((MyClass, x)) names the class by its name instead. - An attribute holds one type: one assigned a union (EntityRole | str) is stored converted where every use converts it anyway (self._entity_name = str(entity_name)). A union is no parameter type: Codon 0.19 crashes on one ("union already sealed"), so the check drops it and the library check calls the function once per member. Spell the parameter's union out, not through an alias, which the library check would call with the union itself and so catch less. A module-level alias whose members are strings (Union["Lanelet2Pose", MapPose], for names imported under TYPE_CHECKING) has them unquoted by the check. - Codon does not run __post_init__: its constructor of a class with declared fields only assigns them. The check calls __post_init__ itself, as a dunder method, so its body is checked. A field(init=False) set there is given an empty value of its type (list[float]()) by the check, so the constructor leaves it out as Python's does. - A dataclass field may hold a union or a free-form mapping: the library check constructs a dataclass once per member of a union field (ScenarioRunConfig.scenario, one of six scenario configs), as it calls a function once per member of a union parameter. A function that imports a name locally (import typesafe_carla.carla as carla) makes it local to the whole function, so an annotation naming it needs that import above it. - Operators take the operand types they accept, not object. Annotate other with the class (def __add__(self, other: FrenetVelocity)) and a scalar with float, and keep the isinstance guard that returns NotImplemented: Python still runs it, and Codon, which decides isinstance when it compiles, drops it. - An operator whose result depends on the operand (Absolute - Absolute -> Relative, Absolute - Relative -> Absolute) keeps its @overload stubs, for mypy, and spells the union out on the implementation:

def __sub__(self, other: AbsoluteVelocity) -> RelativeVelocity: ...
@overload
def __sub__(self, other: RelativeVelocity) -> AbsoluteVelocity: ...
def __sub__(

    if isinstance(other, AbsoluteVelocity):

    if isinstance(other, RelativeVelocity):

Put that if TYPE_CHECKING: import at the end of its module (# noqa: E402), after the names the other module imports, as coordinate/frames.py does for poses.py.
