The check reads an annotation naming one of typesafe_carla's integer enumerations (carla.TrafficLightState, carla.LaneType, ...) as int, so keep the CARLA name (the authoring code generator reads it), and compare with get_state() rather than look a member up by value. A member's name is found through the enumeration's names (for name, member in carla.TrafficLightState.names.items()), which both APIs have, as utils/traffic_light.py does. - A sensor callback gets a carla.SensorData in the check, where the CPython API hands it the measurement itself (a carla.CollisionEvent). Listen through a method that converts only when it has to (if hasattr(data, "as_collision"): data = data.as_collision(), as conditions/collision.py does): Codon decides hasattr when it compiles, and the CPython measurement has no as_<kind>(). The camera and the LiDAR (sensor/) listen the same way, with as_image() and as_lidar(). A bound method of another object (a queue's put) is no listener: wrap it in a method of the sensor. - An array is typed by its shape: Codon's numpy types an array by its dtype and its number of dimensions (np.ndarray[np.float32, 2]), which numpy.typing's NDArray[np.float32] does not say, and Codon has no numpy.typing. Annotate with numpy's shape-typed array instead, np.ndarray[tuple[int, int], np.dtype[np.float32]] (two dimensions), which mypy reads as precisely and the check translates; a shape of tuple[int, ...] or Any, and NDArray, are dropped. An annotation broken over lines keeps its line breaks inside its brackets, so newest: Optional[\n ...\n] = None still compiles. - A measurement's raw_data is a view in typesafe_carla's Codon library, and Codon's np.frombuffer takes the bytes: read np.frombuffer(image.raw_data.tobytes(), ...) under if TYPE_CHECKING: and the CPython raw_data in the else branch, which copies nothing. - queue.Queue[T] is the queue shim's, with CPython's signatures (Queue(maxsize=0), put(item, block=True, timeout=None), get(block=True, timeout=None), put_nowait, get_nowait, empty, full, qsize, and the Empty and Full exceptions). Declare the queue's item type at class level (_frame_queue: queue.Queue[carla.Image]); queue.Queue() in __init__ takes it from there. - threading.Thread is the threading shim's, with CPython 3.10's signature (Thread(group=None, target=None, name=None, args=(), kwargs=None, *, daemon=None), start(), join(timeout=None), is_alive()); the check compiles the call the thread makes, target(*args), so a target that does not take its arguments fails it. args is a tuple, kwargs None and group None. The shim replaces the threading module Codon ships, which Codon's numpy and typesafe_carla's Codon library import for Lock, so it keeps all of that module (Lock, RLock, active_count(), get_native_id(), get_ident()), as Codon has it; a test compares the two. - A datetime is formatted from its fields: Codon's datetime has no __format__, so f"{now:%Y-%m-%d}" is f"{now.year:04d}-{now.month:02d}-{now.day:02d}", the same string for every year from 1000 on (ui.runner._multirun_dir()). - A dataclass derived from a dataclass is constructed with its base's fields first, as Python's constructor and Codon's take them, wherever the base is checked (CarlaCameraSensorConfig(CameraSensorConfig)). Of two bases that both bring fields, Python takes the last one's first and Codon 0.19 the first one's, so such a constructor is a problem: list it as UNCALLED. - No variable-length tuples beyond attributes: Codon's tuples have a fixed length. A class-level tuple[X, ...] and tuple(x) are checked as lists (above), but a tuple built otherwise (a display grown in a loop, a + (b,)) is not, and turning the source's tuple into a list changes what the class does (a frozen dataclass's hash, its equality with a tuple). A function that returns one is checked as returning a List[X] (#191): return tuple(x) of a list (signals.registry.registered_signal_controllers()), not a tuple display, which is a fixed-length Codon tuple, nor (). - No ** of a dict in a call (f(**extra) with extra a dict): Codon unpacks only a named tuple into keyword arguments. Write one call per set of keywords (RoutingAction passes waypoints= only when there are some, in a call of its own). - No escaped brace in an f-string (f"{{min, max}} of {name}"): Codon's parser rejects it, even in a function it never compiles. Concatenate the literal part ("{min, max}" + f" of {name}", as Range.parse does). - Literal["a", "b"] is checked as the type of its values (str), an annotation and a module-level alias alike (route.model's Tristate): Codon's own Literal types a compile-time value of int, bool or str only, and the typing shim's Literal is str (its TYPE_CHECKING is declared with Static[bool], Codon's other name for its Literal). A Literal inside a Union/Optional alias is translated the same way. A Literal of values of several types is dropped as an annotation; as an alias it is left as written, which the check rejects. - No getattr(obj, name) with a name built at run time: spell the attributes out (JunctionSegmentSpec.crossing()), and keep the getattr for any other name in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, so Python still raises the AttributeError it raised. - A method only some subclasses have (EgoVehicle.route_to(), which an entity found as a BackendDriven may or may not have): ask hasattr(entity, "route_to") and call it under that, and keep the call that raises the AttributeError for an entity without it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:. Codon decides hasattr by the static type, which lacks the method, so it compiles none of the calls: the check covers the lookup around them, not the calls (RoutingAction.execute()). - lanelet2's map at the model boundary: the checked MapManager hands out its lanelet_map and routing_graph as the lanelet2 model's classes (above), which the checked RouteFrame (route.frame) takes, so the checked scenario_route_frame() (route.active) builds it from them. - A model shared with checked modules is split out: the model's EgoConfig derives from VehicleEntityConfig, and the checked EgoVehicle.spawn() hands its spawn location to the checked spawn_vehicle_actor(). So the spawn locations and the NPC vehicle live in a model module of their own (_vehicle_entity.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with entity._spawn and entity.vehicle_entity: the model's EgoConfig then holds the checked SpawnLocation. The model of maps.cache (maps/cache.codon, subprocess and json) takes and returns a MapSource from a model module of its own (_map_source.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with the checked maps.source, so the checked maps.resolver hands the model's GitMapCache its own MapSource. Likewise GroundProjectionConfig (_ground_projection.codon, replaced with coordinate.snap): the example scenarios import it from the top-level package, which is the model, and hand it both to the model's BaseScenario and to the checked VehicleEntityConfig (#99). The top-level package model itself is not replaced: the examples derive from the model's BaseScenario, so their constructors' calls to super().__init__() compile the model's constructor. The checked BaseScenario.__init__ is compiled by the library check's own call, with its defaults; the one line that stores the ego's class (ego_type) is under if not TYPE_CHECKING: (#199). The model of ros2.cyclone (ros2/cyclone.codon, cyclonedds) declares the CycloneRos2Transport constructor that the checked entity.ros2_entity._cyclone_transport() calls; its base Ros2EgoTransport and its Ros2EgoConfig come from a model module of their own (_ros2.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with the checked ros2.transport and ros2.config, so the transport _cyclone_transport() returns is the checked Ros2EgoTransport, and its body is compiled. For the scenario check, which has no ROS 2 package, the two are stand-ins whose constructors are a compile_error, as for a class a checked package only re-exports (below). - A class a checked package only re-exports is declared in the model by name and constructor: GrpcAutowareBridgeServer (autoware_bridge/grpc_server.codon, grpc), EgoDriverGrpcClient (driver/egodriver_client.codon, grpc) and CarlaDriverEntity (entity.codon, grpc and carla_driver_interface's protocol), which the checked autoware_bridge, driver and entity packages re-export and no checked module builds or uses, and CoverageReport (coverage.codon, openodd's), which the checked coverage package re-exports with merge_coverage(documents), the COVERAGE_SCHEMA string and the CoverGroup enum (ODD, SITUATION, SCENARIO). Each constructor takes Python's parameters and is a compile_error: its config (AutowareBridgeConfig, DriverClientConfig) is a checked class the model does not have, or the class is only ever built by openodd's merge, so a scenario that builds one fails its check rather than passing it with arguments the run would refuse. Such a class derives from nothing in the model: a subclass of the model's EgoVehicle that nothing builds breaks Codon 0.19's code generation for every scenario (LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type). test_typecheck_model.py compares each with the Python class, and checks that its constructor is the compile_error. Of CoverageReport, which merge_coverage() returns, the model also declares what Codon has types for (runs, scenarios, groups(), group_grade(), to_markdown(), #298). - A Protocol a scenario may take is modelled with what is called of it: the library check compiles autoware_stack.launcher from its source, and for the scenario check autoware_stack/launcher.codon declares the AutowareLauncher that AutowareEgoEntity starts, polls and stops (start(*, name, bridge_address), poll(), stop()), with the prepare() and close() that ScenarioQueue calls (below), and the AutowareEpisode that start() returns. Python cannot instantiate a Protocol, so the model's constructor is a compile_error. - A model function returning a checked class: to_map_frame (coordinate.codon, which the scenario check and the checked modules that import the coordinate package compile against) returns autoware_bridge's BridgePose, which _bridge_pose.codon models (BridgePose, its Vector3 and Quaternion, as @tuples, since they are frozen, and moved_forward()); REPLACED_MODELS replaces it with the checked autoware_bridge.base, so AutowareEgoEntity hands the pose to_map_frame returns to the checked AutowareBridge.configure() (it imports coordinate.transform itself, which is checked, so the library check compiles the real to_map_frame there). - No math.dist in Codon's math: math.hypot of the differences, which is the computation CPython's math.dist makes (AutowareEgoEntity, actions.background_traffic, where test_background_traffic.py pins the two to the same number). - A function whose only return is return None: with an Optional[X] return annotation, the check returns Optional[X]() and realizes X before calling it (Writing a scenario that type-checks, #202), so it compiles as written, as does a local declared Optional[X] = None and returned (_Never.check in actions.background_traffic). Without an Optional annotation a bare None is still Codon's NoneType ("cannot typecheck 'None'"), and del of a parameter is refused. - A method that takes **kwargs, called on a value whose class a checked subclass overrides it in, is called through the base class under if TYPE_CHECKING:, and as written in the else branch: actions.turn calls BackendDriven.turn_at_junction(entity, ...) in the check, since AutowareEgoEntity overrides it and Codon 0.19 calls an overridden method through a dispatch thunk, which takes no keyword argument. The check calls each override through its class. Codon never compiles the else copy, so test_typecheck_else_branch.py guards it: wherever the then branch calls a method through its class and the else branch calls it through an instance, both must pass the same arguments, the receiver aside (#193). - A name the model lacks at the boundary: when a checked module imports a name of a modelled package that the model does not declare (trajectory/__init__.py re-exports ResolvedTrajectory), declare it in the model module. When the package does not export it, add it to _BOUNDARY in test_typecheck_model.py, so it is compared with the Python class as an exported name is. - A Protocol that checked code dispatches through becomes a base class: Codon has no structural typing, and decides isinstance and hasattr by the static type. sweeper.constraints.Constraint was a Protocol; it is an ABC whose evaluate() is abstract (so, as before, it cannot be instantiated itself), and every constraint of the module derives from it. What walks a constraint tree asks each class what to bind (_bind_set_level(), which the composite and set-level constraints override) instead of testing the value with isinstance and hasattr. A constraint of someone else's that does not derive from it still works at run time: the walk takes the duck-typed path for it, in the else branch of isinstance(constraint, Constraint), which Codon decides as true. What a set-level constraint caches (_cached_ids) is a field(init=False, repr=False, compare=False): declared, as Codon needs, but neither a constructor parameter nor part of the repr or the comparisons, and unset until the constraint is bound, as before (dataclasses.fields() now lists it, so dataclasses.asdict() of a set-level constraint includes it, and raises AttributeError before the constraint is bound; nothing in the framework calls either on a constraint). - A registry of classes at module level (sweeper.constraints' _LEAF_REGISTRY, sweeper.bindings' _BINDING_REGISTRY): Codon holds no class as a value, and cannot type dict[str, type]. Declare it dict[str, Any] and assign it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:; only the uncalled parser reads it. - An enum member looked up by name, or an enum iterated over (ComparisonRule[name], list(ComparisonRule)): write it as in Python. The check rewrites both for an enum of the package being checked (Iterating an enum), so sweeper.constraints has no spelled-out member lists left. The framework's own model enums are the exception: they are not iterable. - An exception class raised with no arguments (raise _Exhausted() in route.search): Codon 0.19 raises no exception class without its own __init__, and its Exception takes a message where Python's takes none. The constructor calls super().__init__("") under if TYPE_CHECKING: and super().__init__() in the else branch. - An Optional chosen by a conditional expression, whose value goes to a union field (beside = graph.left(l) if left else graph.right(l), then BindingResult(value=beside.id), a float | int | list[int]): Codon 0.19 generated invalid LLVM IR and crashed without a diagnostic ("Call parameter type does not match function signature", optimize.cpp:1070). Choose with an if statement into a local annotated Optional[...]. - A function that returns a tuple with an Optional member, None in one return and a value in another (route.frame.ego_placement()): annotate the local in each return's own assignment (no_goal: Optional[tuple[int, float]] = None, goal_at: Optional[tuple[int, float]] = frame.locate(s)): one local annotated Optional where it is assigned None, and assigned the value later, was not enough. - A loop variable assigned a subclass's value is retyped: in a function that already declared other: ConstLanelet, other = near (a Lanelet) makes other a Lanelet, and a list of (float, ConstLanelet) then refuses it. Give the upcast a name of its own (nearby: ConstLanelet = near, route.geometry). - A value of a type the model holds: a checked module that hands a checked value to a checked module that imports it through the model (MODELLED_IMPORTS) hands the wrong type. scenario_runner hands the checked BaseScenario to measures.set_measured_scenario(), and its EgoConfig to EgoVehicle.spawn(), which take the model's: it makes those calls in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, and takes the spawned actor from ego.actor in the first. - No module object to assign a global through (vehicle_entity._warmup_done = True): Codon 0.19 imports no module as a value. The module sets its global in a function of its own (entity.vehicle_entity._set_warmup_done()). - The runner's boundary is modelled: coverage.codon declares the CoverageCollector (its constructor, start(), tick(), end(), write(path, scenario), and the run's case and outcome, record_case(case, space=None) and record_outcome(passed, *, failed_at=None, environment=None); openodd's backend and generator are refused), odd.codon resolve_odd(spec), whose union parameter (str, Path, OddDefinition or None) is generic and checked in its body, reset_probes(), the ODD's modules, the case a run records (OddCase, a @tuple of openodd's OddSample and ParameterSpace, which only the sampler builds) and what the runner reads of odd.route's verdict on the ego's planned route (plan_route_coverage(), RouteCoverage and RouteLanelet, which only it builds), and openodd's UNDECIDED, which the checked odd.probes returns: the one instance of a class openodd does not export (odd.model names it Undecided, for annotations), whose constructor is a compile error, as Python cannot build another, so the model allocates its one with Undecided.__new__(); environment.codon the id of the run's environment (capture() and RunEnvironment.id), and autoware_stack/launcher.codon the launcher's prepare() and close(), which the queue calls. test_typecheck_model.py compares each with the Python one. - No attribute of a union: Codon 0.19 reads pose.yaw of a value typed as a union (a vertex's position) as no type, even when every member has it with one type. After isinstance, name the value as the class (relative: RelativeLanePose = position) and read that; a union reaches a parameter typed with one of its members the same way. A generic function handed the union compiles every branch for it, so one that returns a different class per branch (route.positions.resolve_route_pose()) is called with each class on its own (trajectory.resolve._place_on_route()). - A callable of a union: Callable[[Union[A, B]], R] crashes Codon 0.19 ("union already sealed"), whether a parameter's, a variable's or a return's. Spell the callable out in the annotation (the checker drops a Callable parameter or return annotation, so the function is generic, and calls it with _acs_Returning[R, N]); a module-level alias (PositionResolver = Callable[...]) stays for Python and is None to the check, which refuses the alias as an expression ("expected type expression"). A function that takes either a resolver it is given or one it builds hands each to a helper of its own (trajectory.resolve._resolve_vertices()): one variable holds one type. - A closure calling another closure does not see that one's captures ("name 'x' is not defined"): make the inner one a module-level function taking what it read (trajectory.resolve._ego_route_s()). - A tuple display does not make a float the Optional[float] its annotation wants (return world.x, world.y, world.z, world.yaw from a function returning Tuple[float, float, Optional[float], Optional[float]]): a call does (trajectory.resolve._resolved()). - A singleton's __new__: Codon's constructor allocates and calls __init__, never a class's __new__, and its object.__new__ takes no class. The check rewrites super().__new__(cls) to C.__new__(), which allocates a C, and a class without __init__ is built by Codon from every attribute it declares: give it an __init__ that does nothing (MapManager; Python calls it after __new__). - Path.read_text() is in the pathlib shim (CPython 3.10's encoding and errors; 3.13's newline is refused); it reads an empty text.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to use the autoware-carla-scenario package to run autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA simulator.

docs.title: CLI Commands Overview
docs.text:
The package provides these CLI commands:

Command Framework Purpose scenario Hydra Run autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA scenario-new argparse Scaffold a standalone scenario package scenario-check Hydra compose Compile scenarios with Codon without running them (the static check the runner makes before a run) scenario-slurm argparse Follow, collect, resubmit or cancel a batch run as SLURM array jobs (launcher=slurm) scenario-odd argparse Check an ODD and show its buckets; scenario-odd route checks scenarios' planned routes against it on the Lanelet2 map detect-no-3d-model argparse Detect lanelets without a matching 3D ground model in CARLA viewer FastAPI + Uvicorn Web UI for browsing and monitoring scenario test results scenario-editor FastAPI + Uvicorn Web UI for authoring scenarios and exporting reproducible packages

viewer and scenario-editor are separate applications on separate ports, and neither starts the other.

docs.title: scenario - Scenario Runner
docs.text: Runs autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA. Uses Hydra for configuration management. Requires a running CARLA server.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Parses the scenario=... argument (supports glob patterns for batch execution)
  2. Composes a Hydra config from map, server, ego, entity, and scenario configs
  3. Compiles the scenario with Codon and refuses it if it does not type-check (Static Check; typecheck=off skips it)
  4. Connects to the CARLA server and loads the specified map (OpenDRIVE or built-in)
  5. Spawns the ego vehicle at the configured Lanelet2 position (converted to CARLA coordinates)
  6. Enables synchronous mode (fixed 20 Hz tick rate) and starts the native CARLA recorder
  7. Runs a warm-up phase (5 ticks for physics stabilization)
  8. Enables autopilot and applies initial speeds
  9. Executes the main tick loop, checking pass/fail conditions each tick
  10. Writes the results as JSON, and the run's trajectory log as it goes
  11. Reloads the CARLA world for clean state between scenarios

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Run a single scenario
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight

# Run a left-turn variant
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn

# Run traffic light compliance scenario
uv run scenario scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance

# Run a lane change scenario
uv run scenario scenario=lane_change/left

# Run a temporary stop scenario
uv run scenario scenario=temporary_stop/temporary_stop

docs.title: Batch Execution with Glob Patterns
docs.text:
When the scenario= value contains glob metacharacters (*, ?, [), all matching scenario configs are executed sequentially in a single CARLA session:

# Run all intersection-passing variants
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*'

# Run all scenarios matching a partial pattern
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/left_*'

# Run all lane-change scenarios
uv run scenario scenario='lane_change/*'

# Run everything
uv run scenario scenario='*/*'

Batch constraints:

  • All scenarios in a batch must share the same map (CARLA loads one map per session)
  • Results are written to outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/batch_results.json
  • A summary table is printed at the end with per-scenario pass/fail status
  • A case that cannot run at all -- its run raises on every attempt (server.cooldown_max_retries), e.g. a spawn point with no ground under it -- does not end the batch: it is reported as [ERROR] with the error, its batch_results.json entry is "passed": false with "error": true, and the batch goes on with the next case. Ctrl+C still stops the batch
  • A scenario with a sweep: section runs once, as configured; add --multirun to run every case of it (see Running every sweep case in a batch)

docs.title: Running every sweep case in a batch
docs.text:
With --multirun, a batch expands each scenario's sweep: -- lanelet constraints, a route search, the ODD sampler -- into its cases, the same ones scenario-expand prints, and runs them all in the one queue, against one CARLA session (and, with autoware.launcher, a fresh Autoware per case):

# Every lanelet case of both cut-in scenarios
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt

# 10 cases per scenario drawn from the ODD
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt \
  +sweep.odd_sample.count=10 +sweep.odd_sample.strategy=coverage

Scenarios that draw from one ODD go on from each other's draws rather than each draw the same cases: with strategy: coverage a later scenario aims at what the earlier ones left uncovered (see Sampling scenarios from the ODD).

A scenario with more than one case is listed as name#k in the summary, and batch_results.json gives each case its overrides. hydra/sweeper=... may be given but is not needed: the batch is the sweeper.

On a SLURM cluster, launcher=slurm runs a batch's cases as array jobs, several at once, each on a CARLA of its own, with the same outputs (off unless selected; see Running a Batch on SLURM):

uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' +sweep.odd_sample.count=24 \
  launcher=slurm launcher.array_parallelism=2

docs.title: Selecting a Published HD Map
docs.text:
A map group can name a git repository instead of local files, and the map is fetched into ~/autoware_data/maps on first use -- the same directory Autoware's own setup downloads maps into, so a machine that has run it clones nothing:

# Town10HD_Opt, as published for CARLA 0.10, pinned to a commit. The built-in
# scenario configs name Nishishinjuku lanelets, so place the ego on Town10's.
uv run scenario scenario=lane_change/left map=town10hd_opt \
  ego.spawn_lanelet_id=324 ego.spawn_s=10.0 ego.goal_lanelet_id=5650

# Any repository, any revision
uv run scenario map=town10hd_opt \
  map.source='git+https://huggingface.co/datasets/OWNER/NAME@REF#maps/T'

# A map directory on this machine, read in place
uv run scenario map=town10hd_opt map.directory=/path/to/autoware_maps/Town10HD_Opt

See HD Maps from a Git Repository.

docs.title: Lanelet Constraint Sweeping
docs.text:
The package ships a Hydra Sweeper plugin (hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint) that expands a single scenario config into one job per lanelet that matches a set of constraints, optionally deriving per-job parameters via "bindings". Each scenario YAML may declare its own sweep: section (see traffic_light_compliance.yaml for an example).

# Run a Hydra multirun over every lanelet whose `ego.spawn_lanelet_id`
# satisfies the scenario's `sweep.constraints`.
uv run scenario --multirun scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance \
  hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint

# Resume a sweep from job number N (1-indexed; 0 disables).
uv run scenario --multirun scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance \
  hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint sweep.resume_from=10

Sweeps write results under multirun/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/<job-index>/, not outputs/. The result viewer scans both directories.

To get the concrete scenarios without running them (for example, to fan them out over a cluster), use scenario-expand. It takes the same arguments as scenario and prints JSON with one list of Hydra overrides per concrete scenario. These are the same cases, in the same order, that the sweeper runs:

uv run scenario-expand scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance
# {"scenario": "...", "cases": [["ego.spawn_lanelet_id=5", "ego.spawn_s=18.62..."], ...]}

A scenario without a sweep: section is already concrete, so it expands to a single empty case. Only the Lanelet2 map is needed, not a CARLA server.

A logical scenario -- a document with a route search, whose sweep: holds route: instead of constraints: -- expands to one case per route of the map that matches its pattern, each with the ego's spawn and goal and the match itself (scenario.route.*); see Logical Scenarios from Routes.

docs.title: Resume from a Specific Scenario
docs.text:
When running large batches, you can skip already-completed scenarios. --resume-from N starts at the Nth scenario (1-indexed, as for a sweep); in a --multirun batch it counts the expanded cases:

# Resume from the 3rd scenario
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' --resume-from 3

docs.title: Overriding Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Any nested Hydra parameter can be overridden from the command line:

# Select a different map
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight map=nishishinjuku

# Connect to a remote CARLA server
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight server.host=192.168.1.100 server.port=3000

# Change ego vehicle type and speed
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight \
  ego.vehicle_type=vehicle.tesla.model3 \
  ego.initial_speed_kmh=30.0

# Override scenario-specific parameters
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight scenario.timeout_seconds=15.0

# Change Traffic Manager port
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight traffic_manager.port=8200

docs.title: Hydra Configuration System
docs.text:
Configuration files are located in src/autoware_carla_scenario/examples/conf/:

conf/
├── config.yaml              # Root config (defines defaults and top-level overrides)
├── server/
│   └── localhost.yaml       # Server connection settings
├── ego/
│   └── default.yaml         # Ego vehicle settings
├── entity/
│   └── default.yaml         # Entity spawn and ground projection settings
├── traffic_manager/
│   └── default.yaml         # CARLA Traffic Manager settings
├── map/
│   └── nishishinjuku.yaml   # Map file paths and excluded lanelet IDs
└── scenario/
    ├── intersection_passing/
    │   ├── straight.yaml
    │   ├── left_turn.yaml
    │   ├── right_turn.yaml
    │   └── straight_3npc.yaml
    ├── lane_change/
    │   ├── left.yaml
    │   └── right.yaml
    ├── lane_change_fail/
    │   ├── left.yaml
    │   └── right.yaml
    ├── temporary_stop/
    │   └── temporary_stop.yaml
    └── traffic_light_compliance/
        └── traffic_light_compliance.yaml

docs.title: Root Configuration (config.yaml)
docs.text:
Defines the default config group composition:

Default Group Default Value Description server localhost CARLA server connection ego default Ego vehicle configuration entity default Entity spawn and ground projection traffic_manager default CARLA Traffic Manager scenario intersection_passing/left_turn Scenario to run map nishishinjuku Map to load

Parameter Type Default Description entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_upper float 5.0 Ray search range above estimated z (meters) entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_lower float 10.0 Ray search range below estimated z (meters) entity.spawn_retry_max_count int 10 Maximum retry attempts for spawn entity.spawn_retry_t_step float 0.1 Lateral offset shift per retry (meters) entity.spawn_retry_z_step float 0.5 Vertical shift per retry (meters)

docs.title: Seeing a run
docs.text:
A run renders no video (since 15.0.0). What it leaves to look at is its trajectory log, {ScenarioName}.trajectory.jsonl: every vehicle and pedestrian tick by tick, the traffic lights, the map it ran on, the ego's plan (its debug markers), each condition's state and the verdict (Trajectory Log). To see it, make it a Rerun recording, {ScenarioName}.rrd beside the log, and open that in the Rerun viewer. The conversion is the autoware-carla-scenario-rerun package, installed with the rerun extra:

# The converter (rerun), and the Rerun viewer its recordings are made for (viewer):
pip install 'autoware-carla-scenario[rerun,viewer]'
# A recording of every run, made as each run ends:
uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/cut_in rerun.enabled=true
uv run scenario 'scenario=cut_in/*' --multirun rerun.enabled=true
rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12/CutInScenario-3.rrd     # the Rerun viewer
Parameter Type Default Description rerun.enabled bool false Convert each run's trajectory log into {ScenarioName}.rrd as soon as the run ends rerun.strict bool false Fail the conversion of a log with a record type or a field the converter does not know, rather than skip it with a warning

With rerun.enabled=true:

  • A run asking for recordings without the extra installed is refused before anything starts (exit code 2), saying how to install it.
  • Each log is converted on a background thread as soon as its run ends, while the next case runs (the converter releases the GIL; a log takes milliseconds). A run that raised is converted too: its log is what shows what happened.
  • At the end the run waits for the last conversions and prints how they went: Rerun recordings: N/M written, and a line per failure naming its case. A failed conversion does not change any verdict or the exit code.
  • Each case's {ScenarioName}_result.json names its recording (rerun_recording), and so does its entry in a batch's batch_results.json, with rerun_error when the conversion failed. The viewer's scenario page shows it in the embedded Rerun viewer, without converting the log again (Seeing a run in the viewer).
  • A Hydra sweep (--multirun without a glob) runs each case in a process of its own, and each converts its own log. So does each task of a batch run on SLURM (launcher=slurm, Running a Batch on SLURM): it converts its own cases, and scenario-slurm collect reports their recordings as a local batch does.

A run made without it (or by a version before it) can be converted afterwards, the same way:

# Every run of a session (a sweep's directory works the same), or one log:
python -m autoware_carla_scenario.rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12
python -m autoware_carla_scenario.rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12/CutInScenario-3.trajectory.jsonl

or from Python, autoware_carla_scenario.rerun.convert_outputs(path). The converter reads nothing but the log and the map files the log names, so it runs anywhere, without CARLA. The CARLA recording ({ScenarioName}.log) is still written: CARLA's own replayer (client.replay_file()) plays it back on a server running the same map.

video.* settings (video.enabled, video.width, video.height) are accepted for old command lines and configs, and do nothing: a run that sets one warns that it is ignored and says the above.

docs.title: Map Configuration
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description map.name str required CARLA map name (e.g., NishishinjukuMap) map.source str | null null Git repository holding the HD map (see maps.md) map.directory str | null null Local map directory, read in place. Wins over map.source map.xodr_path str | null null Path to custom OpenDRIVE file. If null, loads built-in CARLA map by name map.lanelet2_path str | null null Path to Lanelet2 .osm file (required for lanelet-based spawn) map.no_3d_model_lanelet_ids list[int] [] Lanelet IDs to exclude from sweeps (no ground geometry)

Map paths can use environment variables with Hydra's OmegaConf resolver:

xodr_path: ${oc.env:NISHISHINJUKU_XODR_PATH,path/to/default.xodr}

docs.title: Intersection Passing
docs.text:
Tests ego vehicle traversal through an intersection. Verifies that the ego passes through the expected OpenDRIVE road sequence.

Config Turn Direction Description intersection_passing/straight none Drive straight through intersection intersection_passing/left_turn left Left turn at intersection intersection_passing/right_turn right Right turn at intersection intersection_passing/straight_3npc none Straight with 3 NPC vehicles

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.expected_route_lanelet_ids list[int] varies Lanelet IDs the ego must traverse scenario.timeout_seconds float 5.0 Maximum scenario duration scenario.min_speed_kmh float | null null Minimum ego speed (fail if below). null disables check scenario.speed_check_delay_seconds float 0.3 Grace period before speed check starts scenario.turn_direction str | null null "left", "right", or null for straight scenario.npc_vehicles list [] NPC vehicle configurations (see below)

NPC vehicle configuration:

npc_vehicles:
  - spawn_lanelet_id: 100
    spawn_s: 5.0
    vehicle_type: vehicle.mini.cooper
    initial_speed_kmh: 10.0

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Registers a TurnAction for left/right turns (applies steering via CARLA autopilot route) - Pass condition: ego traverses all expected OpenDRIVE road IDs (checked via StickyCondition + AndCondition) - Fail conditions: timeout, ego destroyed, speed below threshold

docs.title: Lane Change
docs.text:
Tests ego vehicle lane change maneuvers. Can test both successful lane changes and expected failures.

Config Direction Expected Result lane_change/left left success lane_change/right right success lane_change_fail/left left fail (no adjacent lane) lane_change_fail/right right fail (no adjacent lane)

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.direction str "left" Lane change direction: "left" or "right" scenario.expect str "success" Expected outcome: "success" or "fail" scenario.timeout_seconds float 10.0 Maximum scenario duration

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Immediately registers a LaneChangeAction - Derives the target lane from the current spawn position and direction - Pass condition: expect=success requires both road_id and lane_id to change; expect=fail passes when timeout is reached without a lane change - Checks via EntityLanePositionCondition

docs.title: Traffic Light Compliance
docs.text:
Tests that the ego vehicle correctly stops at a red light and proceeds after green.

Config traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.light_switch_delay_seconds float 5.0 Delay before switching red to green scenario.timeout_seconds float 8.0 Maximum scenario duration scenario.stop_zone_min_m float 0.0 Near end of the stop zone: metres before the stop line (stop_line_distance_m) scenario.stop_zone_max_m float 3.0 Far end of the stop zone; standing still farther back until the green fails the run scenario.stop_line_tolerance_m float 0.0 How far the front bumper may pass the stop line on red before the run fails for running the red; that far past counts as at the line for the stop zone scenario.standstill_seconds float 0.5 How long the ego has to stand still in the stop zone, before the green, for it to count as stopped there (latched once it has) scenario.standstill_speed_mps float 0.1 Speed (m/s) at or below which the ego stands still scenario.departure_speed_kmh float 10.0 Speed (km/h) the ego must reach after green to pass; null uses moving_speed_kmh scenario.moving_speed_kmh float 1.0 The departure speed when departure_speed_kmh is null; no longer judges the red phase scenario.merging_time_seconds float 0.5 Deprecated and unused; kept so configs that set it still load

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to RED initially - Registers a TrafficSignalAction to switch to GREEN after light_switch_delay_seconds - Fails as soon as the ego's front bumper crosses the stop line while the light is red - At the green, fails unless the ego has stood still with its front bumper in the stop zone (stop_zone_min_m-stop_zone_max_m before the stop line), saying whether it stopped short of the zone, stopped in it too late, or had not stopped - Pass conditions: ego stood still in the stop zone before the green AND reaches departure_speed_kmh during green

docs.title: Temporary Stop
docs.text:
Tests that the ego vehicle stops at a designated stop line for a minimum duration, then restarts.

Config temporary_stop/temporary_stop

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.s_margin float 5.0 Arc-length margin around stop position (meters) scenario.speed_threshold float 0.1 Max speed considered as "stopped" (m/s) scenario.stop_duration float 0.3 Minimum consecutive seconds to remain stopped scenario.restart_speed_kmh float 3.0 Speed threshold for restart detection (km/h) scenario.timeout_seconds float 5.0 Maximum scenario duration

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Registers a TemporaryStopCondition at the configured stop position - Pass condition: ego stays within s_margin of stop line at speed below speed_threshold for at least stop_duration seconds, then accelerates above restart_speed_kmh

docs.title: Scenario Evaluation
docs.text:
Each scenario registers pass conditions and fail conditions. The tick loop evaluates them every frame:

  • First pass condition satisfied → scenario passes
  • First fail condition triggered → scenario fails
  • Common fail conditions: TimeoutCondition (exceeded time limit), EntityExistenceCondition (ego destroyed)

docs.title: ODD and Coverage
docs.text:
Every run is measured against an ODD, named by the odd key (default unless overridden). Its attributes are sampled on every tick and written, with the scenario's own cover items, to {ScenarioName}_coverage.json. scenario-coverage outputs/ merges those files into a report. See ODD and Coverage.

uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn odd=path/to/urban.yaml
uv run scenario-coverage outputs/ --markdown coverage.md

Before running, scenario-odd route plans each scenario's ego route on the Lanelet2 map (no CARLA server) and reports which parts of it are outside the ODD, which are undecided until run time, the metres it is expected to cover in each bucket, and the buckets no route reaches (Checking a planned route):

uv run scenario-odd route path/to/urban.yaml 'intersection_passing/*' lane_change/left

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
Each scenario run generates output in outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/:

File Description {ScenarioName}.log CARLA native recording (replay format) {ScenarioName}_result.json Machine-readable result with condition statuses {ScenarioName}_coverage.json ODD and scenario coverage hits of the run (merge with scenario-coverage, see Coverage) {ScenarioName}_odd.tar.gz The run's ODD as the files it was read from (an ODD read from OpenODD YAML; openodd's transmission archive, named by its revision; see Versions of an ODD) {ScenarioName}_requirements.lock What the run ran with: every installed distribution pinned, in the requirements format (pip install -r), headed by the framework, the scenario's package, Python and the platform. A distribution from git is pinned to its commit; an editable one (a checkout) names its directory, commit and whether it had uncommitted changes {ScenarioName}_environment.json The same, structured; _result.json carries its summary (environment: the framework, the scenario's package, key dependencies, and the lock's id -- the SHA-256 of what it pins -- so runs on one environment can be found by it) {ScenarioName}.trajectory.jsonl The run, tick by tick, and the map, plan, conditions and verdict (Trajectory Log); make it a Rerun recording to see the run (Seeing a run) {ScenarioName}.rrd The Rerun recording of the trajectory log, with rerun.enabled=true (Seeing a run) batch_results.json Batch summary (glob/batch mode only)

Result JSON format:

{
  "scenario": "intersection_passing/straight",
  "passed": true,
  "message": "All pass conditions satisfied",
  "elapsed_seconds": 3.42,
  "condition_statuses": [
    {"label": "Road 5 visited", "satisfied": true, "message": "..."},
    {"label": "Road 12 visited", "satisfied": true, "message": "..."}
  ]
}

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All scenarios passed 1 One or more scenarios failed or errored, or configuration/runtime error

docs.title: Driving the Ego with an External Policy
docs.text:
By default CARLA's TrafficManager drives the ego. To hand it to an external driving policy over the egodriver gRPC contract instead, start the policy server and select the carla_driver entity:

# 1. Start the policy (in its own environment)
uv run carla-driver-interface serve --policy route_follower --port 50051

# 2. Run any scenario against it
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.address=localhost:50051

ego.entity accepts:

Value Behaviour autopilot (default) CARLA's TrafficManager drives the ego autoware Autoware drives the ego, over the AutowareBridge; with autoware.launcher the framework starts a fresh Autoware per scenario (Autoware as the Ego) carla_driver An external policy drives the ego ros2 ROS 2 nodes drive the ego over DDS, with no bridge node (ROS 2 over DDS)

Common overrides:

# Query the policy every simulation tick instead of every other one
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.policy_timestep_s=0.05

# Pin the rig origin offset when the derived value looks wrong (CARLA 0.9.x)
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.rear_axle_offset_m=-1.4

# Send a smaller, cheaper camera frame
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver \
    driver.cameras.0.image_width=480 driver.cameras.0.image_height=302

See External Driver Interface for the full reference.

docs.title: detect-no-3d-model - 3D Model Detection
docs.text: Detects lanelets that do not have a matching 3D ground model in CARLA. Useful for identifying areas where vehicle ground-projection ray casting will fail. Requires a running CARLA server with the target map loaded.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Reads the map configuration YAML to resolve xodr_path and lanelet2_path
  2. Connects to the CARLA server
  3. For each lanelet's center point, casts a vertical ray (upward and downward from estimated z) to detect ground geometry
  4. Reports lanelets where the ray does not hit any 3D surface
  5. Writes the detected IDs to the YAML configuration's no_3d_model_lanelet_ids field

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Basic detection using map config YAML
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml

# Connect to a remote CARLA server
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml --host 192.168.1.100 --port 3000

# Increase ray search range for hilly terrain
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml --ray-upper 10.0 --ray-lower 10.0

# Longer timeout for slow connections
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml --timeout 30.0

# Debug logging
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml -v

docs.title: Command-Line Options
docs.text: Option Short Required Default Description yaml_path - Yes - Path to map configuration YAML (must contain map.name, xodr_path, lanelet2_path) --host - No localhost CARLA server hostname --port - No 2000 CARLA server port --ray-upper - No 5.0 Ray search range above z estimate (meters) --ray-lower - No 5.0 Ray search range below z estimate (meters) --timeout - No 10.0 CARLA client timeout (seconds) --verbose -v No false Enable DEBUG logging

docs.title: Input YAML Requirements
docs.text:
The YAML file must contain at minimum:

name: NishishinjukuMap        # CARLA map name
xodr_path: path/to/map.xodr  # Path to OpenDRIVE file
lanelet2_path: path/to/map.osm  # Path to Lanelet2 file

docs.title: Integration with Scenario Runner
docs.text: The detected lanelet IDs are stored in the map config's no_3d_model_lanelet_ids field. The scenario runner's sweep feature uses this list to exclude problematic lanelets from automatic spawn point selection.

docs.title: viewer - Scenario Result Viewer
docs.text: Web UI for browsing and monitoring scenario test results. Starts a FastAPI server with Uvicorn.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Scans the base path directory for scenario output files (outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/)
  2. Serves a web interface for browsing sessions and viewing individual scenario results, each with its run in an embedded Rerun viewer (Seeing a run in the viewer)
  3. Provides an API for triggering scenario runs and monitoring progress in real time

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Start with default settings (0.0.0.0:9000, current directory)
uv run viewer

# Custom host and port
VIEWER_HOST=127.0.0.1 VIEWER_PORT=8080 uv run viewer

# Specify results directory
VIEWER_BASE_PATH=/path/to/scenario/outputs uv run viewer

Then open http://localhost:9000 (or the configured host/port) in a browser.

docs.title: Seeing a run in the viewer
docs.text:
A scenario's page shows its run in Rerun's web viewer, embedded in the page: the case's trajectory log made into a Rerun recording (Seeing a run). A recording already beside the log (X.rrd beside X.trajectory.jsonl) is shown as it is; otherwise the viewer makes it the first time the page is opened (in a worker thread, some tens of milliseconds for a case) and keeps it beside the log, or, where the session's directory cannot be written, in its cache directory. Making one needs the converter in the viewer's environment:

pip install 'autoware-carla-scenario[rerun]'    # or: pip install autoware-carla-scenario-rerun

Without it the page says so, and still shows a recording already made. The page's Download .rrd link is the recording itself, for the native viewer (rerun X.rrd).

The web viewer is the @rerun-io/web-viewer package of the version the converter writes recordings with (RERUN_VERSION, 0.38.1 for converter 0.1; a recording opens only in a viewer of its minor version). By default the page loads it from the unpkg CDN, pinned to that version. For a machine without the network, keep a copy that the viewer serves itself:

uv run viewer --fetch-rerun-web-viewer                 # from the npm registry, checked against its integrity hash
uv run viewer --fetch-rerun-web-viewer --from web-viewer-0.38.1.tgz   # from the package's tarball, copied in

The copy goes to ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/viewer/rerun-web-viewer/<version>/ (VIEWER_CACHE_DIR moves the cache) and is used from then on. VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER overrides where the viewer comes from: an unpacked copy of the package (a directory), a mirror of it (a URL), or none for no embedded viewer (the page then names the recording only).

docs.title: Results on the ODD
docs.text: A session's page links its results on the ODD (/session/{type}/{date}/{time}/odd): openodd's coverage matrix (openodd.CoverageView) of the cases' coverage files ({stem}_coverage.json), along two ODD attributes picked above it (by default the two the cases were drawn over that tell them apart most). Each cell holds the runs that spent time in it, coloured by what they did -- green passed, red failed, yellow flaky (both), white not sampled -- and a click on one drills into it: the matrix of the next two attributes inside it, and below, the cases in it, each linking to its page (and its run in the Rerun viewer) with its verdict, the buckets it was drawn in and a few metrics of how the ego drove, read off its trajectory log: the least gap from its box to another road user's (min gap), its hardest braking (over half a second), when it first stopped, how far it drove, its top and final speed, and the elapsed time. openodd's plot of the drawn cases (openodd.CasePlot) is shown too.

docs.title: Comparing runs
docs.text:
/compare (the navigation bar's Compare, or Compare with past runs on a session's page) compares two or more sessions of the same scenarios (?s=batch/2026-10-18/16-09-52&s=...), the oldest the baseline:

  • Cases are matched by what they ran -- their sweep overrides (less ++odd_case, which names a case's position), else the ODD values they were drawn at -- not by their index, so a case keeps its match when a sweep's order or size changes. Each is marked by how its verdict changed between the first session that ran it and the last: pass → fail (a regression, listed first and in red), fail → pass, flaky, the same, or run by one session only. Beside it, the change of each metric (bold when more than 5%), each run's verdict linking to its page, and side by side: the first and last runs in two Rerun viewers on one page (/compare/runs?run=type/date/time/index&run=...).
  • ODD cells: each session's passes and runs in each cell of the two attributes picked (the buckets the cases were drawn in), red where the last session passes fewer of them, green where more; and openodd's matrix of each session beside the others.
  • Pass rates of each session.

docs.title: Running through SLURM
docs.text:
The Run Scenarios panel's Launcher runs the batch here, case after case (local, the default), or submits it as a SLURM array job (SLURM, Running a Batch on SLURM) with the launcher.* keys the panel sets: the partition (from sinfo), array_parallelism, cases_per_task, time, mem, gres, start_stagger_seconds, extra environment variables (launcher.env), and for a viewer whose host sees the nodes' file system at another path (an sshfs or NFS mount) remote_cwd, python and the setup lines a job runs first (A submit host with other paths); the extra overrides can set any other. The viewer runs scenario [--multirun] scenario=... launcher=slurm ... --no-wait (with a sweeper, every case of the sweep) in its base path, and opens the batch's page once it is submitted. Where sbatch is not on the viewer's PATH the option is disabled, and says so.

A SLURM batch's page (outputs/<date>/<time>/ with a slurm/ directory, whoever submitted it) follows it through squeue and the records its tasks write: each case passed, failed, errored, running, pending or missing (with why: its task's state and error), each submission's job and tasks (state, host, cases done, peak memory), and the cases as they land, before the batch has a summary. Its buttons run scenario-slurm on the batch: Resubmit missing (the cases with no outcome, or that errored), Resubmit failed too (--failed), with the array parallelism and cases per task to use, Collect (the summary and batch_results.json) and Cancel jobs.

VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND replaces uv run scenario as the command a SLURM batch is submitted with (.venv/bin/scenario, say, where uv run must not sync the environment).

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description VIEWER_BASE_PATH Current working directory Base path for scanning scenario result files VIEWER_HOST 0.0.0.0 Server bind address VIEWER_PORT 9000 Server listen port VIEWER_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/viewer The web viewer's copy, and recordings of sessions that cannot be written VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER the copy in the cache, else the CDN Where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from: a directory, a URL, or none VIEWER_RERUN_MAP_DIR ~/autoware_data/maps, if it exists Where the converter looks a map up by name when the log's own map file is not on this machine VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND uv run scenario The command a SLURM batch is submitted with

docs.title: Web UI Pages
docs.text: Route Description / Session list — displays all test sessions grouped by date/time /session/{type}/{date}/{time} Session detail — shows all scenarios in a session with pass/fail status /session/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index} Scenario detail — the run in the Rerun viewer, condition tree, per-condition status /recording/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index}.rrd The case's Rerun recording (made first if need be) /session/{type}/{date}/{time}/odd The session's results on the ODD (?x=, ?y= the attributes, ?at=attribute=bucket the cell drilled into) /compare Sessions compared (?s=type/date/time, two or more; ?x=, ?y= the cells' attributes) /compare/runs Runs side by side in Rerun viewers (?run=type/date/time/index, up to four)

docs.title: REST API Endpoints
docs.text:
The viewer also provides API endpoints for programmatic use and the web UI's interactive features:

Method Endpoint Description POST /api/refresh Clear result cache and return updated session table HTML GET /api/scenarios List all available scenario config names POST /api/run/preview Preview the CLI command that would be executed POST /api/run Start a scenario execution in the background GET /api/run/status Get current run status (non-streaming) GET /api/run/progress SSE (Server-Sent Events) stream for real-time progress GET /api/launchers The launchers a run can use here (slurm only where sbatch is, with the partitions) GET /api/slurm/submission The batch the viewer last submitted through SLURM, and its page once submitted GET /api/slurm/{date}/{time}/status A SLURM batch's cases, jobs and tasks POST /api/slurm/{date}/{time}/{resubmit,collect,cancel} scenario-slurm on the batch (resubmit takes failed, array_parallelism, cases_per_task) POST /api/recording/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index} Make the case's Rerun recording if there is none; its URL and path (503 with the install hint without the converter)

Run request body format:

{
  "scenario": "*/*",
  "extra_overrides": ["server.host=192.168.1.100"],
  "sweeper": "",
  "launcher": "local"
}

With "launcher": "slurm", "slurm" holds the launcher.* keys: {"partition": "main", "array_parallelism": 2, "cases_per_task": null, "time": "02:00:00", "mem": "12G", "gres": null, "start_stagger_seconds": 30, "remote_cwd": "workspace/OnePlanner", "python": ".venv/bin/python", "setup": "source ~/env.sh", "env": {"NAME": "value"}} (setup: a shell line per line, without ${...} or backslashes; env: NAME=value lines, or a mapping).

Progress SSE event format:

{
  "current": 2,
  "total": 5,
  "scenario_name": "intersection_passing/straight",
  "status": "running"
}

Where status is one of: "running", "idle", or "done".

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Used By Description CARLA_EXECUTABLE scenario runner Path to CARLA's launcher (CarlaUnreal.sh); defaults to the one scenario-setup installed AUTOWARE_CARLA_SCENARIO_HOME scenario-setup, scenario runner Moves ~/.autoware_carla_scenario (CARLA lives in bin/carla) NISHISHINJUKU_XODR_PATH map config Override default OpenDRIVE file path for nishishinjuku NISHISHINJUKU_LANELET2_PATH map config Override default Lanelet2 file path for nishishinjuku VIEWER_BASE_PATH viewer Base path for scenario results VIEWER_HOST viewer Viewer server bind address VIEWER_PORT viewer Viewer server listen port VIEWER_CACHE_DIR viewer The viewer's cache (the Rerun web viewer's copy, recordings it could not keep beside their logs) VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER viewer Where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from (a directory, a URL, or none) VIEWER_RERUN_MAP_DIR viewer Where the Rerun converter looks maps up by name VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND viewer The command a SLURM batch is submitted with (default uv run scenario) SCENARIO_EDITOR_DRAFTS scenario editor Directory holding scenario drafts SCENARIO_EDITOR_EXPORT_DIR scenario editor Staging area for exported package archives SCENARIO_EDITOR_MAP_ROOTS scenario editor Directories a Lanelet2 map may be served from SCENARIO_EDITOR_HOST scenario editor Editor server bind address SCENARIO_EDITOR_PORT scenario editor Editor server listen port SCENARIO_EDITOR_MAP_VIEWER scenario editor URL of a self-hosted simple_lanelet2 map viewer SCENARIO_EXPORT_FRAMEWORK_VERSION package export Pin exported packages to a published framework release SCENARIO_EXPORT_FRAMEWORK_REPOSITORY package export Repository URL recorded for a commit pin

docs.title: Use Case 1: Run a Single Scenario
docs.text:
# Start CARLA server first, then:
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight

docs.title: Use Case 2: Run All Scenarios for a Map
docs.text: uv run scenario scenario='*/*' map=nishishinjuku

docs.title: Use Case 3: Test on a Remote CARLA Server
docs.text:
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn \
  server.host=192.168.1.100 server.port=2000

docs.title: Use Case 4: Detect Missing 3D Models Before Running Scenarios
docs.text:
# 1. Detect lanelets without ground geometry
uv run detect-no-3d-model conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml

# 2. The detected IDs are written to no_3d_model_lanelet_ids in the YAML
# 3. Now run scenarios — sweep will skip these lanelets
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' map=nishishinjuku

docs.title: Use Case 5: Browse Results in the Web UI
docs.text:
# 1. Run scenarios
uv run scenario scenario='*/*'

# 2. Launch the viewer pointing to the outputs directory
VIEWER_BASE_PATH=outputs uv run viewer

# 3. Open http://localhost:9000 in a browser

docs.title: Use Case 6: Resume a Failed Batch
docs.text:
# Original batch run (5 scenarios, stopped at the 4th, e.g. by Ctrl+C)
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*'

# Resume from the 4th scenario
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' --resume-from 4

docs.title: "Connection refused" or timeout when connecting to CARLA
docs.text:
Cause: CARLA server is not running, or host/port is incorrect.

Solution: - Verify the CARLA server is started and accessible - Check server.host and server.port overrides match the server - Increase --timeout for detect-no-3d-model

docs.title: "batch scenarios must share the same map"
docs.text:
Cause: Glob pattern matched scenarios configured for different maps.

Solution: - Use map=<name> override to force all scenarios to use the same map - Or narrow the glob pattern to match scenarios for one map only

docs.title: Ego vehicle falls through the ground
docs.text:
Cause: The spawn lanelet has no corresponding 3D ground geometry in CARLA.

Solution: - Run detect-no-3d-model to identify problematic lanelets - Add them to no_3d_model_lanelet_ids in the map config - Increase entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_lower for deeper ray casting - Increase entity.spawn_retry_max_count for more spawn attempts

docs.title: Scenario times out unexpectedly
docs.text:
Cause: scenario.timeout_seconds is too short, or the ego vehicle is stuck.

Solution: - Increase scenario.timeout_seconds - Check ego.initial_speed_kmh — a value of 0.0 requires autopilot to start moving - Enable verbose logging and check condition statuses in the result JSON

docs.title: "Unknown scenario name" error
docs.text:
Cause: The scenario.name field in the YAML does not match any registered scenario class.

Solution: - Supported scenario names: intersection_passing, lane_change, traffic_light_compliance, temporary_stop - Check the name field in your scenario YAML config

docs.title: Example Scenarios
docs.text:
The examples shipped in autoware_carla_scenario.examples are logical scenarios: none of them names an intersection, a lane or a map. Each says what the lanelet it starts on has to be -- the approach to a signalised junction, a lane with a lane on its left, a road's right-hand edge -- and the lanelet-constraint sweeper expands it, on whatever map it is run on, into one concrete scenario per lanelet that qualifies. Every other place the scenario names follows from the lanelet the sweep picked.

Scenario What it checks Variants Traffic Light Compliance Waits at a red light, goes on green -- Temporary Stop Stops at a stop sign's line, then goes -- Intersection Passing Turns or goes straight through a junction left, right, right from a standstill, straight Lane Change Changes lane -- or refuses where there is none left, right, refused left, refused right Pedestrian Dart-out Does not hit a pedestrian who runs out -- Cut-in Does not hit a vehicle cutting in from the left, from the right

docs.title: How each page reads
docs.text:
In the Scenario Editor. The screenshot is the example authored in the Scenario Editor, open on Town10HD_Opt. The Places panel binds one of the lanelets the search matches -- the same one the video below it runs -- and draws every place that follows from it: an NPC on the lane beside the ego, the lanelet a condition watches, the ego's goal.

The video. Each page's clip is not something a run writes (runs render no video since 15.0.0; see Seeing a run): it is recorded for these pages by tools/scenario_video/, a separate tool in the repository that films the run with a chase camera of its own, lays it beside a sumo-gui replay and encodes the result with the ffmpeg command-line tool.

A lanelet in the editor is chosen one of three ways:

  • Fixed -- this lanelet.
  • Constraint search -- the lanelets matching a constraint tree; the sweeper runs the scenario once per match. One lanelet per scenario is searched for.
  • From the search -- worked out from the lanelet the search picked, case by case, by a binding:
Binding The lanelet it gives The matched lanelet The pick itself Beside the matched lanelet The lane on its left or right a vehicle may change into Along the route from the matched lanelet The lanelet that many steps on Lanelet before the stop line The lanelet a spawn that far before the pick's stop line stands on

A spawn's position along its lanelet can be derived the same way -- Before stop line puts it a fixed distance short of the stop line.

Scenario. What happens, in the order the editor lays it out: who starts where, what is done and when, and what makes the run pass or fail.

Parameters. The values the example runs with. Each can be overridden from the command line like any Hydra key -- scenario.timeout_seconds=30, ego.initial_speed_kmh=10 -- and the sweep's constraints are what decide where it runs.

Result. One case, run on CARLA 0.10 with SUMO driving the traffic: CARLA's chase camera on the left, sumo-gui replaying the same run on the right.

docs.title: Running one
docs.text:
# Every case on a map, one after another
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=cut_in/left map=town10hd_opt traffic=sumo

# Or list the cases, to run them anywhere
uv run scenario-expand scenario=cut_in/left map=town10hd_opt

docs.title: Cut-in
docs.text:
A vehicle in the next lane, 10 m ahead of the ego, changes into the ego's lane 2 s into the run. The ego must not hit it -- on every lane with a lane on that side.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=cut_in/left map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a lane with a lane on the cut-in side, not in a junction, at least 60 m long, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model. 5 m along it, 30 km/h. NPC1 Beside the matched lanelet, on the cut-in side: the lane next to the ego's. 15 m along it, 30 km/h. Initialization Every traffic light green. NPC1, after 2 s Change lane towards the ego. Pass 3 s have passed since NPC1 reached the ego's OpenDRIVE lane (lane of a position: the matched lanelet at the ego's spawn, the same lane), with no collision. Fail The ego collides with anything -- NPC1, another actor, a static object, map geometry such as a wall or a kerb (ego_collided); the ego's centre is on none of the lanes ahead of it -- the matched lanelet and the lanelets that follow it, up to 1000 m from its start -- for 0.2 s: it changed lanes, turned onto a lanelet that does not follow it, or left the road (ego_left_its_lane); or 20 s pass.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
From the leftFrom the right

scenario=cut_in/left -- a lane on the ego's left; NPC1 changes right.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 324, where the ego starts; NPC1 starts beside it on lanelet 446. Result: PASSED.

scenario=cut_in/right -- a lane on the ego's right; NPC1 changes left.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 446, where the ego starts; NPC1 starts beside it on lanelet 324. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value NPC1 ahead of the ego 10 m along its lanelet (at s = 15 m): npc_ahead_m or, measured npc_gap_m: the gap vehicle_ahead_gap_m reads at the start (bumper to bumper, along the ego's lane); NPC1's s is solved for so it does. Unset by default; an ODD-sampled sweep sets it, 2-30 m NPC1 and ego initial speed 30 km/h Cut-in after 2 s Held in the ego's lane for 3 s Lanelet at least 60 m Timeout 20 s Fail on any collision of the ego on: fail_on_any_collision (off: only a collision with NPC1, hit_cut_in_vehicle) Fail on leaving the lanes ahead on: fail_on_leaving_lane The lanes ahead reach 1000 m from the start of the matched lanelet: lanes_ahead_m Off them for 0.2 s: leaving_lane_seconds (0: the first tick off)

docs.title: Staying on the lanes ahead
docs.text:
The ego is to keep its lane while NPC1 cuts in: braking, or slowing, is the answer the scenario is after, and a run that swerved into the next lane or off the road has not passed it, whatever it did not hit. The lanes ahead are the lanelet the ego spawns on and the ones that follow it in the routing graph (lanelets_ahead: following without lane changes, every branch, up to lanes_ahead_m); in none of them is in the lane beside, on a lanelet that turns off them, or in no lanelet at all.

It is not a condition of its own but a composition of the framework's, left_lanes_ahead in examples/cut_in.py, which any scenario can build the same way:

on_lanes = [
    EntityLanePositionCondition(
        EGO_ROLE_NAME, Lanelet2Pose(lanelet_id=i, s=0.0), label=f"ego_on_lanelet_{i}"
    )
    for i in lanelets_ahead(spawn.lanelet_id, 1000.0)
]
self.register_fail_condition(
    PersistentCondition(                     # off them for 0.2 s, not one tick at a seam
        NotCondition(                        # on none of them -- off the road included
            OrCondition(on_lanes),           # on one of them
            holds_when_pending=True,
        ),
        0.2,
        label="ego_left_its_lane",
    )
)

holds_when_pending=True is what makes it a logical NOT. A condition that has not fired returns nothing, and a plain NotCondition only flips the verdict of a child that has, so it could not say "on none of these". The position tested is the vehicle's centre (its CARLA location), so a wheel over the line is not leaving the lane; a seam between two lanelets is covered by the next one, and the 0.2 s wait absorbs a tick that falls between them.

A scenario document says the same with the editor's cards -- Persistent, NOT (with Holds while the child does not), ANY and one Position (Lanelet2) per lanelet:

- type: persistent
  params: {duration: 0.2}
  children:
    - type: not
      params: {holds_when_pending: true}
      children:
        - type: any
          children:
            - {type: entity_lane_position, params: {entity: ego, lanelet_id: 79016}}
            - {type: entity_lane_position, params: {entity: ego, lanelet_id: 79017}}

docs.title: Placing NPC1 by the measured gap
docs.text:
npc_ahead_m is a raw setting: NPC1's s on its lanelet less the ego's on its own. It is not the gap the vehicle_ahead_gap_m measure reads: the measure is bumper to bumper -- NPC1's rear bumper less the ego's front bumper -- along the ego's lane (Scenario measures), and lanelets side by side are not the same length on a curve (the outer one is longer), so their s do not line up and the difference changes from place to place.

npc_gap_m is that gap itself. When it is set, the scenario places NPC1 with place_at_vehicle_ahead_gap: from the ego's spawn pose, it finds the s on NPC1's lanelet at which the measure -- the same code, run on the poses the two will spawn at -- reads npc_gap_m, so the run starts at exactly that gap wherever it is placed. The bumpers are the vehicles' own: before either is spawned, a vehicle of each blueprint (ego.vehicle_type, npc_vehicle_type) already in the world is read, or else one is spawned high above the map, its bounding box read and the vehicle destroyed (vehicle_bumpers, once per blueprint), so NPC1 is spawned once, where the gap reads right, rather than spawned and moved. A gap the lanelet cannot reach (too short, or curving out of the lanes the measure counts) fails the setup, saying what gaps it does reach.

On CARLA 0.10 Town04_Opt, with the ego (a Lincoln MKZ) on lanelet 79016 at s = 640 and NPC1 (a Mini) placed on lanelet 77298 beside it, gaps of 2.5, 8, 12, 15, 20, 25 and 30 m were measured back within 0.001 m on the first tick (within 0.01 m two ticks later). Placed by a calibrated npc_ahead_m offset instead, and measured centre to centre, the same place read 2.2 m more than drawn.

The scenario's controls draw the gap this way (target: measure, Controls), so a sweep's vehicle_ahead_gap draws are the gaps the runs start at:

uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/left map=<map> scenario.npc_gap_m=15

The relative speed needs no solving: npc_initial_speed_kmh less the ego's initial speed is what the vehicle_ahead_relative_speed_kph measure reads at the start, up to the cosine of the small heading difference on a curve.

docs.title: Intersection Passing
docs.text:
The ego approaches a junction from 25 m short of its stop line and takes one movement through it -- left, right or straight on -- on every junction movement of that kind on the map. Every light is green, so nothing stops it.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a junction lanelet whose turn_direction is the movement and which has a stop line -- any, or a traffic light's (see the variants) -- excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model, except from a standstill. Position before stop line: 25 m short of it -- which walks back onto the lane that approaches the junction, where the run starts. Goal from the search: the lanelet after the junction lanelet. Initialization Every traffic light green. Ego, from the start Turn at the next junction, in the movement's direction. Pass The ego has been on the road of the junction lanelet (the matched lanelet), and on the road of the lane it comes out on (along the route, one step on). Any lane of each road counts. Fail The timeout -- and, going straight, slowing below 3 km/h after 0.3 s.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
LeftRightRight, from a standstillStraight

scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn -- turn_direction: left, a stop line (a signal's or a stop sign's), 20 km/h, 20 s.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4412 and the ego starts on lanelet 5975, 15.2 m along it. Result: PASSED.

scenario=intersection_passing/right_turn -- turn_direction: right, a stop line, 20 km/h, 20 s.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4766 and the ego starts on lanelet 3235, 7.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

scenario=intersection_passing/right_turn_sweep -- turn_direction: right at a signalised junction only (a traffic-light stop line), starting at 0 km/h, so the ego has to pull away as well as steer; 60 s. It does not leave out the lanelets with no 3D model.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4766 and the ego starts on lanelet 3235, 7.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

scenario=intersection_passing/straight -- turn_direction: straight at a signalised junction only, 5 km/h, 15 s. Also fails if the ego drops below 3 km/h after 0.3 s: with every light green it never has to stop.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4503 and the ego starts on lanelet 860, 3.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Lane Change
docs.text:
The ego is told to change lane as soon as the run starts. Where there is a lane to change into, it has to end up in it; where there is none, it has to stay where it is.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=lane_change/left map=<map>
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=lane_change_fail/left map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Ego Constraint search: a lane that is not in a junction and is long enough, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model -- with a lane on that side to change into, or, for the refused change, without one. 1 km/h. Initialization Every traffic light green. Ego, from the start Change lane, left or right. Pass Changing: the ego has been on the OpenDRIVE lane beside the one it started on (lane of a position: the matched lanelet at the spawn, the lane to its left or right). Refusing: the timeout passes. Fail Changing: the timeout. Refusing: the ego reaches that lane.

The lane checked is the OpenDRIVE lane next to the spawn's, anywhere along its road, rather than the lanelet next to the spawn's: a refused change has no such lanelet to name.

LeftRightRefused, leftRefused, right

scenario=lane_change/right -- a lane on the right, at least 30 m long; 10 s.
